Also dort, wo man sich schon kennt. Es sei nach Ansicht des NETZWERK ARTIKEL 3 völlig unverständlich, warum diese Arbeitsplätze nicht in reguläre sozialversicherungspflichtige Arbeitsverhältnisse mit Unterstützung des Budget für Arbeit umgewandelt werden…“

 

Artikel von Ottmar Miles-Paul vom 9. Februar 2022 bei den kobinet Nachrichten

 




[Werkstätten der Baunataler Diakonie Kassel] Beutet die nordhessische BDKS Menschen aus?  


„

Der christliche Beschäftigungsträger Baunataler Diakonie Kassel (BDKS) e. V. wehrt sich gegen den Vorwurf Menschen mit Beeinträchtigungen im öffentlich geförderten Beschäftigungssektor über ein undurchsichtiges Entlohnungssystem auszubeuten.




Zu den Kunden der BDKS zählen u.a. Volkswagen, B. Braun und die Hütt-Brauerrei. Im Juli ’21 haben die Mitglieder der BDKS den ehemaligen Vorstandsvorsitzenden der B.Braun Melsungen AG, Prof. Dr. Heinz-Walter Große, zum Vorsitzenden des Aufsichtsrats gewählt. 

Dem bei der BDKS beschäftigten Ralf G. war in seinen Lohnabrechnungen aufgefallen, dass er bei gleichbleibender Arbeit immer weniger Lohn von der BDKS erhielt; zusammen mit seinem Vater schaltete G. sogar einen Anwalt ein und versuchte sich dagegen zu wehren. (…)




Nun wehrt sich die BDKS gegen den Vorwurf sie würde z. B. behinderte Menschen zusammen mit der nordhessischen Wirtschaft ausbeuten und verweist 

in der HNA vom 6.2.22

 

 auf ihr komplexes, kompliziertes und undurchsichtiges Entlohnungssystem. Das BDKS-Entlohnungssystem ist für die betroffenen Beschäftigten und ihre Angehörigen kaum nachzuvollziehen – ist das so gewollt?




Die Beschreibung des Entlohnungssystems, für die BDKS-Basisbeschäftigten – aus Sicht der BDKS-Geschäftsführung -, ist bezeichnend: Zu komplex, zu kompliziert und somit vermutlich nur für BWL’er (und andere Fachleute) nachvollziehbar bzw. verständlich, jedoch nicht für die Entlohnten selbst; zudem ermöglicht dieses Entlohnungssystem betriebsinterne Interpretationen und (willkürlich ausgelegte) Spielräume für den Arbeitgeber, die BDKS. Im Bereich des Bundesteilhabegesetzes verhält es sich ganz ähnlich: Zu schwerverständlich für die Betroffenen (…)




Wenn diese o. a. geschilderten Dinge für die Betroffenen (und ihre Angehörigen) nicht einfach nachzuvollziehen sind und zudem (bewusst?) intransparent gehalten werden, erweckt das großes Misstrauen bei den Beschäftigten gegenüber dem Beschäftigungsbetrieb BDKS. Und genau das ist hier geschehen und wird nun öffentlich diskutiert.




Hat die BDKS sich diesbezüglich einfach keine Mühe gegeben, liegt hier ein Kommunikationsproblem (bspw. zwischen der BDKS-Geschäftsführung und den Basisbeschäftigten) vor? Oder spielen hier noch andere (gewinnträchtige) Gründe für die BDKS eine wichtige Rolle? Die BDKS ist hierbei in einer Art Bringschuld gegenüber den Betroffenen und der Öffentlichkeit. Auch die o. a. nordhessischen Unternehmen sollten ein starkes Eigeninteresse daran habe diesbezüglich bei der Aufklärung der Vorwürfe mitzuwirken. Ausbeutung von Menschen im öffentlich geförderten Beschäftigungssektor – zu Gunsten der (nordhessischen) Wirtschaft – darf es nicht geben!

“ 

Beitrag von anonym am 07.02.2022 bei indymedia

 










Aufruf zum Streik für den Mindestlohn für Menschen in Behindertenwerkstätten ab dem 01.12.2021 – und Petiton für den Mindestlohn 




„

STREIKAUFRUF in WfbM. Wir fordern Mindestlohn. Macht blau bleib daheim 

geht nicht arbeiten ab den 01.12.2021. Das wird erst beendet wenn wir den Mindestlohn 

haben und die Politik endlich handelt

“ 

Aufruf von SakulTalks vom 26.11.2021 auf Twitter

 

, siehe dazu:







Petition: #StelltUnsEin – Ich fordere den Mindestlohn für Menschen in Behindertenwerkstätten!




„

Ich habe 6,5 Stunden am Tag in einer Werkstatt gearbeitet. Diese Werkstattart macht in Deutschland acht Milliarden Umsatz im Jahr. Dennoch zahlt man mir und meinen Kolleg*innen für unsere Arbeit nur 1,35 Euro die Stunde. Es ist für niemanden möglich, davon zu leben, weswegen wir dann auch Grundsicherung vom Staat brauchen. Das kann man mit uns machen, weil wir eine Behinderung haben. (…) Diese Vollzeitarbeit von der man nicht leben kann, nennt man dann “Teilhabe”. Ich generiere Milliarden für Unternehmen, mein eigener Lohn ist dabei aber fast nur die Arbeit selbst. Als Antwort auf eine Verfassungsklage von André Thiel, der auch in einer Behindertenwerkstatt gearbeitet hat, wird die Position der Werkstattbetreiber sehr deutlich: unser “Lohn sei nicht vorrangig Geld, sondern Teilhabe”. Unser Lohn soll also sein, dass wir überhaupt arbeiten dürfen, für andere Gewinn machen dürfen? Das ist an Frechheit nicht zu überbieten. Ich fordere den Mindestlohn für Menschen in Behindertenwerkstätten! Das würde bedeuten, dass die Arbeiter*innen der Behindertenwerkstätten als Arbeitnehmer*innen gelten und sich auch gewerkschaftlich organisieren dürften. (…) Das Konzept der Behindertenwerkstätten ist im Grunde kriminell und gehört abgeschafft. Dass die Werkstätten von heute auf morgen abgeschafft werden, ist jedoch wenig realistisch. Langfristig müssten Menschen mit Behinderung auch auf “normale” Schulen, um eine freie Entscheidung zu bekommen, ob sie in eine Behindertenwerkstatt oder in den ersten Arbeitsmarkt treten wollen. Das ist aber ein langer Weg den wir da vor uns haben. Immer gilt aber: wir arbeitenden Menschen mit Behinderung, wollen dieselben Rechte haben, wie alle anderen Arbeiter*innen Deutschlands. Wir wollen Mindestlohn

…“ 

Petition von Lukas Krämer bei change.org

 

 an Olaf Scholz (Kanzlerkandidat SPD zur Bundestagswahl 2021 ) und weitere










BeHindernisse: »Wer einmal in der Werkstatt ist, kommt nie wieder heraus«  




Ein Interview von Frédéric Valin mit Anne Gersdorff und Sven Papenbrock aus ak 676 vom 16. November 2021

 

 

„über die Ausbeutung Beschäftigter auf dem sogenannten zweiten Arbeitsmarkt und die Kämpfe dagegen (…) Anne Gersdorff: Das deutsche Werkstättensystem wird gerügt, weil es nicht inklusiv ist. Es ist ein in sich geschlossenes System, denn die Übergänge von den Werkstätten in den weiteren Arbeitsmarkt liegen seit Jahrzehnten konstant unter einem Prozent. Das heißt, kaum jemand, der in eine Werkstatt geht, kommt da je wieder raus. Die Beschäftigten sind ihr Leben lang auf Grundsicherung angewiesen, weil sie von den Werkstätten nur ein Taschengeld für ihre Arbeit ausgezahlt bekommen. In der UN-Behindertenrechtskonvention ist festgeschrieben, dass jeder Mensch das Recht hat, seinen Arbeitsplatz frei zu wählen, und dass man mit dem Lohn für seine Arbeit auch den Lebensunterhalt bestreiten können sollte. Darüber hinaus sollte der Arbeitsmarkt barrierefrei zugänglich sein. In Deutschland wird dafür einfach zu wenig getan. Die Werkstättenplätze wurden in den 1990er und 2000er Jahren sogar um 50 Prozent ausgebaut. Die Zahl der Beschäftigten und auch die Zahl der Werkstätten nehmen weiter zu, und ich bin überzeugt, dass es nach der Pandemie auch noch einen weiteren Anstieg geben wird, weil sich Leute vielleicht weniger auf den allgemeinen Arbeitsmarkt trauen und weil ihnen suggeriert wird, dass es mit der Arbeit in der Werkstatt die Perspektive auf ein sicheres Leben gäbe und man dort gut untergebracht sei. (…) Aktuell sind etwa 312.000 Menschen in Werkstätten tätig, Tendenz steigend. (…) Menschen in Behindertenwerkstätten gelten nicht als Arbeitnehmer*innen, sondern als Beschäftigte; das bedeutet, dass sie meist unter 200 Euro im Monat verdienen, also für ein Taschengeld arbeiten. Die Personen, die in den Werkstätten sind, werden vorher als »nicht erwerbsfähig« gelabelt. Und diese Argumentation wird benutzt, um diese fadenscheinige Einteilung als »Nicht-Arbeitnehmer*innen« aufrechtzuerhalten. Dazu kommt, dass mit vermeintlichen Schutzmaßnahmen argumentiert wird: Leute in Werkstätten müssten nicht so hart arbeiten, wird dann gesagt. Oder es gäbe ja besondere Arbeitsbedingungen. Außerdem würden die Menschen in den Werkstätten ohnehin weiterhin Grundsicherung erhalten, egal, wie leistungsstark sie seien. All das führt dazu, dass die Personen nicht dieselben Rechte haben wie Arbeitnehmer*innen, obwohl sie für große Unternehmen Profite erarbeiten oder Dienstleistungen erbringen – und das zum Teil auch acht Stunden am Tag, wie alle anderen Arbeitnehmer*innen auch. (…) Ich bin wirklich überzeugt, dass Inklusion auf dem allgemeinen Arbeitsmarkt mit der entsprechenden Beratung und Unterstützung wirklich funktionieren kann, und das brauchen wir dringend, solange die Gesellschaft Arbeit so stark mit Teilhabe verknüpft.“




Sonderwirtschaftszone „Behindertenwerkstätten“. Beschäftigten mit Einschränkungen wird »Arbeitnehmerstatus« verweigert. Konzerne profitieren vom System 




„

Es ist ein Heer prekär Beschäftigter: In rund 750 »Behindertenwerkstätten« an knapp 3.000 Standorten malochen mehr als 320.000 Menschen mit körperlichen oder kognitiven Einschränkungen. Für einen Billiglohn, durchschnittlich etwa ein Euro pro Arbeitsstunde. Tendenz sinkend. Erhielten Arbeitende in den Werkstätten 2018 ein monatliches Entgelt von zirka 229 Euro, waren es ein Jahr später nur noch 220 Euro und ein paar Cent. Das sind Ergebnisse eines Zwischenberichts, der jüngst seitens des Bundesministeriums für Arbeit und Soziales (BMAS) vorgestellt wurde. Das BMAS hatte 2020 zwei Forschungsinstitute beauftragt, das Entgeltsystem in den Werkstätten samt »Reformbedarf« zu ermitteln. Der Abschlussbericht ist erst für Ende 2023 angekündigt. Wie kommen die mickrigen Summen in die Lohntüte? Die Bundesarbeitsgemeinschaft Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen (BAG WfbM) klärt auf: Die Einrichtungen zahlen einen Grundbetrag in Höhe eines Ausbildungsgeldes und einen »leistungsangemessenen Steigerungsbetrag«, sagte Volker Berg, Pressereferent der BAG WfbM, am Donnerstag auf jW-Nachfrage. Hinzu käme ein öffentlich finanziertes Arbeitsförderungsgeld. Das bedeutet: WfbM-Prekäre sind »Sozialfälle«, müssen mittels Grundsicherung aufstocken oder erhalten eine Erwerbsminderungsrente.




Fest steht: Gehandikapte Beschäftigte fertigen in einer Art Sonderwirtschaftszone. Ein einträgliches Business. Der Jahresumsatz aller WfbM liegt hierzulande nach Angaben der Kampagne »Job inklusive« bei rund acht Milliarden Euro. Zahlreiche Konzerne und mittelständische Unternehmen haben Verträge mit Werkstätten, lassen dort produzieren oder lagern Dienstleistungen dorthin aus. »Job inklusiv« nennt Firmennamen: Volkswagen, Thyssen-Krupp, Siemens, Daimler, Panasonic. Ferner würden Startups, die nach Fairtrade-Standards handeln, mit WfbM-Geschäftsführungen kooperieren. (…) Möglich macht dieses System der fehlende sogenannte Arbeitnehmerstatus der Werktätigen mit Handikaps. Eine Rechtfertigung klingt oft so, Beispiel BMAS: Bei der Werkstattarbeit gehe es vorrangig um Betreuung und Rehabilitation, die Bedingungen seien mit denen einer »normalen« Berufsausübung nicht vergleichbar. (…) Als wäre das nicht genug, gibt es auch noch ein Ost-West-Gefälle. Die Entlohnung in ostdeutschen »Behindertenwerkstätten« liege um etwa ein Viertel unter jener im Westen der Republik, ärgerte sich der Leipziger Linke-Bundestagsabgeordnete Sören Pellmann am Donnerstag gegenüber dieser Zeitung: »Der Gesetzgeber muss hier eine Angleichung erzwingen.« Apropos Arbeiterrechte, was sagt der Deutsche Gewerkschaftsbund (DGB) zu Dumpinglöhnen bei Hunderttausenden in den Werkstätten? Eine Pressesprecherin bat jW um Verständnis, eine Stellungnahme sei am Donnerstag zeitlich nicht drin gewesen

.“ 

Artikel von Oliver Rast in der jungen Welt vom 12.11.2021

 




Beschäftigte in Behindertenwerkstätten: Nur 180 Euro pro Monat! 




„… 

Ausgangslage im Juli 2021: Während die politische Linke derzeit gebannt auf die Arbeiter:innenkämpfe der „Riders“ und deren wilde Streiks blickt und sich solidarisch zeigt, übergab Lukas Krämer am 30.06.2021 eine Petition für den Mindestlohn in Behindertenwerkstätten, welche mehr als 125.000 Menschen unterzeichnet haben. In kleinem Rahmen wurde diese vor dem Deutschen Bundestag Kerstin Griese (SPD), als parlamentarische Staatssekretärin beim Bundesminister für Arbeit und Soziales übergeben. Wichtig ist an dieser Stelle der Blick auf diese Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen (WfbM) – dort sind in Deutschland ca. 320.000 Menschen beschäftigt, die nicht als Arbeitnehmer:innen gelten, sondern in sogenannten „Beschäftigungsverhältnissen“ stehen. Daraus resultiert, dass diese Personen weder Recht auf Mindestlohn noch auf gewerkschaftliche Organisation, öffentliche Tarifverträge oder Streiks haben. Immerhin würde sich auch diese marginalisierte Gruppe wünschen, mit ihren Forderungen auf mehr Gehör zu stoßen. In Deutschland gelten schließlich 7.902.960 Millionen Menschen als schwerbehindert, das entspricht etwa jede:r zehnten Person. Behinderung ist oft ein Ausschlusskriterium, ob im privaten Alltag oder im Arbeitsleben. Ein Viertel aller Anfragen der Antidiskriminierungsstelle betreffen das Feld von Behinderungen. Wäre nicht ein solidarischer diskriminierungsfreier Grundkonsens notwendig, um wirklich positive gesellschaftliche Veränderungen erzielen zu können? Speziell die Haltung der politischen Linken verstehe ich hierbei jedoch nicht ganz, denn im Endeffekt sind das modern geführte Arbeiter:innenkämpfe, die sich jedoch noch nicht mal als Arbeiter:innen bezeichnen können. Während also von der wilden Streikkultur geschwärmt wird, was auch vollkommen in Ordnung ist, finden die Bemühungen für grundlegende Dinge wie den Arbeitnehmer:innen Status und den Mindestlohn der Werkstattbeschäftigten wenig bis kaum Gehör. Mir stellt sich zunehmend die Frage, woran das liegen könnte

…“ 

Gastbeitrag von Michael Herrmann vom 15.7.2021 bei Klasse gegen Klasse

 




Behindert arbeiten. Sonderwelten für Menschen mit Einschränkungen oder geschützter Arbeitsraum? Ein Werkstattbericht. 




„

Mehr als 300 000 Menschen mit Behinderung arbeiten in Deutschland für sehr wenig Geld in sogenannten Werkstätten. Sie bekommen keinen Mindestlohn, weil sie arbeitsrechtlich als Rehabilitanden gelten. Ist das fair? Dass es die Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung gibt, ist eine Errungenschaft des Wohlfahrtsstaates. Doch ein größer werdender Kreis von Aktivist*innen und Politiker*innen fordern ihr Auslaufen oder wenigstens eine radikale Reform. Mehr als ein halbes Jahrhundert nach ihrer Gründung wird den Werkstätten vorgeworfen, Sonderarbeitswelten zu sein. Ein verschwindend geringer Teil der Beschäftigten – nur ein Prozent jährlich – schafft den Sprung auf den ersten Arbeitsmarkt. Dabei waren die Werkstätten, so liest man es in ihrer Verordnung von 1980, als Übergangseinrichtungen gedacht für Menschen, die aufgrund ihrer geistigen, psychischen oder körperlichen Beeinträchtigungen nicht, noch nicht oder noch nicht wieder auf den allgemeinen Arbeitsmarkt gelangen. Katrin Langensiepen ist Berichterstatterin zum Thema Menschen mit Behinderung in Brüssel. 

Die Abgeordnete im Europaparlament veröffentlichte Ende Januar einen Bericht, in dem sie fordert, die Werkstätten langfristig auslaufen zu lassen

 

. Er wurde vom Ausschuss für Beschäftigung und soziale Angelegenheiten im Europaparlament mit großer Mehrheit angenommen. Langensiepen kritisiert die Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung als weder inklusiv noch vorbereitend auf den allgemeinen Arbeitsmarkt. Die Befürworter der Werkstätten sehen das, was in den Werkstätten an Inklusion geleistet wird, gänzlich anders. (…) Doch die Unzufriedenheit der Beschäftigen mit Behinderung ist deutlich größer als die der Arbeitnehmer ohne Einschränkungen, das geht aus dem 

Bundesteilhabebericht

 

 

 hervor. Die Einstellungen der Beschäftigten zu den Werkstätten sind durchaus ambivalent. (…) Wie könnte eine Reform der Werkstätten aussehen? 

Die Werkstatträte haben dazu einen Vorschlag gemacht. Sie nennen es «Basisgeld»

 

. Die betriebsratsähnliche Struktur vertritt die Interessen der Werkstattbeschäftigten, ihr Konzept denkt aber weit über diesen Kreis hinaus. Alle Menschen in Deutschland, die dauerhaft voll erwerbsgemindert sind, sollen das Basisgeld erhalten, 70 Prozent des gesamtdeutschen Durchschnittsverdienstes soll es betragen. Im Jahr 2019 hätte das einer Summe von 1450 Euro entsprochen. «Ein selbstbestimmtes Leben heißt, Geld in der Tasche zu haben», meint Birgit Meierdiecks, Werkstatträtin aus Bremen und Mitentwicklerin des Basisgeldes. Am Ende hätten die Menschen dabei gar nicht viel mehr Auskommen, als durch die Grundsicherung. Aber: «Es wird ihnen die Demütigung erspart, alles offenzulegen.» Ein Basisgeld hätte bestimmt auch Rückwirkungen auf die Werkstätten, die Menschen könnten freier entscheiden, ob sie dort arbeiten wollen. Letztlich sei das aber auch eine gesellschaftliche Frage, betont Meierdiecks. «Dass viele Leute sich sagen, es ist schon in Ordnung, wenn Menschen mit Behinderung arm durchs Leben gehen, das muss sich ändern.» In anderen Ländern gibt es andere Systeme, Menschen mit Behinderungen in Arbeit zu bringen. In Großbritannien gab es einst ähnliche Werkstätten wie in Deutschland, dann wurden sie abgeschafft. Mit ambivalentem Ausgang: Während einige der Menschen nun auf dem allgemeinen Arbeitsmarkt gelandet sind, finden andere von ihnen keinen Job

…“ 

Artikel von Fabian Hillebrand vom 26.02.2021 im ND online

 







Der Beitrag 

Immer nur Behindertenwerkstätten: Warum verdienen Menschen mit Behinderung so wenig? Und wo bleibt die Inklusion?

 erschien zuerst auf 

LabourNet Germany

.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Las cuentas no cierran en Vaca Muerta: la fuga de dólares que oculta el relato extractivo
content:
Por Natalia Concina




La explotación de Vaca Muerta permitió el ingreso al país de casi dos mil millones de dólares entre lo que vendió y lo que pidió como préstamo durante 2026. Lejos de quedarse en el país, 

esas divisas volvieron al exterior y le permitieron a las empresas petroleras y de diferentes rubros fugar sus ganancias

. Un nuevo estudio del grupo de investigación EJES confirma que el yacimiento de petróleo no convencional permite hoy sostener la estabilidad cambiaria, pero 

consolida a los sectores de poder concentrado y genera una millonaria deuda a futuro

.




Durante la primera parte del año, las empresas que explotan Vaca Muerta pidieron préstamos por 936 millones de dólares mensuales promedio, una cifra incluso superior a las divisas que generaron por las ventas al exterior de hidrocarburos (que rondaron en un promedio de 754 millones por mes).




Esta inyección de divisas extranjeras es la que garantiza hoy la estabilidad cambiaria, es decir, que el precio de la moneda estadounidense esté más o menos estable. Sin embargo, 

los dólares que ingresan por el endeudamiento privado son un problema para toda la sociedad

 porque —a futuro— utilizarán los dólares que genera toda la economía. ¿Por qué? Porque para cancelar sus deudas la empresas comprarán los dólares disponibles en el Banco Central, que a su vez ingresarán por las exportaciones u otros mecanismo (como podría ser esta de toma de deuda).




En otras palabras, Vaca Muerta permite hoy la “sostenibilidad” del modelo a través de estos dólares de los que se nutren, además de las empresas petroleras, los sectores corporativos más concentrados de la economía local para remitir sus ganancias al exterior, un proceso que se intensificó desde diciembre pasado. 

Una especie de puerta giratoria de dólares

, aunque las deudas quedan.




Foto: Martín Álvarez Mullally




Estas conclusiones son los pilares más importantes d

el informe “

¿A dónde van los dólares de Vaca Muerta”,

 

el tercer estudio realizado por el Enlace por la Justicia Energética y Socioambiental (EJES)”

, una articulación de organizaciones que desde 2024 analiza sistemáticamente los números del yacimiento no convencional en forma crítica, exponiendo sus implicancias ocultas detrás del supuesto boom energético.




“El análisis de los datos del Banco Central de 2025 y lo que va de 2026 permite consolidar dos miradas respecto a Vaca Muerta: por un lado, que su función es traer dólares y no se está pensando en eslabonar un conjunto de actividades económicas a partir del yacimiento; por el otro, que 

lo único que dejará al país son deudas

”, asegura a Tierra Viva el economista Marco Kofman, autor del trabajo.




¿A dónde van los dólares de Vaca Muerta? - EJES




Récord de ventas




En los primeros cinco meses de 2026, el país exportó 314.000 barriles diarios de petróleo, acumulando un total de 3.773 millones de dólares, lo que da un promedio de 754 millones por mes. No sólo se aumentó la cantidad de crudo sino que coincidió con un precio internacional relativamente elevado.




De las diez primeras empresas que comercializan internacionalmente el crudo argentino, hay cinco que exportan más del 50 por ciento de su producción local. Respecto al gas de Vaca Muerta, se vende al exterior sólo entre el cuatro y el cinco por ciento.




Pese a la orientación exportadora, el informe destaca que en los últimos años Argentina disminuyó la importación de hidrocarburos drásticamente, parte por la producción de Vaca Muerta, parte por la crisis en la producción local. En ese contexto, la balanza comercial energética (diferencia entre la compra y la venta de petróleo y gas) es favorable para la Argentina, que pasó de estar en rojo a tener un superávit de 3.000 millones de dólares acumulado sólo en los primeros cinco meses de 2026.




“A este ingreso de dólares por ventas (dólares comerciales), 

se le suman los dólares financieros, es decir los que ingresan por toma de deuda de las empresas

 

que funcionan como un respirador artificial del modelo de Milei 

y le permite que el dólar se mantenga estable, sin tener que devaluar ni poner controles cambiarios”, explica Kofman.




Foto: Depositphotos




El trabajo de EJES explica que de los 22.617 millones de dólares que el sector privado ingresó al país por la vía del endeudamiento, 14.441 millones —casi el 64 por ciento del total— fueron aportados por las empresas energéticas; en los primeros cinco meses del año, ese endeudamiento fue de 936 millones de dólares promedio mensual.







“Este proceso de ingreso de dólares financieros es algo que está pasando por debajo del radar. Pero como llegan se van: hay un montón de actores que se llevan dólares de la economía que son los que están bancando al presidente Milei. Por eso sostengo hace un tiempo que detrás de Vaca Muerta hay una muy sólida comunidad de negocios que involucra no sólo las empresas energéticas sino a todos los sectores que en Argentina tienen capacidad de apropiación de riquezas”, dice Kofman.







Para comprender cómo se da este proceso en la práctica hay que imaginar lo siguiente: cuando una empresa toma una deuda, al Banco Central le figura un ingreso de dólares. Probablemente esa moneda estadounidense nunca se pesifique, porque la mayoría de las operaciones del sector energético son en dólares. Pero el punto es que esas divisas están allí, disponibles para que cualquier empresa (por ejemplo, una empresa alimenticia o metalúrgica) pueda comprarlos y enviarlos al exterior.




Y aquí viene otro dato clave que el trabajo revela: 

la salida de dólares al exterior está batiendo récord en 2026.




Foto: Presidencia de la Nación




Récord de fuga

 de dólares




“Todas las empresas que operan en Vaca Muerta, tengan o no casa matriz en Argentina, están transnacionalizadas, es decir que tienen su estructura jurídica en países con escasa o nula tributación, lo que se conoce como paraísos fiscales”, explica Kofman.




En 

trabajos anteriores

 realizados por EJES, Kofman ya había detallado los diferentes mecanismos por los cuales las compañías logran enviar al exterior sus ganancias en dólares: remitir a sus casas matrices los excedentes generados por las ventas, pagar servicios que contrataba fuera del país e incluso “auto endeudarse”, pedir préstamos a empresas del mismo grupo para luego tomar dólares para pagar los intereses.




Desde el macrismo y 

hasta abril de 2025

, la primera forma —que es el envío de las ganancias a la casa matriz— se vio afectada por lo que popularmente se conoció como “cepo”, que era en realidad un monto máximo. Tras la flexibilización de esta medida, entre diciembre y mayo de 2026, empresas de diferentes rubros —con las petroleras a la cabeza— remitieron al exterior más de 2.000 millones de dólares. Como se menciona antes, la disponibilidad de los dólares para estas operaciones fue posible gracias a Vaca Muerta.




“Argentina está en un récord histórico de exportaciones y, sin embargo, cuando analizamos las cuentas del central, no hay un sólo mes en el que le hayan sobrado dólares, es decir, todos los meses está en rojo. Esto quiere decir que a través de todos estos mecanismo, 

se fugaron más dólares de los que ingresaron

”, señala Kofman.




Foto: Ministerio de Economía




Lo que dejará Vaca Muerta




Como parte de los beneficios del 

Regimen de Incentivo a la Grandes Inversiones (RIGI)

, las empresas no tienen exigencias de contratar proveedores internos, por lo que el eslabonamiento productivo —que en algún momento se consideró que podía suceder a partir de Vaca Muerta— no pasó.




“Si uno mira cómo evoluciona el empleo en Neuquén, es una de las pocas provincias que no perdió puestos de trabajo, pero al ritmo que está creciendo le harían falta 200 años 

para llegar a un cuarto de los dos millones de personas que prometió Federico Sturzenegger

”, sostiene Kofman.




Y añade: “

No deja empleos, no deja dólares, lo que sí está dejando es una comunidad de negocios muy sólida y una deuda de más de 20.000 millones de dólares

. Y la deuda privada es un problema para toda la sociedad porque para pagarla se utilizan los dólares que genera toda la economía”.




El economista deja en claro cuál es la verdadera trampa: “Los dólares que se generan a partir de la actividad de las empresas en Vaca Muerta son producto de un largo eslabonamiento de actividades humanas, sociales y productivas. Sin la educación de los trabajadores, las rutas, la salud; no se podría explotar. Entonces, 

ese esquema de que las empresas tienen derecho de quedarse con los dólares que se producen por las ventas que hacen es una trampa

, porque esos dólares fueron generados por la sociedad argentina. Esas empresas no podrían vender sin toda la infraestructura y sin los trabajadores”.




La entrada 

Las cuentas no cierran en Vaca Muerta: la fuga de dólares que oculta el relato extractivo

 se publicó primero en 

Agencia de Noticias Tierra Viva

.

author: Unknown
title: PFDKê ceza li Amedsporê birî
content:
Lijneya Dîsiplînê ya Futbola Profesyonel (PFDK), biryarên xwe yên derbarê bûyerên ku di maçên hefteya 7an a Lîga Superê de qewimîbûn, eşkere kir.




PFDKê di mijarên, ji ber dirûşmên “kirêt û nexweş” ên alîgirên Gençlerbîrlîgiyê yên di maça Gençlerbîrlîgî-Amedsporê ya ku li Enqereyê hat lîstin de, kartên alîgirên ên li pişta qaleya bakûr, trîbuna rojava û vîpê biryara xwe da. PFDKê xwest hem ev kes werin astengkirin û ketina wan a maçên din bê qedexekirin.




Li gorî nûçeya Ajansa Welat PFDKê 280 hezar lîre cezayê pere li Amedsporê birî. Lijneyê ev ceza wekî “bûyerên li qadê” bi nav kir û cih neda bê ka ev bûyer çi ne. Lijneyê ji ber bûyerên di gelek maçên dawiya hefteyê de qewimîn, cezayên cûda dan tîman.




Maça Mardînspor û Bursasporê




Di Lîga 1emîn a Trendyolê de, di maça ku Bursasporê di 11ê Cotmehê de li qada xwe li dijî Mardîn 1969 Sporê lîst û 2-1 winda kir.




Alîgirên Bursasporê hema hema di seranserê maçê de dirûşmên nexweş berz kirin. Dîmenên van dirûşmên nexweş li ser platformên medyaya dîjîtal bi hezaran caran hatin parvekirin. Bi taybetî dirûşmên nexweş ên li dijî golparêzê Mardînsporê Erce Kardeşler bûn rojev.




Lê belê, PFDKê ji ber bûyerên qadê li gorî xalên 52/2 û 46/1 ên FDTyê (cezarkirina tîmê ya ji ber bûyerên qadê yên ku ji aliyê temaşevan, endamên klûbê an jî futbolvanan ve hatine kirin; avêtina madeyên biyanî bo nav qadê, ketina temaşevanan bo nav qadê, vêxistina meşaleyan hwd. vedihewîne) 140 hezar TL cezayê pereyan da.




Tevî ku dirûşmên kirêt û nexweş ên alîgirên Bursasporê yên di seranserê maçê de ji aliyê her kesê ku maç ji TVyê temaşe dikir ve hat bihîstin jî, nedana cezayekî bi vî rengî careke din nîşan da ku PFDK biryarên çiqas alîgir digire.




(AY)

author: Andrea DiP
title: Por que os estudantes voltaram às ruas? – com Gutemberg Rodrigues
content:
“Estamos na rua contra a extrema direita e, sobretudo, contra o que ela representa de retrocesso no nosso país”,  é o que afirma o vice-presidente da União Nacional dos Estudantes, Gutemberg Rodrigues, nesta entrevista para o Pauta Pública que analisa a volta de estudantes às ruas após o resultado do primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais.




Desde o dia 5 de outubro, universitários têm organizado assembleias e manifestações em apoio à reeleição de Lula em diferentes cidades brasileiras. Na conversa com Andrea Dip, Gutemberg relembra o papel histórico do movimento estudantil na resistência a retrocessos, na defesa da educação pública e na formação de novas lideranças políticas, destacando também a importância de defender direitos já conquistados.

author: anred
title: Argentina, no la entenderías: la marcha que transformó un reclamo universitario en una batalla contra el ajuste
content:
Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




La quinta Marcha Federal Universitaria desbordó su reclamo original y se convirtió en una movilización multisectorial contra el ajuste. Universidades, sindicatos y organizaciones sociales defendieron la educación pública, la soberanía, los derechos sociales y los bienes comunes. Más de 100 mil personas marcharon al Congreso pese a la represión estatal. 

Por Melina Deledicque (trabajadora no docente de la Facultad de Trabajo Social de la UNLP) y Mariano Féliz (trabajador docente de la Facultad de Humanidades y Ciencias de la Educación de la UNLP), para Huella del Sur.







Cronología de una marcha que unió las luchas




Hace un mes, el movimiento universitario resolvió convocar a la quinta Marcha Federal Universitaria para el jueves 15 de octubre en la Plaza de Mayo, frente a la sede del Poder Ejecutivo.




La convocatoria respondió a la negativa del Gobierno nacional a cumplir la resolución dictada por el juez de primera instancia Martín Cormick, que ordena al Poder Ejecutivo aplicar la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario, a casi un año de su aprobación. 

Según el Gobierno

, la ley no está siendo incumplida, sino que se encuentra “suspendida”. Sin embargo, el Poder Ejecutivo desoye el fallo judicial, que dispone la actualización de los salarios docentes y Nodocentes y de las becas estudiantiles conforme a lo establecido por la ley.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Mientras tanto, el proyecto de Presupuesto 2027 contempla partidas aproximadamente un 33% inferiores a 

las solicitadas

 por el Consejo Interuniversitario Nacional (CIN): mientras el Gobierno prevé unos 7,3 billones de pesos para las universidades nacionales, el CIN reclama 11 billones.




El miércoles 14 de octubre, el juez Cormick hizo efectivo el apercibimiento que había dispuesto previamente y fijó astreintes —multas compulsivas— de 100.000 pesos diarios para Diego Santilli, titular de la Jefatura de Gabinete, mientras persista el incumplimiento de la resolución judicial. La sanción recae inicialmente sobre Santilli y podría extenderse a otros funcionarios o incrementarse si el Gobierno no acata la decisión. Sin embargo, el mismo día de la movilización, la Cámara de Apelaciones puso en suspenso la multa.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Todo cambió con la resolución de la Corte Suprema de habilitar el artículo 154 del DNU 70/23, permitiendo la extranjerización sin límites de tierras rurales en Argentina. Si bien, frente al repudio popular, la Corte 

dio marcha atrás

, el clima político ya se había enrarecido.




Estas circunstancias aceleraron la convocatoria de la oposición en la Cámara de Diputados para avanzar en el rechazo definitivo del DNU 70/23. En esa misma sesión se proponía discutir también la prórroga de la Ley de Emergencia en Discapacidad y una ley destinada a aliviar la situación de las familias sobreendeudadas y en mora.




Recordemos que el Senado de la Nación ya había votado la derogación del DNU 70/23 a comienzos de 2024. Ese decreto continúa en el centro de la escena por sus efectos sobre el precio de los alquileres, las tasas de interés de los créditos y las cuotas de la medicina prepaga, entre otros aspectos. En la Cámara de Diputados, la oposición nunca consiguió los votos necesarios para avanzar en ese sentido. Lamentablemente, este jueves tampoco se alcanzó el quórum para habilitar la sesión. 

Varios gobernadores

 aliados del gobierno libertariano blindaron el DNU 70/23, ya que diputados de Tucumán, Jujuy y Santa Fe vaciaron sus bancas, al igual que los gobernadores de Unión por la Patria, Melella y Zamora.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Con ese contexto, la comunidad universitaria decidió que la movilización sería frente al Congreso. De esa manera, en pocas semanas, una marcha inicialmente convocada por el movimiento universitario se transformó en una movilización multisectorial de alcance nacional, con concentraciones frente al Congreso y en las principales plazas de todo el país.




La movilización sumó más de 100 mil personas en CABA (y decenas de miles más en el resto del país)

, y se sostuvo a pesar de un clima inhóspito e incluso un chaparrón intenso al cierre. A la misma se sumaron 

organizaciones de personas con discapacidad, de familias endeudadas, sindicatos combativos —como los integrantes del FreSU, bancarios, aceiteros, camioneros y otros—, e incluso la CGT

.




Como tantas veces, ante el reclamo legítimo para exigir el cumplimiento de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario, la única respuesta de un gobierno abiertamente autoritario es la represión. Antes del cierre del acto iniciado alrededor de las 15:30 horas, las fuerzas de seguridad salieron a “despejar” la Plaza de los dos Congresos con gases lacrimógenos y carros hidrantes.




Una marcha multisectorial con una prenda de unidad: defender la vida en común




A pesar de que el Congreso no sesionó, podríamos decir que la marcha logró un objetivo superior. Si decimos que articuló múltiples demandas sectoriales, no estaríamos equivocados, pero esa mirada sería insuficiente si no lográramos ver lo que las vincula.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




En los hechos, 

a casi tres años del inicio del gobierno de Milei, la movilización convocada unifica a las comunidades agredidas por el programa de austeridad y crueldad del gobierno libertariano.

 La agenda de las organizaciones pone en el centro a quienes se encuentran en situaciones de mayor vulnerabilidad y a quienes sostienen su defensa: 

jubilades, personas con discapacidad, estudiantes y trabajadores universitaries, personal sanitario y familias endeudadas

.




Lo que se puso en juego este jueves es la utopía de construir una sociedad que priorice la reproducción de la vida en todos sus momentos y etapas, en sus formas simbólicas y materiales. 

Lo que esta movilización pone en el centro es el conjunto de los bienes comunes: la tierra y el territorio, el conocimiento como bien colectivo y no mercancía, y el cuidado de la vida de las personas

.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Las luchas van tejiendo un entramado político y delineando un camino de superación radical del plan libertariano de Milei. La pregunta que se abre es si el sistema político, tan fracturado y degradado como el actual, podrá nutrirse de esas energías colectivas para abrir una etapa capaz de sepultar el programa de guerra de las clases dominantes contra los sectores populares.




Será una batalla decisiva, aunque no la última ni la definitiva.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Imagen: Melina Deledicque.




Fuente: 

https://huelladelsur.ar/2026/10/15/argentina-no-la-entenderias-la-marcha-que-transformo-un-reclamo-universitario-en-una-batalla-contra-el-ajuste/

author: Cas Smith
title: Land Forces weapons expo protested in a time of genocide
content:
Around 2000 anti-war activists took to the streets on October 6, in a strong rebuke to the weapons’ manufacturers displaying their wares at the Land Forces International Land Defence Exposition and Western Australian Labor, which welcomed it.

The rally, one of the biggest in recent years, began at Yagan Square near Northbridge, before marching through the city to Elizabeth Quay, close to the Perth Convention Centre.

A “security area” had been set up around the expo venue, which included the Elizabeth Quay train station and several sections of surrounding streets.

A new law, the Land Forces (Special Powers) Act 2026, gave police the “ability to establish checkpoints, cordons, and roadblocks, while also searching people, bags, and vehicles, and issue lawful directions for a 10-day period”, until October 10.

Alongside this, several activists had been told they were banned from the security area, and could face fines of up to $36,000 and three years in prison if they challenged this.

The media coverage of these repressive security initiatives — to which WA Premier Roger Cook had allocated $11.5 million — may have encouraged people to come to the rally, which was hosted by WA Anti-War Collective, Stop AUKUS WA, Nuclear Free WA, Independent and Peaceful Australia Network (IPAN), Friends of Palestine WA (FOPWA), Students for Palestine WA, Right To Protest WA and Extinction Rebellion Western Australia.

It included several creative aspects, including a flash mob dance to the tune of the Temptations’ song “War” and a performance by Drummers for Climate Action.

Noongar Elders Uncle Headley Hayward and Uncle Herbert Bropho gave the Welcome to Country. Adrian Glamorgan (Independent and Peaceful Australia Network and Stop AUKUS WA), Danica Scott (Stop AUKUS WA and Freiends of Palestine WA), Greens MLC Sophie McNeill, Rojin Didari (Students for Palestine WA) and Berlin Guerrero (Migrante and International People’s Struggle) addressed the protest.

Sam Wainwright (Stop AUKUS WA), who MCed the rally, said Labor’s decision to roll out the red carpet for weapons manufacturers indicated his priorities.

“[Land Forces] comes in the context of a worldwide increase in military expenditure, including a 50% increase in military expenditure by Donald Trump. It comes in the context of the genocide in Gaza, and a climate emergency,” Wainwright said.

“It poses the question: What is the real response of our rulers to what are known as the ‘poly crises’ of capitalism. Is it not repression at home and war abroad?”

It was particularly horrific that weapons used in Gaza would be on display at the exhibition, Wainwright added.

“For the last three years, we have begged this federal government to stop sending arms to Israel and to cancel bilateral military ties, because it’s the one thing you’d do if you were serious about stopping the genocide.

“Labor won’t, because it has committed to making Australia one of the 10 major weapons exporters in the world. Roger Cook has said he wants to make weapons exports the number two industry in WA. The place of Israel in the military industrial complex means deepening bilateral military ties with that state.”

Elbit Systems and Rafael were among the Israeli weapons companies featured at Land Forces, alongside Lockheed Martin, which constructs the F-35 fighter jets used in much of the destruction of Gaza.

author: Ash Sarkar
title: A Motion, a Meltdown, and an Andy Burnham-Shaped Opportunity
content:
They’re calling it the E motion heard around the world, as the fallout continues from the Green party’s ‘Zionism is Racism’ policy, passed at its conference earlier this month.




The motion has dominated the headlines since making it onto the agenda for autumn conference, eclipsing what the leadership had hoped would be the party’s trademark rent controls policy. It kicked off a briefing war, led by GPEW stalwart and second referendum-enthusiast Caroline Lucas. It also prompted 

pointed queries

 from the Equalities and Human Rights Commission.




And now, unwilling to let a good crisis pass him by, prime minister Andy Burnham has piled in, 

ruling out any future coalition

 with the Greens while the policy remains in place. Supporters of the motion may greet this news as a strategic win – distance from Labour cements the Greens’ status as an insurgent, anti-establishment force. But there are rumblings of discontent amongst parts of the Green party of England and Wales.




It’s no secret that Zack Polanski (while publicly supportive of the argument that Israel’s displacement of, and genocide against, the Palestinians is the result of racist ideology) needed this motion like he needed a hole in the head. He was careful to neither unequivocally back nor deride the motion, and warned that it may “create a distraction” by putting Green members and pro-Palestine activists in a position of being attacked.




Whatever the virtues of the motion were, and still might be, Polanski was proved right on this latter point. The days leading up to his unsuccessful attempt to become the MP for Holborn and St Pancras were a storm of negative media coverage, in which he was forced to defend his party against accusations of being a threat to Jewish people. It would be wrong to characterise the byelection loss as a direct result of the ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion. But it didn’t exactly help his efforts to get elected either.




What followed were the first stirrings of Green infighting. For those steeped in the factional bloodletting of Labour party politics, this is all fairly tame stuff: Lucas, the night of the count, 

failing to shut down talk

 of Polanski stepping down, Ellie Chowns 

calling on her leader to “step up”

. But while the Greens might put the ‘civil’ in civil war, this level of publicly-litigated internal division is new for the party.




What’s more, local Green parties and councils have had to manage the reactions of a significant number of Jewish residents and organisations. Haringey council, led by the Greens, found its attempts at overture 

knocked back

 by one local synagogue. “We take it from both the tone and the content of your email that you are deeply embarrassed with the decision taken by your party,” wrote Highgate United Synagogue. “[Your] embarrassment is not enough. If you really want us to feel you do not agree with the racist and genocidal implications of your party’s policy, the least we can expect is for you to publicly resile yourself from that policy and commit yourself and your party colleagues to reverse that policy.”




Enter one Andrew Burnham. Though the early months of his premiership have been marked by his attempts to mend fences with voters alienated from Labour by the party’s moral turpitude on Palestine, the temptation to kick his progressive rivals while they’re down was seemingly too much to resist.




Condemning the motion in the House of Commons at this week’s PMQs, 

Burnham thundered

: “It is wrong, it is antisemitic, and this side of the House will have nothing to do with it.” Polanski, in a statement, hit back, pointing out that he’s the only Jewish leader of a political party and himself a victim of antisemitism – while the prime minister “arms a genocide and locks pensioners up for opposing it”.




Westminster grandstanding has since filtered down to local governance. Yesterday, Labour issued an ultimatum, saying it would scrap any power-sharing deals with Greens in local authorities unless local Green electeds reject the ‘Zionism is Racism’ motion passed by members at conference. According to the New Statesman, such agreements prop up 

more than a dozen local authorities

, including in Bristol. Nice gauntlet you’ve got there, shame if anyone threw it.




Perhaps Alanis Morissette might have something to say about a devolution-loving prime minister imposing the will of the Westminster government on local authorities the minute he thinks it’s advantageous to do so. It’s worth pointing out that it has every chance of backfiring on the Labour party – there are few voters who want to see local government dysfunction inflicted in the name of protecting Israel’s state ideology. Labour lost votes over Gaza, and it might prove unwise for Burnham to remind people of that particular issue.




But we’re at a moment where the interests of Green electeds, and some Green activists, are at odds. The May 2026 breakthrough was powered by thousands of Green members – doorknocking, canvassing, leafleting, and getting out the vote. But that very achievement, getting Greens into councils where they might advance the eco-socialist cause by delivering for voters, is easily imperilled by that selfsame membership attempting to remodel the party in their image. That’s a tension: and one that Burnham is determined to exploit.




You can see how this puts Polanski in an invidious position. On the one hand, there’s making and protecting electoral gains, and establishing the Green party’s credibility by governing effectively. On the other, there’s standing with his members when they’re under ferocious attack by the British establishment (even if he’d rather not have picked this particular battle). But perhaps the looming interest of the EHRC, who wrote to the Greens citing the “many Jewish people [feeling] vulnerable” as a result of the motion, might hint at a way out.




Should the Greens face legal challenge, or EHRC investigation, the tactical case for reintroducing the amendments aimed at protecting Jewish members within the party gets stronger. If Polanski backs it wholeheartedly for spring conference, he might just find a way of mitigating the attack lines on antisemitism – and get back to the things he’d much rather talk about.

author: groundxero
title: No Bonus, Unpaid Wages, Missing PF Dues: Thousands of Tea Workers Take to the Streets in North Bengal
content:
More than a hundred tea estates in North Bengal reportedly missed the 5 October deadline for payment of the 20% annual bonus. Thousands of workers across Merico-Sammelan gardens in the Dooars are protesting unpaid bonuses, outstanding wages and provident fund dues, even as the state government’s assurances and meetings yield little.




 




Groundxero

 | 16 October 2026




 




On the morning of Shashthi, as people across Kolkata throng Durga Puja pandals, women tea garden workers in North Bengal are taking to the streets to fight for a bonus that should already have been in their bank accounts. Workers, led by women workers from Hantapara, Gayerdanga and Dumkipara tea estates marched towards Madarihat to demand payment of their bonus. Workers at Birpara are preparing similar protests, while others staged demonstrations outside factory gates and approached the police.




 




Their immediate demand is straightforward: payment of the full 20% annual bonus. But the protests expose a much wider crisis of unpaid wages, withheld provident fund contributions, unpaid gratuity, and the continuing impunity enjoyed by tea garden owners.




 




At the centre of the current confrontation is the Merico Agro Industries and Sammelan Tea & Beverages group, which controls 12–13 tea estates employing nearly 10,000 workers, the vast majority of them women. The management has sought to persuade workers to accept a bonus of just 10%. The workers, led by the Paschim Banga Cha Majdur Samiti (PBCMS), have refused to settle for half of what they are demanding.




 




The West Bengal government had set 5 October as the deadline for payment of a 20% bonus to tea garden workers. Yet, according to available reports, only 170 of the Dooars’ 285 tea gardens had paid bonuses by 10 October. More than a hundred estates had reportedly failed to pay workers even a single rupee.




 




The failure is particularly revealing because the change of government in West Bengal was accompanied by the BJP’s promise of a new political and administrative dispensation. For tea garden workers, however, the much-publicised ‘double engine’ government appears to be running along the same tracks as its predecessor: false assurances for workers, impunity for defaulting employers, and little effective action to compel payment.




 




Last year, the Trinamool Congress government had also advised employers to pay a 20% bonus. This year, the BJP government issued a similar directive, setting a deadline of 5 October. But an advisory, however emphatically worded, is no substitute for enforcement. Employers continue to delay and withheld payments while workers lose wages, spend days in demonstrations and struggle to meet their basic needs.




 




Pay slips issued but no payment made 




 




The confrontation at Bagrakote Tea Garden illustrates the gap between management promises and workers’ actual experience. After the bonus remained unpaid, workers went on strike and blocked the Siliguri–Dooars national highway at Meena More. Following the mobilisation, the management issued a notice promising payment of the 20% bonus by 13–14 October.




 




Both dates passed without the promised payment.




 




On the night of 14 October, owner Surajit Bakshi telephoned PBCMS leaders and reportedly asked them to persuade workers to accept a 10% bonus, saying that this was all he had managed to arrange. The union refused to endorse the proposal, maintaining the workers’ demand for the full bonus.




 




On 15 October, garden managers distributed pay slips promising a 20% bonus. Workers waited for the money to arrive in their bank accounts. Managers waited for funds to become available. Police stood guard over the managers, while rumours circulated among workers that payments had been made in neighbouring areas.




 




By 10 pm, according to PBCMS, not one of the approximately 10,000 workers employed across the Merico-Sammelan group’s gardens had received any money.




 




The episode captures the absurdity of a system in which paperwork and promises can be produced on schedule, but the payment of workers’ dues remains indefinitely negotiable. The workers are expected to trust pay slips, wait through successive deadlines and accept management’s financial difficulties as an excuse. Their own financial difficulties, and their rightful dues, meanwhile, receive little consideration.




 




Labour department calls meetings without accountability




 




The labour department’s handling of the dispute has added to workers’ frustration. According to PBCMS, one meeting was cancelled on the grounds that management representatives were busy arranging bonus payments. No payment followed. At another meeting, union representatives reportedly waited for six hours without any meaningful discussion. The proceedings eventually deteriorated into shouting and the breaking of chairs, with BJP-affiliated union leaders allegedly abusing their own MLA, Puna Bhengra.




 




For workers already waiting for their dues, such meetings mean another day lost without a resolution. The spectacle of official consultations cannot conceal the absence of effective intervention.




 




The crisis is not confined to the annual bonus. PBCMS alleges that almost all the Merico-Sammelan gardens owe workers three to four fortnights’ wages, last year’s leave allowance and 10% of last year’s unpaid bonus. The union also alleges that provident fund (PF) contributions deducted from workers’ salaries have not been deposited into the Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (

EPFO

) accounts since June 2023—an action unions label as criminal breach of trust. Retired workers are reportedly dying without receiving their gratuity.




 




Meanwhile, factories have shut, gardens have deteriorated and green leaves are reportedly being sold through brokers. The conditions raise serious questions about the management of these estates, the protection of workers’ livelihoods and the government’s willingness to hold employers accountable.




 




Workers suffer for the owners’ impunity




 




Workers are mobilising across the Dooars and North Bengal, with protests reported at Dumkipara, Lankapara, Hantapara, Nagaisuri, Garganda and other gardens associated with the group. Women workers have been at the forefront of the mobilisation, marching towards Madarihat and organising demonstrations at factory gates. Workers in Birpara have also been preparing to join the protests.




 




Their determination exposes the unequal balance of power in the tea industry. Workers whose labour sustains the plantations must organise, march and confront the authorities to secure payments that are already due to them. Employers, by contrast, appear able to delay and even withheld payment even after announcing deadlines and issuing written assurances.




 




The reports of prolonged non-deposit of provident fund contributions are particularly grave. The government must also address the reported non-payment of wages and gratuity. Issuing advisories and convening meetings will not resolve the crisis unless the authorities ensure that employers meet their obligations and face consequences for violations. The failure to secure payment by the announced deadline demands an explanation of what enforcement measures, if any, have been taken.




 




PBCMS has demanded immediate payment of the full 20% bonus, all outstanding wages, leave allowance and gratuity, the deposit of every rupee deducted towards provident fund contributions, and legal action against those responsible for violations.




 




These are not extravagant demands. They concern workers’ earnings, statutory entitlements and economic security. The government must move beyond assurances and take effective steps to ensure that workers receive what is owed to them.




 




As people in Kolkata sip tea between visits to Durga Puja pandals, the workers who produce that tea are fighting to obtain their own unpaid dues. The contrast is stark: the festive economy depends on workers’ labour, yet thousands of them face the prospect of celebrating the festival season without money that should already have been paid.




 




The Government has changed but the ‘Acche Din’ of tea garden owners appears remarkably secure. The BJP’s ‘double engine’ government now faces a simple test: will it enforce workers’ rights, or will it let garden owners to continue with their illegal exploitative labour practices, while its engines runs smoothly — in the service of employers!




 




Workers cannot pay their bills with government advisories, feed their families with pay slips or retire on false promises. Unless the workers’ united struggle force authorities to compel employers to pay, the change of government will mean little to the thousands of women and men whose labour sustains North Bengal’s tea gardens, and its economy.

author: Enrico Gnaulati, PhD
title: The Hidden Psychotherapy Drop-Out Crisis
content:
T

here is a psychotherapy drop-out crisis that the general public is largely unaware of and the mental health field apparently overlooks. 

Conservative estimates

 of the 

number of people who discontinue psychotherapy

 after starting hover around 28-33 percent, with well upwards of half doing so within the first few sessions. 

Trustworthy sources

 reveal that the 

median number of sessions

 received by people entering psychotherapy falls somewhere between seven and nine.




I call these estimates conservative because the way psychotherapy drop-out is typically defined and measured reflects medicalized models of short-term interventions aimed primarily at symptom reduction. 

Evidence-based treatment protocols

 considered adequate for improvement typically last 12-16 sessions, with 

a range of roughly 6 to 20 sessions

 depending on the type of disorder and its severity.




Admittedly, there are those people for whom a brief course of therapy aimed at symptom reduction is both preferred and satisfactory. However, it appears that such individuals are in the minority. 

A recent survey sponsored by the Psychotherapy Action Network (PsiAN)

 of more than 1500 adults in the U.S. found that 88 percent “Prefer therapy that may take longer because it helps you manage your symptoms and also addresses the root cause of problems.” Moreover, a substantial number of clients who receive short-term evidence-based treatments do not walk away recovered. 

One set of meta-analyses of depression treatments

 observed that more than half of clients studied failed to respond (experience at least a 50 percent reduction in symptoms) and only one third were in remission upon completion, or experienced symptoms at subclinical levels.




Image created by AI tool




All this begs the question: How much psychotherapy does the typical person need  presenting with some combination of anxiety, depression, difficult personality traits, and life distress, to obtain meaningful and lasting change?




Recent robust meta-analytic findings deliver an answer. A 

study out of University College London

 assessing the results of sixteen randomized trials of long-term intensive psychotherapy substantiated that obtaining a course of treatment greater than or equal to 9 months, or 30 sessions, is associated with significant and sustained alleviation of depression, compared to active, less intensive treatments. Another 

research team out of Amsterdam found

 that obtaining 50 psychotherapy sessions a year (beginning twice weekly) produced faster and greater amelioration of depression and difficult personality traits than approximately 25 sessions.




Consequently, if we land on 30-50 sessions of psychotherapy as a ballpark reasonable  number of sessions for the typical anxious and depressed client facing interpersonal challenges to obtain meaningful and sustained change, it falls woefully short of the median 7-9 sessions most people typically receive when they pursue psychotherapy.




What accounts for this underutilization? Obviously, there are the material and logistical reasons that people cite for discontinuing: cost/financial hardship, inadequate insurance coverage, transportation issues, scheduling conflicts. Nonetheless, in my estimation a pivotal overlooked reason is the discrepancy between what most people embarking on psychotherapy seek from the experience and what legions of practitioners are trained to provide.




The PsiAN survey cited above underscored how 73 percent of participants agreed that “The most valuable aspect of therapy is sharing your thoughts and feelings without feeling judged or ashamed”; and 67 percent of those asked why people sought therapy endorsed the statement: 

“

To better understand yourself and the root of your issues.” Extrapolating from these results, it would seem that most people cultivate preferences for age-old notions of psychotherapy that have proven remarkable durable: A culturally sanctioned space to candidly share whatever is on your mind for as long is needed to obtain fundamental salutary shifts in how you feel about yourself and your life.




Yet, current professional training diverges from this ethos, underscoring evidence-based treatments, or short-term, protocol-driven approaches to psychotherapy focused on symptom reduction. The 

National Psychotherapy Training Survey

, conducted over the past few decades 

points to greater numbers

 of clinical psychology Ph.D. programs (81 percent, up from 56 percent) and Psy.D. programs (59 percent, up from 33 percent) requiring evidence-based practice training, and 75 percent of programs across the mental health disciplines surveyed offered some mix of didactic and supervised training in these methods.




Even though in the psychotherapy world it is common knowledge that the therapy alliance—good rapport rooted to relational sensitivity and responsiveness to client needs—constitutes one of the most robust predictors of psychotherapy outcome, formal coursework devoted to alliance building remains remarkably rare. In 

a survey of APA-accredited clinical and counseling psychology doctoral programs

, only 17 percent required students to take even one alliance-related course, and only 13 percent offered an elective course specifically covering the therapeutic alliance.




We have to wonder whether the training and education of countless psychotherapists sets them up to force feed clients formulaic models of treatment they are well-versed in, rather than fall back on the tried-and-true old standards of careful and caring listening—striving to make the client fit the therapy, rather than the therapy fit the client.







There may be something to my point of view. A 

recent study looking at premature psychotherapy discontinuance

 zeroed in on seven themes: therapist misattunement, inert therapeutic relationships, unmanaged therapist responses, unmanaged therapist interventions, rigid protocol adherence, readiness for change, and repeating interpersonal dynamics.




We know with confidence that it bodes well for psychotherapy continuance when 

practitioners can be responsive to clients’ needs and preferences

. We also know with confidence that a 

strong psychotherapy alliance is associated with lower drop-out numbers

. Taking matters a crucial step further, if we are to turn the tide of psychotherapy drop-out, the mental health field will need to seriously grapple with prioritizing the type of education and training of psychotherapists that optimizes the sort of genuine relating, open-ended listening, and emotional responsiveness that renders psychotherapy meaningful and effective enough for clients to want to stick with it.




The post 

The Hidden Psychotherapy Drop-Out Crisis

 appeared first on 

Mad In America

.

author: Richard Sears
title: Four New Studies Raise Concerns About Benzodiazepine-Related Harms
content:
T

his week, 

Mad in America

 examines four new studies around harms linked to benzodiazepine use. The first finds that benzodiazepines are linked to increased risk of heart failure and heart failure related hospitalization. The second reports that long-term benzodiazepine use (60 days or longer) is associated with worse cognitive function in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. The third finds that taking these drugs during pregnancy is linked to an increased risk of miscarriage. The fourth links benzodiazepines to increased risk of falls and fractures in older adults.







Benzodiazepines Linked to Increased Risk of Heart Failure




A new 

study

 published in 

Cardiovascular Toxicology

 finds that benzodiazepine use is linked to higher risk of heart failure and heart failure related hospitalization in people prescribed these drugs to treat insomnia. This research, led by Yi-Sin Huang from Taipei Medical University in Taiwan, also suggests that benzodiazepines are associated with a higher risk of heart failure hospitalization than other drugs used to treat insomnia.




The goal of this study was to examine the link between heart failure and benzodiapepine use in people with insomnia. The authors also wanted to compare heart failure outcomes between benzodiapepines and other drugs prescribed for insomnia. They conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of previous research on this topic. In total, they used data from 11 studies.




Benzodiazepine use was linked to a 41% increased risk of heart failure and a 29% increased risk of heart failure related hospitalization compared to non-use. The risk of heart failure related hospitalizations in people taking these drugs to treat insomnia was also elevated compared to other drugs, including Z-drugs, suvorexant,and antipsychotics. These increased risks were particularly elevated in people that had a history of heart failure and those at high-risk.




This research had three main limitations. Most of the included studies were observational, meaning the findings can speak to a link between bezodiazepines and heart failure, but cannot definitively say that these drugs cause heart failure. Only 11 studies were included in the current work. The included studies varied significantly in follow-up range, methods, and patient populations.




Benzodiazepines Linked to Worse Cognitive Functioning




A new 

study

 published in 

BMC Psychiatry

 finds that long-term benzodiazepine use is linked to worse cognitive functioning in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. This research, led by Caiping Liu from the Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine in China, also reports that there was no significant difference in terms of cognition between low- and high-dose users. This means that while any long-term benzodiazepine use was associated with poorer cognition, the current work did not find that higher doses were linked to poorer cognitive function.




The authors used data from the SALT-C study in China, a research project around atypical antipsychotic use in people diagnosed with schizophrenia. They used data collected from 114 SALT-C participants recruited at the Shanghai Mental Health Center between 2016 and 2019. For the purposes of analysis the authors divided participants into two groups, people that had never taken benzodiazepines before and those that had taken a stable dose for at least 60 consecutive days. Each of these groups included 57 participants. The groups were similar in terms of sex, age, duration of illness, and types of atypical antipsychochotics prescribed. There were also no significant differences in overall psychiatric symptoms severity, “illness” severity, or psychological functioning.




Long-term benzodiazepine users had an average score of 16.02 on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment compared to 19.33 for non-users. This indicated significantly poorer cognitive performance for participants taking benzodiazepines for at least 60 consecutive days. This deficit was observed mostly in the visuospatial and executive cognitive domain, meaning benzodiazepine users had greater difficulty understanding visual/spatial information and planning, organizing, and solving problems. The authors note that there was no clear dose-response relationship between benzodiazepine use and cognitive impairment. This means similar cognitive impairment was observed in both low- and high-dose users.




This research had four main limitations. Cognitive ability was assessed at one point in time and the authors were not able to track cognitive changes before and after exposure to benzodiazepines. As a result, the findings cannot establish that benzodiazepine use caused poorer cognition, only that these factors are linked. Unmeasured factors may have affected the outcomes. All participants came from a single treatment facility in China, limiting generalizability. The relatively low number of participants further limits generalizability.




Benzodiazepines Use During Pregnancy Linked to Miscarriage




A new 

study

 published in 

BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth

 links benzodiazepine use during pregnancy to miscarriage. This research, led by Cyndie Picot from the Hospices Civils de Lyon in France, also presents some evidence that miscarriage risk increases with dose.




The aim of this study was to investigate the link between benzodiazepine use during pregnancy and miscarriage. The authors also wanted to examine whether miscarriage risk varied between individual benzodiazepines. They conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of previous research around benzodiazepines and miscarriage. To be included in the current work, studies had to compare miscarriage risk between a group that used benzodiazepines during pregnancy and one that did not. The researchers used data from 10 studies.




Overall, benzodiazepine use during pregnancy was linked to a 68% increased risk of miscarriage. All seven individual benzodiazepines with at least 100 exposed pregnancies were linked to greater risk of miscarriage:










Clonazepam – 82% increased risk










Diazepam – 70%










Lorazepam – 48%










Alprazolam – 48%










Oxazepam – 48%










Bromazepam – 55%










Chlordiazepoxide – 42%










While the meta-analysis found increased risk for each of these individual benzodiazepines, the results did not reach statistical significance for bromazepam and chlordiazepoxide.




Three included studies examined the dose-response relationship between benzodiazepine use and miscarriage, with all three reporting that larger doses translated to higher risk. For example, one study reported an 84% increased risk of miscarriage for low dose clonazepam compared to a more than quadrupled risk (4.5 times higher odds) for high doses. The authors note that they were unable to combine results from the these three studies into a single does-response estimate due to significant differences in definitions and methods.




This research had four main limitations. Five of ten included studies had a high risk of bias due to the possibility of unmeasured factors affecting the findings. Included studies were mostly observational, meaning these results cannot definitively say that bezodiazepines caused miscarriage. Studies differed in their definition of miscarriage. Early miscarriages are likely under-reported, which could have affected the results.




Benzodiazepines Linked to Increased Risk of Falls and Fractures in Older Adults




A new 

literature review

 published in 

Medical Science

 reports that benzodiazepine use is linked to greater risk of falls and fractures in older patients. This review, led by Szymon Barczak from Mazovian Brodnowski Hospital in Poland, also reports that these risks may be greatest in the 24 hours after starting benzodiazepines.




The goal of this review was to examine the link between benzodiazepine use and fall/fracture risk in older adults. The authors reviewed 21 previously published studies on fall/fracture risk and benzodiazepine use in geriatric patients. Included studies had to be peer-reviewed and published in English.




Most included studies found a link between benzodiazepine use, falls, and fractures in older adults. Included studies found between a 40% to a more than tripled (3.128 times higher odds) increased risk of falls, and between 20% to nearly quadrupled (3.73) increased risk of fractures linked to benzodiazepine use. One study presented evidence that the risk of falls was nearly quadrupled (3.79 times higher odds) in the first 24 hours following the start of benzodiazepine use. Some included studies also reported that higher doses, longer duration of use, and polypharmacy were all linked to increased fall and fracture risk. The authors note that not all included studies linked benzodiazepine use to greater fall risk. Studies conducted with hospitalized participants were less likely to find a link between benzodiazepine use, falls, and fractures.




This study had 3 main limitations. Only English language studies were included, limiting generalizability. Included studies varied significantly in design, definitions of falls and fractures, and exposure periods. Most included studies were observational, meaning these results cannot say for certain that benzodiazepine use causes falls and fractures.




****




Barczak, S., Hertz, Z., & Barczak, J. (2026). The risk of falls and fractures in geriatric benzodiazepine users: A review. 

Medical Science

, 

30

(167), 1–11. (

Link

)

author: Kodao Productions
title: Marcos Congress set to pass another corrupt budget, progressives warn
content:
Progressive legislators expressed alarm over the 2027 national budget passed by the House of Representatives (HOR) on Monday, saying it is the opposite of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s promise of cleaner government spending.




“The Marcos budget they are passing is not a budget for Filipinos. It only funds politicians, political dynasties and war and militarism against our people,” the Makabayan Coalition lawmakers said in voting against the measure.




The HOR approved a P7.2-trillion budget for next year, the biggest in the country’s history. With a few alterations to accommodate pet projects of Marcos allies in the chamber, the total amount followed the national expenditure program earlier submitted by Marcos.




How did the budget pass so quickly?




Marcos allies control the HOR. Led by a Speaker loyal to the president and persuaded by the Senior Deputy Speaker who happens to be Marcos’ eldest son Sandro, 282 legislators agreed to the proposed budget.




Only 13 voted against the proposal while a lone representative abstained.




The HOR glowingly described the approved budget as a

 “

boost to public education and health, as well as the country’s preparations for El Niño” now starting to affect the Southeast Asian country.




Opponents of the measure, however, said Marcos’ budget is meant to continue both patronage politics and corruption the Philippine government is notorious for.




Who opposed Marcos’ planned budget?




Of the 254 district representatives of the Philippines Congress – as many as 80 per cent of whom are members of political dynasties – only five voted against the measure. Eight of their fellow oppositionists are party representatives, led by the three members of the progressive Makabayan Coalition.




The few HOR members who opposed the “porky” 2027 proposed General Appropriations Act. (HOR photo)




ACT Teachers Representative Antonio Tinio pointed out that while the Marcos proposal already reduced the budget for public health, the president’s allies further reduced Department of Health’s budget. He said funds on health facilities and equipment, commodities for family health, immunization, nutrition and responsible parenting, Health Promotion and Quick Response Fund would be reduced by billions of pesos.




Tinio also revealed that funds for education would be substantially cut, impacting construction and renovation of classrooms as well as the country’s school computerization program




Contrary to government claims the budget factors in effects of the El Niño, government’s calamity fund was also reduced by P9.5 billion, Tinio revealed.




What does the Marcos budget contain?




 

Appropriations Committee chairperson and Representative Mikaela Angela Suansing was in tears when the HOR approved the budget on Monday night, overjoyed by the approval of the proposal she pushed along for months.




“The House’s budget amendments were guided by the shared judgment of the House to protect key spending priorities, particularly education and healthcare, while responding to the most pressing needs of the Filipino people,” she claimed.




Leaders of the House of Representatives celebrate after passing its version of the 2027 General Appropriations Bill. (HOR photo)




Kabataan Youth Represenative Renee Louise Co, however, disagreed with Suansing’s glowing description of their work.




“Mister Speaker, this begs the question: What is taking up all that fiscal space? Year-in, year-out, the national budget is overflowing with pork [barrel],” Co exclaimed in her explanation of her rejection of the proposed budget.




Co revealed that the approved budget retained P361.19 billion for the Marcos government’s controversial infrastructure projects, such flood control and farm-to-market roads.




The budget would also give P136.94 billion to Marcos’ financial assistance programs the young legislator said are used to deodorize the president’s failure to defend the economy against uncertainties brought by the conflicts in West Asia.




Co also flagged the P51.88 billion that would be given to Marcos as “discretionary funds.”




Can the budget still be cleaned?




While the HOR holds the Philippine government’s “power of the purse,” the proposed 2027 budget has yet to go through the Philippine Senate before it is signed into law.




Tinio said he hopes that instead of introducing pork barrel-type amendments of its own, the Senate should make the necessary corrections by decreasing allotted funds for congressmen’s pet projects and increase the budget for social services.




Senate finance committee chairperson Jose Victor Ejercito flagged the realignment of P206 billion for the Representatives’ pet projects. Ejercito noted that roughly 206 allocations were altered by the HOR.




“So this leaves the Senate with very little for its own amendments,” Ejercito told reporters, referring to the Senators’ own pet projects.




Aside from President Marcos himself, both the HOR and the Senate are also blamed for the increasingly corrupt Philippine government budget that has led to hundreds of billions worth of anomalous projects.




Both Senators and congressmen are facing plunder charges before various Philippine courts, with an incumbent senator – Jose “Jinggoy” Estrada – and one representative – Marcos’ own cousin and former HOR Speaker Ferdinand Martin Romualdez currently in jail awaiting trial.




But as far as the HOR-approved 2027 proposed budget is concerned, the Marcos government does not seem to have learned any lesson at all. # 

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

Marcos Congress set to pass another corrupt budget, progressives warn

Η πρωτόδικη απόφαση αποτύπωσε τη σαφή κατεύθυνση του αστικού συστήματος να καταδικάσει ανθρώπους των κινημάτων και να τους εμπλέκει σε πολύχρονους και πολυέξοδους δικαστικούς αγώνες, για να φρενάρει τη λαϊκή απαιτητικότητα.




Ταυτόχρονα η απειλή φυλάκισης του Κ.Α. διεκδικεί να ολοκληρώσει την τρομοκρατική εκστρατεία που κορυφώθηκε στην πόλη του Βόλου με τον βασανισμό και την κρατική δολοφονία του Βασίλη Μάγγου. Τα επιχειρηματικά συμφέροντα ζητούν αίμα και διώξεις για να στεριώσουν.




Στα πλαίσια αυτά την Παρασκευή 16/10 στις 21:00 στο χώρο της Λέσχης εργαζομένων και νεολαίας, θα διεξαχθεί συζήτηση – ενημέρωση για τη δίκη του αγωνιστή Κ.Α., με συμμετοχή και του ίδιου, και θα ακολουθήσει μπαρ οικονομικής ενίσχυσης για τα δικαστικά έξοδα.
