Derzeit wird in Brüssel über den Vorschlag für eine neue EU-Verordnung diskutiert, die das europäische Asylsystem grundlegend verändern würde. Josephine Liebl vom Europäischen Flüchtlingsrat ECRE erklärt die schwerwiegenden Folgen. Das Asylrecht als Ganzes steht zur Disposition, wenn EU-Länder nach Belieben Ausnahmeregelungen erlassen können.




[Frage] Aktuell wird im Rat der EU über den

 Vorschlag der EU-Kommission für eine Verordnung

 

 

 diskutiert, die es den Mitgliedstaaten erlauben soll, im Falle einer »Instrumentalisierung« von Asyl und Migration von ihren Verpflichtungen nach dem Asylrecht abzuweichen. Was ist so gefährlich daran?




Diese Verordnung würde es den Ländern ermöglichen, ganz offiziell vom geltenden EU-Recht abzuweichen, also Asylstandards nicht anzuwenden. Es klingt absurd, aber es handelt sich tatsächlich um einen Gesetzesvorschlag, der regulieren soll, wann das Recht ausgesetzt wird. Alle Versuche, die Mitgliedstaaten anzuhalten, das Asylrecht einzuhalten, werden durch diesen Gesetzesvorstoß torpediert. (…) Es soll zwar Regeln geben, unter welchen Umständen die Länder die geltenden Standards senken dürfen, aber diese Umstände sind so breit gefasst, dass Regierungen schon in alltäglichen Situationen – zum Beispiel, wenn Flüchtlinge versuchen, außerhalb der offiziellen Grenzübertritte ins Land zu gelangen – sagen könnten: »Wir werden instrumentalisiert und sind deshalb berechtigt, die Menschenrechte und das geltende EU-Recht auszusetzen.«  Wir von ECRE befürchten, dass Regierungen wie die polnische oder die griechische künftig permanent mit einer Ausnahmesituation argumentieren werden, um das Recht zu umgehen. (…) 

Die Mitgliedstaaten dürften zum Beispiel bis zu vier Wochen warten, bis sie Asylanträge registrieren. Wir wissen aus Erfahrung – etwa an der griechisch-türkischen Grenze – dass die Gefahr von illegalen Pushbacks steigt und weitere Menschenrechtsverletzungen auftreten, wenn die Menschen nicht registriert sind. Denn dann weiß offiziell niemand, dass sie existieren und um Schutz bitten – das öffnet dem Missbrauch und der Willkür Tür und Tor.




[Was wird unter Instrumentalisierung überhaupt verstanden?]




Was genau unter Instrumentalisierung zu verstehen ist, bleibt vage. Es geht weit hinaus über die Situation an der polnisch-belarussischen Grenze, man kann alles da reinlesen. Damit ein Mitgliedstaat verkünden kann, dass er instrumentalisiert wird, ist es nicht nötig, dass eine bestimmte Anzahl an Menschen ins Land kommt. Stattdessen kann einfach jeder Staat behaupten, ein anderes Land oder ein nicht-staatlicher Akteur motiviere Menschen dazu, an seine Grenzen zu kommen, um die EU zu destabilisieren. Das wäre ausreichend, damit ein Mitgliedstaat argumentieren kann, die Ausnahmeregelungen in Anspruch nehmen zu dürfen. (…)




Nach dem Vorschlag der Kommission soll es so ablaufen, dass ein Mitgliedstaat, der sich instrumentalisiert fühlt, das äußert. Die Kommission schaut sich den konkreten Fall dann an und macht einen Vorschlag zum weiteren Vorgehen, über den die Nationalstaaten im Rat mit qualifizierter Mehrheit abstimmen. Somit hätte man durch die Kommission eine gewisse Kontrollinstanz. Momentan liegt der Vorschlag der Verordnung allerdings bei der tschechischen EU-Ratspräsidentschaft. Und viele Mitgliedstaaten wünschen sich eine viel aktivere Rolle des Rates, also der Nationalstaaten. Das lesen wir als Versuch, die EU-Kommission zu schwächen. (…)




Die Verordnung würde einem gemeinsamen europäischen Asylsystem den Todesstoß versetzen. Das bereits existierende Gefälle innerhalb der EU würde verstärkt: Binnenländer halten Standards ein, Länder mit Außengrenzen senken sie. (…) Leider haben wir von der Bundesregierung bisher nicht gehört, dass sie die geplante Absenkung von Asylstandards kategorisch ablehnt. Hier vermissen wir klare Worte und eine unmissverständliche Verurteilung des Kommissionsvorschlags

…“

„Solidaritätsmechanismus“: Systematische Haft an den Außengrenzen? Bundesregierung muss dies verhindern!  

„

Die Innenminister*innen der EU haben sich zwar auf einen freiwilligen Solidaritätsmechanismus für aus Seenot gerettete Menschen geeinigt. Aber ihre grundsätzliche Position zu Identitätsklärungs- und Grenzverfahren können die Lage von Schutzsuchenden in Europa stark verschlechtern, bis hin zu systematischer Haft an den EU-Außengrenzen. 

Am 10. Juni 2022 wurden im Rat der Europäischen Union entscheidende Weichen für die künftige Europäische Flüchtlingspolitik gestellt. Zu begrüßen ist, dass sich die Staaten auf einen neuen Solidaritätsmechanismus zur Aufnahme von aus Seenot geretteten Menschen einigen konnte. Dieser positive Schritt wird aber von weiteren Verschärfungen für Schutzsuchende an den EU-Außengrenzen flankiert. PRO ASYL befürchtet, dass die neue Positionierung der EU-Innenminister*innen das Recht von Flüchtlingen, an Europas Grenzen Asyl zu suchen, weiter beschneiden wird – so etwa ihre Positionierung zur Screening- und Eurodac-Verordnung (der Datenbank zur Identifikation von Schutzsuchenden) und zum Schengener Grenzkodex (der den Personenverkehr zwischen den EU-Staaten regelt). Insbesondere die vorgesehenen Verschärfungen bei der Grenzsicherung im Falle von »Instrumentalisierung von Migranten«, wenn etwa ein Drittstaat Flüchtlingen den Weg an die EU-Außengrenze erleichtert und darin ein vermeintlicher Destablisierungsversuch für die EU gelesen wird, bieten eine Steilvorlage für Mitgliedstaaten, die ihre rechtswidrigen Pushbacks europäisch legitimieren wollen. (…) 

Eine solche Fiktion der Nicht-Einreise trifft auf erhebliche Bedenken. Insbesondere ist zu erwarten, dass sie letztlich nur durch freiheitsbeschränkende bzw. –entziehende Maßnahmen durchgesetzt werden kann. Dies könnte zu systematischer Haft an den Außengrenzen führen. In Griechenland lässt sich dieser Ansatz schon jetzt beobachten. Die Einführung einer verpflichtenden Fiktion der Nicht-Einreise während des Screening-Verfahrens könnte zudem Wegbereiter für eine verpflichtende Fiktion der Nicht-Einreise auch während der auf drei Monate ausgweiteten Asylgrenzverfahren sein. Am 14. Dezember tagt der Rat der Europäischen Union für Justiz und Inneres darüber. Mit dem Vorhaben kommt die Kommission all jenen Mitgliedstaaten weit entgegen, die am liebsten gar keine Flüchtlinge aufnehmen wollen. Aber eben auch jenen, für die Menschenrechte und der Flüchtlingsschutz nur noch ein Lippenbekenntnis sind und die längst die Abriegelung Europas mitvorantreiben. Das Vorgehen erinnert an die Jahre 1992 und 1993, als in Deutschland mit dem sogenannten Asylkompromiss die Axt an das Grundrecht auf Asyl gelegt wurde. Der Vorschlag der Kommission verknüpft den Pakt mit Änderungsvorschlagen zur Asylverfahrensordnung aus dem Jahr 2016. Wann ein dritter Staat sicher im Sinne des Flüchtlingsrechts ist, ist bisher hoch umstritten, da die Standards, wann ein Staat als sicher betrachtet wird, hoch sind. Die Türkei erfüllt diese Bedingungen nicht. PRO ASYL befürchtet, dass Zurückschiebungen an den EU-Grenzen nun dadurch drastisch erleichtert werden sollen, weil die bisherigen verbindlichen Kriterien, wann ein dritter Staat sicher ist, nun drastisch gesenkt werden. Die Durchreise durch einen Staat wie die Türkei soll bereits genügen, sodass dieser Staat als sicher gilt, selbst wenn er die GFK nicht ratifiziert hat sondern nur den sogenannten »ausreichenden Schutz« bietet. (Art 45 Abs 3a, Asylverfahrensverordnungsentwurf aus 2016). Diese drastische Rechtsverschärfung geht einher mit einer bis zu 24-wöchigen de-facto-Inhaftierung an der EU-Grenze. Hinzu kommt, dass es gegen ablehnende Entscheidungen nur eine Rechtsmittelinstanz gibt (Art 53 Abs 9 Entwurf der Asylverfahrensverordnung, Änderungsvorschlag der EU-Kommission vom 23. Diese Abschiebung muss innerhalb von acht Monaten erfolgen. Gelingt das nicht, muss das Land sie selbst aufnehmen. (…) Auch an der Grenze sollen sich die Verfahren ändern. Bevor ein Migrant ins Land kommt, soll der betroffene Staat die Personen deutlich umfangreicher als bisher überprüfen. Der Migrant soll registriert und Fingerabdrücke genommen werden, zudem muss er sich Gesundheits- und Sicherheitschecks unterziehen. Kommt der Asylbewerber aus einem Land mit geringerer Anerkennungsrate – Tunesien oder Marokko etwa – soll innerhalb von zwölf Wochen ein solches Grenzverfahren durchgeführt werden. Dies soll sowohl Schmuggler als auch die Menschen selbst abschrecken, sich auf den Weg nach Europa zu machen. Gelingt das Verfahren nicht innerhalb von zwölf Wochen, müsste ein normales Asylverfahren durchgeführt werden. (…) Zudem hält die EU-Kommission an den derzeit gültigen Dublin-Regeln grundsätzlich fest, was eine Einigung zusätzlich erschweren dürfte. Die Dublin-Regeln sehen vor, dass meist jener EU-Staat für einen Asylantrag zuständig ist, auf dessen Boden der Schutzsuchende zuerst europäischen Boden betreten hat. Dieser Mechanismus belastet vor allem Länder an den südlichen EU-Außengrenzen wie Griechenland oder Italien. Sie fordern schon lange mehr Unterstützung und eine verpflichtende Verteilung der Migranten auf die anderen Länder. Auf der anderen Seite lehnen Staaten wie Österreich, Ungarn, Tschechien und Polen eine verpflichtende Aufnahme kategorisch ab.“

 

Beitrag vom 23. September 2020 bei tageschau.de

 




Flüchtlingspolitik: EU will Asyl-Schnellverfahren an den Außengrenzen




„… Neue Verteilmechanismen, neue, schnellere Grenzverfahren und ein deutlich stärkerer Fokus auf das Ziel, Menschen ohne Bleibeperspektive schnell wieder abzuschieben: So lassen sich die Vorschläge zu einer Neuregelung der EU-Asylpolitik zusammenfassen, die die EU-Kommission an diesem Mittag in Brüssel präsentiert hat. (…) Besonders heikel ist bei solchen Grenzverfahren stets die Frage, ob die Ankommenden in dieser Phase in offenen oder in geschlossenen Unterkünften untergebracht werden. „Wir schlagen keinen Arrest vor“, sagt Kommissarin Johansson. Er sei aber auch nicht verboten, sondern in bestimmten Fällen denkbar, etwa bei Sicherheitsrisiken oder der Gefahr, dass sich die Migranten dem Verfahren entziehen könnten – was faktisch recht häufig der Fall sein dürfte, zumal dann, wenn die Menschen anderenfalls einer Abschiebung entgegensehen. (…) Den Plänen der EU-Kommission zufolge soll ausnahmslos jeder Mitgliedstaat verpflichtet sein, an diesem System mitzuwirken – allerdings nicht zwingend dadurch, dass er selbst einige der Menschen übernimmt, um Staaten wie Griechenland, Malta oder Italien so zu entlasten. In der Vergangenheit hatte gerade dieser Punkt stets für Streit gesorgt. Stattdessen können die Mitgliedstaaten sich beispielsweise auch dadurch solidarisch zeigen, dass sie dabei helfen, Abschiebungen zu organisieren, oder die Grenzstaaten auf andere Weise unterstützen. (…) Auch den umstrittenen „Pushbacks“ will die EU-Kommission einen Riegel vorschieben, bei denen Menschen illegal und oft mit Gewalt zurück über die EU-Außengrenze gedrängt werden, damit sie gar nicht erst einen Asylantrag stellen können. Gemeinsam mit der europäischen Grundrechteagentur will Kommissarin Johansson ein besseres System installieren, um solche Fälle zu überwachen. Bisher habe die EU-Kommission keine eigenen Möglichkeiten, solche Fälle zu überprüfen. Der neue Mechanismus solle der Behörde in dieser Frage „schärfere Waffen“ an die Hand geben, so Johansson…“

 

Beitrag von Karoline Meta Beisel vom 23. September 2020 bei der Süddeutschen Zeitung online

 







Anm.: Wesentlich ist das Zugeständnis an bestimmte EU-Mitglieder vom Art. 78 AEUV und Art. 18 GRCh abweichen zu dürfen, obwohl rechtlich eigentlich bindend. Beteiligung an Abschiebungen ist noch keine Beteiligung an den Verpflichtungen nach dem EU-Asylrecht. Es wäre ein erster Schritt punktuell das Asylrecht zu beseitigen und ein Entgegenkommen an rassistische Einstellungen.










Teuflischer Pakt der Entrechtung – PRO ASYL warnt vor dem von der EU-Kommission vorgestellten EU-Pakt und fordert das EU-Parlament auf, Rechtsstaat und Asylrecht zu verteidigen




„»Dies ist ein teuflischer Pakt der Entrechtung. Von Rechtspopulisten getrieben verrät die EU-Kommission das Asylrecht und die Menschenrechte von Schutzsuchenden«, reagiert Günter Burkhardt, Geschäftsführer von PRO ASYL. »Wir fordern das EU-Parlament auf, Rechtsstaat und Menschenrechte zu verteidigen und diesen Pakt abzulehnen. Die EU-Kommission ist dabei, die Grundlagen der Europäischen Union, die Menschenrechte, zu verraten. Eine Einigung der EU-Länder auf Kosten der Schutzsuchenden darf es nicht geben«. (…) Es sollen möglichst Viele von der Grenze aus sofort zurückgeschickt werden. Faire Asylverfahren wird es in Massenlagern an der Grenze aber nicht geben. Es findet keine umfassende, individuelle Prüfung der Fluchtgründe statt. »Entweder gibt es Hauruckverfahren im Eiltempo oder die Menschen sitzen lange in einem Zustand der Perspektivlosigkeit fest«, kritisiert Burkhardt. Der Pakt droht somit, den Rechtsstaat an den Außengrenzen abzuschaffen. In Lagern unter freiheitsbeschränkenden Lagerbedingungen – wie u.a. von der griechischen Regierung geplant – ist kein effektiver Rechtsschutz möglich, die gerechte Würdigung des Einzelfalls bleibt auf der Strecke. Die nun bekannt gewordenen »Abschiebepatenschaften« durch andere nichtaufnahmewillige EU-Staaten, sind für Schutzsuchende bedrohlich. Die neue europäische Solidarität heißt, sich darin einig zu sein, Menschen abzuschieben.“

 

Erste Reaktion von PRO ASYL zum New Pact on Migration and Asylum vom 23. September 2020

 







Siehe auch #MigrationPact




Wir erinnern an unser Dossier: 

“Menschenfeindlicher Unsinn”: Seehofer will „Erstprüfung“ von Asylanträgen an EU-Außengrenzen










“Dublin abschaffen” – aber wie?  


„

Die EU-Kommission legt mit monatelanger Verspätung ihren Vorschlag zur Asylreform vor, Ratspräsident Michel sagt aus dubiosen Gründen den Türkei-Gipfel ab – und der deutsche EU-Vorsitz kriegt das Chaos bei den Reisewarnungen nicht in den Griff: Die Watchlist EUropa vom 23. September 2020. Moria brennt – die EU pennt? Diesen Vorwurf will Kommissionschefin von der Leyen nicht auf sich sitzen lassen. Sie hat die seit Monaten überfällige Reform des gemeinsamen Asylrechts zur Chefsache gemacht und angekündigt, die umstrittene Dublin-Verordnung zu streichen. Am Mittwoch soll der Vorschlag kommen. Wir werden die Dublin-Verordnung abschaffen”, kündigte von der Leyen vor einer Woche vor dem Europaparlament an. “Wir werden es durch ein neues europäisches System zur Migrationssteuerung ersetzen.” Dieses neue System werde “gemeinsame Strukturen zu Asyl und Rückführen” haben und “einen neuen starken Solidaritätsmechanismus” beinhalten. (…) Die Grundzüge hat Migrationskommissar Schinas aber bereits bei einem Besuch in Berlin ausgeplaudert. Demnach soll das neue System auf drei Säulen oder Etagen ruhen. Die Basis sollen Abkommen mit Drittstaaten wie der Türkei bilden. Die Herkunfts- und Transitländer sollen dafür sorgen, dass weniger Flüchtlinge in die EU kommen. Der umstrittene Türkei-Deal, den Kanzlerin Angela Merkel 2016 mit dem türkischen Präsidenten Recep Erdogan ausgearbeitet hatte, dient dabei offenbar als Vorbild. Er sieht vor, dass die Türkei gegen Milliardenhilfen die Grenzen zur EU abriegelt und Flüchtlinge zurücknimmt. Auf der zweiten Etage soll ein „robuster Außengrenzenschutz“ entstehen. Er wird die Festung Europa nochmals verstärken. Erst danach, auf der dritten und wohl letzten Ebene, soll ein System europäischer Solidarität entstehen. Es dürfte allerdings kaum über das Prinzip hinausgehen, dass alle EU-Staaten irgendwie helfen müssen

…“ 

Beitrag von Eric Bonse auf LostInEU

 




Kritik an deutscher Linie für EU-Asylreform  


„

Menschenrechtsorganisationen kritisieren die Reformpläne der Bundesregierung, Asylverfahren in Zukunft an die EU-Außengrenzen zu verlegen. Menschenrechtskommissarin des Europarates wirft EU-Staaten vor, den Flüchtlingsschutz zu umgehen. Die Linie der Bundesregierung zur Reform der EU-Asylpolitik stößt auf Kritik aus der Zivilgesellschaft. Schutzsuchende schon vor der förmlichen Einreise an den EU-Grenzen einem Verfahren zu unterziehen bedeute „Haftlager“, sagte der Geschäftsführer von Pro Asyl, Günter Burkhardt, am Dienstag in Berlin. Schnelle Verfahren für Tausende von Menschen bedeuteten zugleich, dass die Frage der Sicherheit der Menschen in einem Drittland gar nicht mehr geprüft werde, warnte Burkhardt beim 20. Berliner Symposium zum Flüchtlingsschutz der Evangelischen Akademie zu Berlin

…“ 

Meldung vom 24.06.2020 beim Migazin

 

 (im Abo)







Der Beitrag 

Migrationspakt und GEAS: Neuer Anlauf in der EU-Flüchtlingspolitik (???)

 erschien zuerst auf 

LabourNet Germany

author: Unknown
title: Ji bo Halk TVyê qeyûm hat tayînkirin  | Rêxistinên çapemeniyê bertek nîşan dan: “Em vê zordariyê qebûl nakin”
content:
Polîsan îro (14ê Cotmehê) di saetên sibehê de bi ser avahiya navendî ya Halk TVyê ya li Stenbolê de girt. 

Qeyûm

 ji bo kanalê hat tayînkirin, weşana televizyonê hat rawestandin.




Bernamegerê Halk TVyê Deniz Bayramoğlu di saet 05.15an de li ser hesabê xwe yê medyaya civakî daxuyaniyek da û got: “Ji bo Halk TVyê qeyûm hat tayînkirin. Tîmên Şubeya Darayî, KOM û TEMê li kanalê lêgerînê dikin.” 



















Polîsan bi ser Halk TVyê de girtin: Qeyûm hat tayînkirin û weşan hat rawestandin




14 Cotmeh 2026










Li ser hesabê medyaya civakî ê Halk TVyê  jî hatibû ragihandin ku qeyûm ji bo kanalê hatî tayînkirin û weşan hatine rawestandin.







Di çarçoveya lêpirsîna ji bo Halk TVyê de, 17 kesên ku biryara desteserkirina wan hatiye dayîn, ev in: 




Hasan Ozdemir, İbrahim Ozdemir, Armagan Kuçuk, Mustafa Ozdemir, Halit Akın, Ali Turan, Mediha Burumoglu, Murat Koçak, Erkan Yagci û Suleyman Ozen.




Her weha Cafer Mahiroglu, Hakan Arican, Mehmet Necati Yagci û Sevim Kul ên ku biryara desteserkirinê ji bo wan heye, li dervayî welat in.







Rêxistinên pîşeyî yên çapemeniyê bertek nîşanî tayînkirina qeyûm a ji bo kanalê dan.




“Çapemenî azad e, nayê sansûrkirin”




Sendikaya Rojnamegerên Tirkiyeyê (TGS) li hesabê xwe yê Xê daxuyanî da û weha got: 







“Ji bo Halk TVyê qeyûm hat tayînkirin! Desthilatdariya siyasî di salên dawî de ji bo derbasbûna her pirsgirêkê vê bêhiqûqiyê bi kar tîne û îro careke din ev bêhiqûqî li dijî azadiya çapemeniyê bikaranî. Bi biryareke kêfî serê sibehê ji aliyê polîsan ve bi ser Halk TVyê de hat girtin, mudaxele li weşanê hat kirin. Em vê zordariyê qebûl nakin! Çapemenî azad e, nayê sansûrkirin!”







“Ewlehiya hiqûqî ya medyayê nemaye”




DISK Basin-İşê jî bertek nîşanî tayînkirina qeyûm da. Daxuyaniya wan weha ye: 







“Tayînkirina qeyûm a ji bo Halk TVyê û rawestandina weşanê nayê qebûlkirin ku rasterast azadiya çapemeniyê û mafê agahîgirtina gel hedef digire. Sala borî li hemberî TELE1ê ev yek pêkanîn û îro li Halk TVyê tê dubarekirin. Ev yek nîşan dide ku li Tirkiyeyê ti ewlehiya hiqûqî ya medyayê nemaye. Ev biryar tenê bi rawestandina weşanê re sînordar nemaye; ji metbexê heta ber ekranê xuhdan, kar û paşeroja bi sedan kedkarên çapemeniyê jî rasterast hedef girtiye. Em li cem bi sedan hevalên xwe yên pîşeyî û kedkarên Halk TVyê ne. Em hemû raya giştî vedixwînin ku xwedî li azadiya çapemeniyê, mafê agahîgirtina gel û keda hevalên me yên pîşeyî derkevin.”







“Darbeyeke giran e li dijî azadiya derbirînê”




Komeleya Rojnamegerên Hevdem (ÇGD) di daxuyaniya xwe de wiha got: 







“Tayînkirina qeyûm a ji bo Halk TVyê û rawestandina weşana wê, mudaxeleyeke giran e li dijî azadiya çapemeniyê û derbirînê. Ev biryar nayê qebûlkirin ku mafên destûrî û azadiya agahîgirtina gel dike armanc. Tam salek berê qeyûm ji bo TELE1ê hatibû tayînkirin û wekî lekeyeke reş ketibû dîroka çapemeniya me. Îro jî ev biryar li hemberî Halk TVyê hat pêkanîn. Careke din diyar bû ku li Tirkiyeyê ewlehiya weşanê ya ti saziyeke çapemeniyê nîne. Em li cem xebatkarên Halk TVyê û hevalên xwe yên pîşeyî ne. Em ê ji bo demokrasiyê, çapemeniya azad û mafê agahîstandina gel têkoşîna xwe berdewam bikin. Em hemû raya giştî vedixwînin ku xwedî li demokrasiyê, çapemeniya azad û mafê agahîstandina gel derkevin!”







“Mafê agahîgirtina gel nayê astengkirin”




Komeleya Rojnamegeran a Dîcle Fıratê (DFG) jî daxuyaniyeke nivîskî weşand. Daxuyaniya DFGyê wiha ye:







 “Qeyûm derbe ye li dijî azadiya çapemeniyê. Tayînkirina qeyûm a ji bo Halk TVyê, rawestandina weşanên kanalê û ketina tîmên polîsan a avahiya li Stenbolê, ji aliyê azadiya çapemeniyê û mafê agahîgirtina gel ve metirsiyeke cidî çêdike. Piştî zextên li ser rojnamegeriyê, astengiyên gihîştinê, desteserkirin û girtinan niha jî mudaxelekirina li ser rêveberiya kanala televizyonê û rawestandina weşanên wê, tê wateya ku kontrola li ser çapemeniyê hîn girantir bibe. Pêkanînên qeyûm û biryarên rawestandina weşanê yên li hemberî saziyên medyayê, tenê rojnamegeran hedef nagirin, di heman demê de mafê agahîgirtina civakê jî hedef digirin. Em wekî DFG diyar dikin ku em bi xebatkarên Halk TVyê û hemû rojnamegerên ku azadiya çapemeniyê diparêzin re di nava hevgirtinê de ne. Em ê li hemberî mudaxeleyên li dijî azadiya çapemeniyê û mafê agahîgirtina gel têkoşîna xwe berdewam bikin.”







(FY/AY)

title: maybe once the hysteria dies down we could start getting some interesting research into exactly why…
content:
maybe once the hysteria dies down we could start getting some interesting research into exactly why so many people are using AI tools for ‘basic tasks’ now. is it because this many people struggled to keep up with these things before and have only just now been given the tools they need to keep up with their peers? is it that modern demands have increased so much that this level of automation becomes a requirement across the board to keep up with demand increases (and possibly be used as an excuse to increase demand even more)? a combination? something else? maybe people just have a tendency towards being curious about weird new toys? [puts a hand up to the bluetooth in my ear] oh sorry I just got word that the real reason is “modern humans are lazy and stupid NPCs causing the degeneration of society, and we should start bullying each other to get back in line” ohhh ok got it. I’m sure that’s a stable and moral worldview to hold.

Also these tools are designed to constantly tease us into using more of them in the same way social media is designed to keep us scrolling deep into the night. Tools people used before are deliberately being shittified to make AI the more attractive option. Exhausted, overburdened humans versus every trick these tool-designers can throw at them. Focusing on the users is a really weird priority.

Finally someone said it. Your aunt generating minion memes on Facebook is not the fucking enemy. I’m so tired of people arguing against personal usage of AI under the idea that “new technology bad” – the issue was never about new tech, it’s about the billionaires orchestrating a techno-fascist future and destroying the environment in the process. A lot of “leftists” online would rather eat each other alive than to coalition build against a common enemy. Sorry dog, you’re gonna have to work hand-in-hand with people who write work emails with AI. It shouldn’t be a surprise that in one of the most overworked countries in the world (US) people have turned to using AI to automate tasks. There is no ethical consumption under capitalism. You literally buy slave labor products constantly.

author: Reem Aljeally
title: Class, Creativity, and Cultural Production in Africa
content:
Artistic freedom and expression has long been shaped and constrained by many factors, including power, economic hierarchies, and class. In Africa, the right to create and distribute art without censorship has always been a contested terrain. Artists’ realities in the African region are directly influenced by both their geographical and societal positions; class plays a big role in how the art world runs. What does society consider as art?  Who gets to buy, collect, or even witness art?  Who has access to exhibition spaces or international residencies? These questions are not abstract; they define the careers of many artists, including my own.




Since 2011, we have seen youth-led movements harness creativity as a tool for political resistance, from the Arab Spring uprisings to #FeesMustFall in South Africa, #EndSARS in Nigeria, and, most recently, Kenya’s Gen Z protests. In Sudan, where I was born and raised, the December Revolution was marked not only by chants in the streets but also by murals, poems, songs, and performances that transformed the cityscape into a living archive of resistance. Yet, even within such moments of collective creativity, class distinctions determined who could participate, whose voices were amplified, and whose remained unheard.




In this article, I reflect on how class shapes artistic and cultural production in Africa: how it has defined access to creativity, how it limits cultural consumption, and what mechanisms – grassroots, digital, and transnational – have begun to narrow these divides. My reflections are grounded in personal experience as an artist and curator working between Khartoum and Cairo, as the founder of The Muse multi-studios and the Sudan Art Archive, and as a participant in regional and international networks of cultural production.




Social hierarchy and access to creativity




In Khartoum, where I first studied architecture before turning to painting and curation, access to art education was already limited to two art schools at the Sudan University for Science and Technology and the newly founded Art programme at the Al-Nileen University. Access to these institutions was competitive, and while not restricted in principle, in practice it was shaped by social status and community expectations. Families in Sudan often encouraged more “practical” fields like engineering, medicine, or architecture – disciplines seen as more secure.




Many young Sudanese who aspired to become artists may have had their educational background shaped by these community views, yet it has not stopped them from pursuing a career in the field upon completing their studies. Those who came from upper-class families had a better chance of accessing educational institutions abroad, while the majority were funnelled into informal workshops or self-taught practices because institutions were either non-existent or insufficiently resourced.




German curator and researcher Larissa-Diana Fuhrmann observes that the development of art education in Sudan has been deeply influenced by colonial legacies. Institutions such as the College of Fine and Applied Arts in Khartoum (originally established under British colonial rule) implemented curricula modelled on Western art academies. These frameworks introduced formalist, Eurocentric paradigms that continue to shape artistic discourse, pedagogy, and aesthetic hierarchies in the postcolonial context.




Access to these institutions, and to international art education more broadly, has historically been mediated by class intersecting with gender and racial categories. During both the late colonial and early post-independence periods, educational and cultural policies enabled a small elite (predominantly from Khartoum’s middle- and upper-class families) to study abroad. Upon their return, these artists occupied influential positions in Sudan’s cultural institutions and helped define national artistic narratives. As Fuhrmann notes, the stratification becomes evident when examining how some of these artists categorize work produced outside formal institutions or urban centres as “folkloric”, thereby reinforcing classed and spatial distinctions in cultural valuation.




This dynamic illustrates the broader relationship between class, cultural capital, and aesthetic authority. Artists with international training and transnational visibility have historically been more likely to receive institutional recognition and access to resources such as galleries, collectors, and critical discourse. By contrast, locally trained artists without such networks often remain marginalized. As Fuhrmann suggests, this pattern is not unique to Sudan but reflects global inequalities in the circulation and validation of artistic production.




The relationship between social class and education is critical here. Education may open doors, but class determines whether those doors can truly be walked through. In Khartoum, access to art schools was less of an issue than what came after: exhibition spaces, residencies, opportunities to travel, and access to international networks. These post-education opportunities were overwhelmingly skewed toward those with means – financial, linguistic, or social. Khartoum’s art scene has been dominated by foreign institutions and their cultural centres, the activities of embassies and supported programmes that have shaped narratives around certain artists and their work. A young artist with fluent English, for instance, could navigate these circles and be able to manage applications for grants or residencies abroad, while others were excluded by language barriers before their talent was even considered.




Class and collecting art




If class determines who creates art, it also shapes who consumes it. In Khartoum, the culture of collecting is limited, and where it exists, it is often restricted to a narrow elite or international buyers; exhibitions are often attended by the same small circle of artists, academics, and diplomats. Public engagement with art was limited, not because of lack of interest but because of structural barriers: galleries were concentrated in certain neighbourhoods, often inaccessible to working-class communities. 




In Cairo, a more developed art market exists, but even there, collecting tends to be restricted to a certain kind of social status and even to certain artists in some cases – those already exhibiting internationally, or those whose work aligns with global trends and higher-ranked individuals or institutions. This means that while art education might be accessible, sustaining a career as an artist is still determined by class, by whether one can find patrons, collectors, or institutions willing to invest.




In his work “Funny Effects 1”, young Egyptian artist Omar Gabr addresses this class-controlled environment of art collecting in Cairo. Having entered the art scene at just 19, he uses sarcasm to depict the unease of navigating collectors and audiences from upper-class circles, subtly exposing the divide between young creators and elite consumers.




Omar Gabr, Funny Effect 1 – Oil on Canvas, 182 x 342 cm, 2019-2020




Despite these elite-driven strictures, informal cultural practices continue to thrive across African cities, offering alternative spaces for creativity that resist class-based gatekeeping. During Sudan’s revolution, walls became canvases, songs were shared freely, and poetry circulated on the streets. These practices challenged the monopoly of elite cultural production, demonstrating how art can thrive in public spaces even without institutional support. Yet they were also vulnerable to erasure: murals were painted over by authorities, performers were harassed, and documentation was often absent. This precarity underscores how fragile artistic freedom remains when it relies solely on informal networks.




Young Kenyan independent curator Thaddeus Wamukoya (Tewa) reflects a shared experience of how status, money, power, and political positions affect the art market. When Tewa is asked why he usually hosts his exhibitions at The Village Market, one of Nairobi’s high-end malls, he says it gives him easier access to potential clients and collectors, adding that, unfortunate as it is, we have to acknowledge that status and class determine how art is circulated. Referrals and word of mouth are also of high value in Kenya’s market: “The culture of having someone refer you can guarantee easy work. People often consume average things – and art – because they saw someone else do it,” says Tewa. 




It is important to note that class rarely operates in isolation; it intersects with gender and race in ways that reshape cultural hierarchies. The latter further complicates Kenya’s scene: a market dominated by white gallery owners privileges buyers and tourists, who often access information about artists and their artworks more easily than local Black Kenyans. The “white cube” model is a foreign concept to Africa, introduced by the West and structured to gatekeep, introducing classism to the market, leaving local models of studios, collectives, and initiatives to struggle in a system that does not serve them. Across the continent, similar dynamics play out with local variations.




A Contemporary Art Affair: Emerging African Voices Exhibition, TewasArtGallery, 2025




In many African countries, Western women with backgrounds in the aid industry channel their capital into the art market. Their influence extends beyond gallery ownership to social networks, including exclusive networks and events. Here, class and race become the driving forces of access and authority, even in a space where gender, in another context, might have limited such visibility. This stands in contrast with Sudan, where, historically, male artists from Khartoum’s upper and middle classes have held privileged access to recognition and resources, while voices from marginalized regions, such as the Nuba Mountains or Darfur, have been systematically excluded. The picture is therefore uneven: in one context, class intersects with race to privilege white women, while in another, class intersects with gender to privilege men. Both reveal how deeply entrenched systems of power shape who becomes visible in the art world.




New models, new ages




Despite these challenges, mechanisms have emerged to counter the impact of class on cultural production. Tewa’s model of operating has been heavily reliant on the Internet and Instagram as a platform that has been transformative. Social media allows artists to bypass traditional gatekeepers, share work directly with audiences, and build transnational communities. It has enabled artists who lack institutional support or access to collectors to create visibility, mobilize solidarity, and even sell works directly. In contexts where state repression or elite capture of the art market is strong, these digital tools have opened spaces for alternative forms of recognition.




At the same time, the digital sphere reproduces its own hierarchies. Algorithms reward certain aesthetics that align with global trends, while artists without access to high-quality documentation or steady internet remain at a disadvantage. Visibility can be purchased through sponsored posts, and those with greater resources – better studios, professional photography, fluent English captions – still hold an edge. The very same platforms that dismantle some barriers end up constructing new ones.




Alongside social media, we see the rise of collectives, pop-up exhibitions, and community-driven archives that challenge the dominance of the white cube. In Sudan and Egypt, grassroots initiatives have reimagined cultural infrastructure through shared studios, neighbourhood art projects, and self-organized residencies. These models rely on networks of trust and reciprocity rather than on class-based patronage. They also produce new forms of value: visibility in the public space, belonging in community, and solidarity across borders. What these examples suggest is not the disappearance of class, but a reconfiguration of how it operates. Digital and grassroots models do not erase inequality, but they redistribute visibility, shifting the power of who speaks and who is heard. They carve out spaces where young, marginalized, or self-taught artists can assert their presence without waiting for institutional approval.




Class remains one of the most enduring obstacles to artistic freedom in Africa. It shapes who becomes an artist, who sustains a career, and who consumes culture. It also influences whose stories enter the record and whose remain untold. Yet class is not an insurmountable barrier; it is a terrain of struggle, negotiation, and reimagination. The future of creativity in Africa depends on inclusivity, on breaking down class divides to empower diverse voices. When artists from all backgrounds can create, share, and sustain their work – whether through digital platforms, collectives, or reimagined public spaces – cultural production becomes not just an elite pursuit but a collective force for transformation. Only then will artistic freedom truly embody its promise as a cornerstone of democracy and human rights.




The post 

Class, Creativity, and Cultural Production in Africa

 first appeared on 

The Elephant

.

author: Trojka
title: Nasze Ulice, Wasze Granice – relacja z demonstracji z rozbrat.org
content:
W sobotę 3 października odbyła się w Toruniu demonstracja pod hasłem – Nasze Ulice, Wasze Granice. Była ona częścią kampanii organizowanej wspólnie przez Federację Anarchistyczną i kolektyw 161 Crew i stanowiła wyraz sprzeciwu wobec rasistowskiej i ksenofobicznej polityce granicznej. W proteście brały udział m.in osoby związane z poznańskim środowiskiem anarchistycznym – Rozbratem, Sambą Hałastrą, Federacją Anarchistyczną Czarny Region. Organizatorem była Toruńska Grupa Anarchistyczna. 




Protest rozpoczął się o godzinie 15:00 pod pomnikiem Mikołaja Kopernika na toruńskim rynku. Początkowo demonstrację próbowała zakłócić grupka neofaszystów, chroniąca się za transparentem “Defend Europe” i przekreślonym symbolem trzech strzałek, symbolem jednoznacznie antyfaszystowskim. Od utraty owego transparentu neofaszystów uchroniła interwencja policji, która osłoniła tę kuriozalną kontrmanifestację. Obecność neofaszystów na toruńskim rynku jedynie unaoczniła, do czego prowadzi ignorancja oraz wzmacniająca się rasistowska retoryka stosowana nie tylko przez polityków skrajnej prawicy, ale również rządzącej koalicji. Podkreślano to w przemówieniu rozpoczynającym demonstrację. Z okrzykami “Żaden człowiek nie jest nielegalny” i “Każdy inny wszyscy równi” demonstracja ruszyła z rynku wyznaczoną trasą, bez dalszych incydentów.







Idąc ulicami miasta, przy akompaniamencie samby wznoszono hasła “Solidarność naszą bronią”, “Bez granic, bez nacji, stop deportacji” “Naszą ojczyzną jest człowieczeństwo”. W krótkich postojach na trasie protestu kolejne osoby podkreślały jego cel. Mówiono między innymi o wykorzystywaniu migrantów jako taniej siły roboczej, których prawa pracownicze są stale łamane, a w zasadzie nie obowiązują. Wyzysk ekonomiczny idzie w parz ze zwykłym rasizmem, a jednocześnie sama obecność migrantów jest wykorzystywana do dyscyplinowania pozostałych pracowników i nastawiania ich przeciwko przyjezdnym. Odciąga to uwagę od rzeczywistego przeciwnika, jakim są wyzyskujący obie strony pracodawcy. To z nimi jako zjednoczeni pracownicy powinno się toczyć spór i walczyć o poprawę warunków pracy, a nie naiwnie wierzyć w ksenofobiczną propagandę, która z migrantów robi wrogów i “najeźdźców”




Pod siedzibą redakcji jednego z lokalnych mediów podkreślono rolę propagandy w budowaniu atmosfery strachu przed obcymi. Pseudodziennikarskie portale walcząc o klikalność, z łatwością posługują się językiem mającym jedynie podsycać nienawiść, wzmacniać stereotypy i grać na emocjach. Konsekwencję takiej propagandy odczuwają przedstawiciele narodowych i etnicznych mniejszości. Mocnym tego wyrazem była przemowa jednego z uczestników protestu – pochodzenia arabskiego. Jak sam wspominał, choć urodził się w Polsce, jego kolor skóry od zawsze narażał go na rasistowskie ataki. Musiał słuchać najgorszych obelg; często od neofaszystów, którzy bez żenady eksponowali na swoim ciele symbole swojej ideologii.Jednak to on miał się kryć i unikać wrogich spojrzeń ludzi, tylko z uwagi na ilość pigmentu zawartego w skórze. Dodatkowo jego rodzina wielokrotnie była nękana przez przedstawicieli państwowych służb. Kraj pochodzenia rodziców czy ich kontakty z bliskimi, tylko z uwagi na wyznawaną religię i, nie oszukujmy, się – rasizm i islamofobię – powodowały telefony z policji, przesłuchania i rozpytywania. Tak wygląda rzeczywistość osób, których kolor skóry naraża na bycie łatwą ofiarą różnego typu nacjonalistów i szowinistów. Dlatego tak ważna jest międzyludzka solidarność i reagowanie na wszelkie przejawy dyskryminacji i rasizmu.




Na zakończenie protestu podkreślono również powody migracji, do których oprócz konfliktów zbrojnych należą także zmiany klimatyczne. A te można dostrzec nawet po poziomie wody w przepływającej przez Toruń Wiśle. Nie mamy pewności czy, jak to nie raz było w historii, tym razem nie z uwagi na konflikt zbrojny czy sytuację ekonomiczną, ale właśnie zmiany klimatyczne, mieszkańcy Polski nie będą zmuszeni do masowej migracji. Czy dopiero wówczas zrozumiemy, czym jest ksenofobia i rasizm, zjawiska, które teraz pozwalamy utrwalać, kiedy odczujemy ich działanie na własnej skórze? Dlatego zaapelowano o działania nie tylko w ramach demonstracji, ale w codziennym życiu i własnym lokalnym środowisku. Obojętność na rządową politykę graniczną, narastający język pełen pogardy dla przedstawicieli mniejszości, cyniczne granie na narodowych resentymentach i fobiach, to wszystko dzieje się tylko z uwagi na nasz zbyt cichy sprzeciw. Kampania i wieńcząca ją demonstracja nie mogą być naszym jedynym głosem sprzeciwu, a winny być tylko jednym z elementów codziennej walki z rasizmem i ksenofobią. Apelujemy więc o kolejne WSPÓLNE protesty, demonstracje, akcje bezpośrednie i opór.







Nasze Ulice Wasze Granice




Równe prawa dla wszystkich 




Swoboda przemieszczania się




Artykuł 

Nasze Ulice, Wasze Granice – relacja z demonstracji z rozbrat.org

FEDERACJA ANARCHISTYCZNA - wolność, równość, pomoc wzajemna

.

author: Michael Beltran
title: America’s AI ambitions threaten Indigenous lands in the Philippines
content:
This is an original story by 

Mongabay

 republished through the Indigenous News Alliance.




Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. arrived at the Grand Hyatt Manila on Sept. 10 to address hundreds of foreign business representatives assembled for the Luzon Economic Corridor investors’ forum.




Outside the hotel, hundreds of demonstrators had also gathered, carrying signs that read “No to Pax Silica!” The scene reflected both the government’s ambitious plans to ride the artificial intelligence wave and deep ambivalence in civil society.




Police confronted the crowd, shoving them with riot shields and batons on the street outside the hotel lobby. Activists say police injured at least 27 protesters and arrested five. Police, meanwhile, reported minor cuts and injuries to 16 personnel. 




Protester Jona Yang, from the activist-scientist group AGHAM, said she was negotiating with the police to cool tensions when they arrested her. “We want the Marcos government and investors to see the outrage all of this has caused,” Yang told Mongabay. “They’re taking away our resources and our lands.”




The Luzon Economic Corridor, or LEC, is an economic initiative focused on the Philippines’ biggest island, begun in 2024. Pax Silica, the U.S.-led global pact to build an AI and semiconductor supply chain that is not reliant on China, includes the LEC. In April, Washington and Manila announced plans to 

build a 4,000-acre high-tech manufacturing hub

 in the Central Luzon region.




Pax Silica has become a lightning rod for political and environmental contentions. The government maintains it’s a boon for the Philippine economy. But opponents of the project, including Indigenous and local communities living on the land designated for the project, say it’s an international land and resource grab in the name of U.S. AI ambitions.




U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visited Manila in July to affirm bilateral commitment to the project, with a final agreement slated for signing in November.




At the LEC forum, Pax Silica was discussed behind closed doors, and officials gave few details about its future. Angela Ignacio, an undersecretary at the Philippine Department of Finance, told reporters it would be premature to share any details on Pax Silica before plans are finalized. But she did call it a chance for the Philippines to become a “global player when it comes to technologies that will shape the future.”




Heather Variava, senior adviser to the U.S. State Department’s Bureau of Economic, Energy, and Business Affairs, added that “the goal of the U.S. is always to be an additive, to bring more power, to bring water, to bring more benefits to the Philippines.”




The Pax Silica hub will be built within 

New Clark City

, a government-planned “smart” city inside the greater 79,000-acre Clark area, a former U.S. military complex. Clark is titled and managed by the Bases Conversion and Development Authority, or BCDA, an office under the supervision of the president. At a press briefing, development authority chief Joshua Bingcang shared a “conservative” estimate that the facility would need around 3 gigawatts of energy to run. He also said that it would be green and mainly solar powered.




“We are blessed with 300 days of sunshine,” Bingcang added.




Running consistently, the Pax Silica facility would demand about 26.3 terawatt-hours each year; by contrast, the Philippines’ entire service sector consumed about 

28 TWh

 in 2024.




Giovanni Tapang, former dean at the University of the Philippines’ College of Science and a convenor of the Network Opposed (NO) to Pax Silica, told Mongabay that the Philippines has the “most to lose” among the 25 nations involved in the pact as it chains domestic resources to U.S. policies. “How many thousands of hectares will they be taking from farmers to build solar panels? And if we’re generating all this clean energy, why let the U.S. use it instead of local households?” Tapang said.




The development authority initially said that data centers could be part of the Pax Silica. But Bingcang and the 

president’s office later denied this

 in a September press briefing where he emphasized it would be a semiconductor facility.




A document shared at the LEC forum listed data centers as part of the planned infrastructure in New Clark City. It did not specify whether the data centers would be built inside the Pax Silica hub.




Bingcang said the Pax Silica hub would also consume about 16 million to 24 million gallons of water each day, sourced from rainwater via an impounding dam. “We can ramp it up to 300 million liters [79 million gallons] a day with the available technology,” he told reporters in Filipino.




Tapang voiced concerns about how the development authority’s plan would work during the Philippines’ dry season, which runs from December to May. “This is the same period where farmers need their water for irrigation,” he said.




The BCDA says it intends to house 

mineral processing

 technology as well. Thony Dizon of the advocacy group BAN Toxics said the government has yet to reveal anything about how it will manage the resulting waste. “How will the government ensure that after 30 years, we are not left with a contaminated environment and depleted natural resources?” Dizon said.




The United States’ history with Clark dates to a military base established in 1903, when the Philippines was under U.S. colonial rule. The base remained under U.S. military control until 1991, when Clark finally came under the control of the Philippine government 45 years after the country gained independence.




Long before that, 

historians argue

, the area was the ancestral territory of the Aetas, considered to be some of the earliest settlers on the archipelago.




The Pax Silica site, located within the 23,350-acre New Clark City, overlaps with the ancestral domain claims of thousands of Aetas. A survey of the land by Arnisson Andre Ortega, a professor at Syracuse University in the U.S. and a member of the geographer group Countermapping Ph, revealed that planned construction for 

Pax Silica would impede on the lands

 of at least three existing Aeta villages.




“There is no ancestral domain title in that area,” BCDA chief Bingcang said, denying that the project would displace anybody.




Gloria Capiz-Estabillo, 76, is one of the elders of the Aeta Hungey tribe. She said tribal members have already been told by the Bases Conversion and Development Authority to leave their land.
 

Michael Beltran for Mongabay.




Gloria Capiz-Estabillo, 76, an elder of the Aeta Hungey tribe, told Mongabay that the development authority has already begun informing Aetas that they need to leave the land. “They’re setting up right in the middle of our land. Where are we going to live? How about our crops? Where will they take us, just drop us in the ocean?” Estabillo told Mongabay in Filipino.




To gain land rights, Indigenous peoples must apply for what’s known as a certificate of ancestral domain title from the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples.




Aetas in Clark have been lobbying for a certificate since 1994, but have been beset by frequent delays as the impoverished communities struggle to complete the minimum requirements needed: a detailed area map, a population census, genealogy of at least five clans covering the past three generations, and elder testimonies.




Ortega said the process has lagged for decades under “Indigenous-unfriendly” red tape involving the Bases Conversion and Development Authority and the commission. “The absence of a formal title does not invalidate their claim to their ancestral lands; rather, it highlights a critical lack of government support,” Ortega told Mongabay.




By contrast, the Pax Silica hub is supported by the Investor’s Lease Act, signed by President Marcos Jr. in September, which allows foreign businesses to lease commercial and industrial lands for up to 99 years.




The second day of the LEC forum was held in New Clark City. The BCDA led a field visit for the hundreds of prospective businesses. Hundreds of protesters continued to hound them, joined by nearby Aeta communities.




“They’ll have to kill us to take us off this land,” Estabillo said.




This story was originally published by 

Grist

 with the headline 

America’s AI ambitions threaten Indigenous lands in the Philippines

 on Oct 14, 2026.

author: infolibre
title: “Αμετανόητοι οι κατηγορούμενοι”, ανταπόκριση του Γιάννη Μάγγου από τη δίκη των 6 βασανιστών του Βασίλη Μάγγου
content:
Με ανάρτηση του, ο Γιάννης Μάγγος σχολιάζει τις εξελίξεις στη δίκη των 6 ένστολων βασανιστών του γιού του Βασίλη Μάγγου, αναφέροντας πως οι κατηγορούμενοι ένστολοι παρουσιάζονται αμετανόητοι και προσφέυγουν σε συνεχή ψέματα και αντιφάσεις στις απολογίες τους.




Παρακάτω η ανάρτηση του Γιάννη Μάγγου:







ΑΜΕΤΑΝΟΗΤΟΙ ΟΙ ΚΑΤΗΓΟΡΟΥΜΕΝΟΙ










Ολοκληρώθηκαν στις 12.10.2026 οι απολογίες των έξι κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών, βασανιστών του Βασίλειου Μάγγου. Όσον αφορά για το συνολικό περιστατικό, παραδέχτηκαν ότι “έγινε σωρεία λαθών και παραλείψεων” για τα οποία ευθύνονται και οι ίδιοι. “Έπραξα λάθος” είπαν.




Κανένας τους όμως δεν ζήτησε συγγνώμη από εμάς τους γονείς του για την προσβλητική,




κακοποιητική και ανάρμοστη συμπεριφορά τους.




Είναι αδίστακτοι και αμετανόητοι.




-Στην ερώτηση για την κινητικότητά του, απάντησαν πως, όταν κατέβηκε από το αυτοκίνητο, περπάτησε κανονικά, ανέβηκε τις σκάλες και έφτασε στον πρώτο όροφο της Υ/Α Βόλου χωρίς δυσκολία.




*Ακριβώς! Επειδή τα πιο σφοδρά χτυπήματα και η πιο βάναυση συμπεριφορά επακολούθησαν κατόπιν μέσα στην Ασφάλεια.




-Και σε άλλη ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, πώς δικαιολογούνται τα έξι σπασμένα πλευρά και η θλάση στο ήπαρ, η απάντηση όλων των κατηγορούμενων ήταν ότι αυτοί μέσα στην Υ/Α δεν έκαναν τίποτα, ότι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος δεν είχε τίποτα, δεν παραπονέθηκε για τίποτα…




-Και γιατί ο Μάγγος δεν πονούσε μόνο κατά το διάστημα από 4 μέχρι 5 μ.μ. που τον είχαν στην Ασφάλεια;




– …..




*Οι μάρτυρες που τον βρήκαν κατέθεσαν ότι πονούσε φρικτά και δεν μπορούσε να σηκωθεί να περπατήσει. Όλα αυτά επιβεβαιώθηκαν από τις καταθέσεις των γιατρών και την αξονική τομογραφία.




-Και γιατί δεν τον πήγαν στο νοσοκομείο; -“Δεν το ζήτησε”…




-Ούτε τους ζήτησε νερό.




“Αν ζητούσε κάτι, μέχρι και ελικόπτερο θα κατεβάζαμε για να του το δώσουμε”…




*Κανένας όμως δεν είπε ότι του έδωσαν, έστω, ένα ποτήρι νερό.




Όπως κατήγγειλε ο ίδιος, τον παρέπεμψαν να πιει νερό από ένα χαλασμένο ψύκτη, σύρθηκε μέχρι εκεί και προσπάθησε να πάρει λίγες σταγόνες νερού στο στόμα του για να ανακουφίσει το σωματικό και ψυχικό του μαρτύριο. Και αυτοί τον χλεύαζαν και γελούσαν εις βάρος του για την προσπάθεια που κατέβαλλε. Αυτό του κόστισε ανυπολόγιστα, ακύρωσε την ύπαρξή του, όπως διαπιστώσαμε κι εμείς οι γονείς του.




-Και σαν προσαχθείς, σε ποιον ήταν χρεωμένος;




– …..




-Και ενώ δεν επρόκειτο παρά για μία απλή προσαγωγή κι ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος ήταν ήσυχος και ήρεμος (όπως είπαν), γιατί απαιτούνταν η συνδρομή έξι αστυνομικών; Τέσσερις της οπκε και δύο της Υ/Α Βόλου.




Πάλι απάντησαν ανεύθυνα, λέγοντας ψέμματα ότι δεν παρείχαν συνδρομή. Στην προανάκριση όμως άλλα κατέθεσαν. π.χ. κατηγορούμενος της οπκε: “..προσήλθαν και όλοι οι υπόλοιποι μηνυόμενοι. Παρείχαμε επιτήρηση στον Μάγγο Β.” (έγγραφα 1,2,6).




Κάποιος, σε σχετική ερώτηση του δικαστηρίου, γιατί άλλα έλεγαν πριν και άλλα τώρα, είχε την αφέλεια να απαντήσει ότι άλλαξε η υπερασπιστική γραμμή…




Παρατήρηση του δικαστηρίου: “η αλήθεια δεν αλλάζει”.




*Όπως ακριβώς με την ιατροδικαστή και τους γιατρούς τους. Οι τρεις γνωμάτευσαν ότι τα πλευρά τα είχε σπασμένα, πριν τον χτυπήσουν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια και ο τέταρτος υποστήριξε ότι του τα έσπασαν μπροστά στα δικαστήρια…




-Και τί ώρα αποχώρησαν από την υπηρεσία τους;




Οι αστυνομικοί της οπκε απάντησαν ότι αποχώρησαν πριν τις πέντε μ.μ. Όμως στον Πίνακα Διάταξης της Υπηρεσίας και σε δεύτερο έγγραφο αναφέρεται ότι η υπηρεσία τους ήταν από 10π.μ. έως 6 μ.μ. (έγγραφα 3,4,5). Και ο σκοπός πύλης κατηγορηματικά κατέθεσε ότι τους είδε να αποχωρούν στις 6μ.μ.




Και ποιοι αποχώρησαν πρώτοι; Όλοι ισχυρίστηκαν ότι οι κατηγορούμενοι της οπκε




αποχώρησαν πρώτοι. Όμως στην προδικασία ένας κατηγορούμενος ισχυρίστηκε το




αντίθετο (έγγραφο 6).




Αντιφάσεις, αντιφάσεις και ψέμματα…




-Γιατί τον κράτησαν σχεδόν δύο ώρες και τον άφησαν αβοήθητο, ενώ ήταν ήδη χτυπημένος;




Του έκαναν σωματική έρευνα, (δεν του βρήκαν τίποτα) αλλά δεν αντιλήφθηκαν να πάσχει από κάτι:




“Ηταν μια χαρά!”.




*Έκθεση σωματικής έρευνας, όμως, δεν συνέταξαν. Ούτε ενημέρωσαν τον εισαγγελέα. Κι ενώ έπρεπε, όπως ισχυρίστηκαν, να τον συλλάβουν για τα υποτιθέμενα αδικήματα αντίστασης κατά της αρχής και απόπειρα απελευθέρωσης κρατουμένου, παρ΄όλα αυτά δεν το έκαναν, ούτε σχημάτισαν δικογραφία εις βάρος του…




Όμως “αυτοί δεν ευθύνονται για τίποτα”, οι ανώτεροί τους φταίνε που έδωσαν προφορικές εντολές να μη σχηματιστεί δικογραφία και να τον ελευθερώσουν…




“Φταίει ο διοικητής της Υ/Α”… “Ήταν εντολή άνωθεν να μη γίνει σύλληψη και δικογραφία”… “Ο διοικητής της Υ/Α δεν ενημέρωσε τον εισαγγελέα και βρισκόμαστε εμείς στο εδώλιο”, κραύγαζαν αγανακτισμένοι!! Όμως δεν ζήτησαν εξηγήσεις γιατί “κανένας ανώτερος δεν θα δώσει λόγο σε κατώτερο ποτέ”! Και γι αυτό “πάντα την πληρώνουν οι χαμηλόβαθμοι”…




Και στην ερώτηση, γιατί δεν ήρθε ο διοικητής να καταθέσει “Δεν ξέρω, είναι και εν ενεργεία” απάντησαν.




* Όμως, παρά την εμπειρία τους και την “εντιμότητά” τους, δεν αντέδρασαν, ούτε έκαναν αυτό που όφειλαν να πράξουν, να απαιτήσουν δηλαδή τη σύλληψή του και το σχηματισμό δικογραφίας, όπως οι ίδιοι διατείνονταν ότι έπρεπε να γίνει.




Στην προανάκριση όμως δεν ανέφεραν τίποτα από όλα αυτά!




Παρατηρούμε εδώ μία προσπάθεια να μεταφερθούν ευθύνες στην Αστυνομική Διεύθυνση ή στην Υ/Α Βόλου. Θα είχε μεγάλο ενδιαφέρον να ακούγαμε τις εξηγήσεις των ανωτέρων τους στις “μομφές” των κατηγορουμένων.




Ο διοικητής της Υ/Α Βόλου πάντως, παρότι ήταν μάρτυρας, δεν εμφανίστηκε στο δικαστήριο…




Το πιο σημαντικό όμως που συνδέεται άμεσα με την προστασία του πολίτη είναι αν πράγματι η Αστυνομική Διεύθυνση Μαγνησίας και η Υ/Α Βόλου λειτουργούν κατ αυτόν τον παράτυπο, ανεξέλεγκτο τρόπο. Χωρίς δηλαδή να εφαρμόζεται ο νόμος, αλλά οι αποφάσεις παίρνονται από τους ανώτερους και εκτελούνται με προφορικές εντολές, από τους υφισταμένους τους, σύμφωνα με τις απολογίες των κατηγορούμενων…




Κάτι που αν ισχύει, πρέπει να απασχολήσει σοβαρά τον υπουργό Προστασίας του Πολίτη.




Κύριε Χρυσοχοΐδη, στη συγκεκριμένη περίπτωση ο Βασίλειος Μάγγος οδηγήθηκε στο θάνατο, εξ αιτίας όσων υπέστη μέσα στην Υ/Α Βόλου και οι κατηγορούμενοι πετάνε το μπαλάκι στους ανώτερους. Μήπως αυτά είναι δικαιολογίες και προφάσεις των κατηγορουμένων να ενεργούν κατ αυτόν τον τρόπο, γνωρίζοντας ότι θα έχουν το ατιμώρητο; Τι πραγματικά συμβαίνει;




-Επίσης υποστήριξαν ότι είναι έμπειροι αστυνομικοί, ότι έχουν κάνει χιλιάδες συλλήψεις, όμως εκείνη την ημέρα όλα πήγαν στραβά, τίποτα δεν λειτούργησε σωστά, υπήρξε “σωρεία λαθών και παραλείψεων”.




-Καταμετρήσαμε και 21! παρεμβάσεις των συνηγόρων υπεράσπισης στις απολογίες των κατηγορουμένων καθώς και στις ερωτήσεις του δικαστηρίου…




-Τέλος, επικαλούμενοι τα θρησκευτικά τους αισθήματα, χρησιμοποίησαν επιχειρήματα που μόνο ως ύβρεις μπορούν να εκληφθούν.




Και όλοι τους δήλωσαν πως είναι περήφανοι που είναι οικογενειάρχες, που έχουν παιδιά και τα μεγαλώνουν…




Αυτό όμως δεν στάθηκε εμπόδιο στις 14 Ιουνίου 2020 να χτυπήσουν ανελέητα, να βασανίσουν ένα άλλο παιδί τον Βασίλειο Μάγγο και να τον στείλουν στο θάνατο.

title: Yekem rêzefîlma anîmasyonî ya kurdî: "Pirsên Azad" wê di Zarok TVyê de dest pê bike
content:
Rêzefîlma ku derhênerîya wê Ceren Asik Demîr dike ya bi navê “Pirsên Azad” di 12ê Cotmehê de li ser ekranên Zarok TV yê dest bi weşanê dike. Dûblaja rêzefîlmê bi temamî Kurmancî û dîmenên wî bi alîkarîya hişê çêkirî hatiye çêkirin.




Anîmasyon dê her hefte bi beşeka nû were pêşberî bîneran. Rêzefîlm ji bo zarokan hatiye amadekirin û lehengê bimeraq Azad, bi saya pirsên ku ji jiyana rojane, ji civaknasiyê heta stêrnasiyê, ji felsefeyê heta fîzîkê deriyên qad û dîsîplînên cuda vedike.




Di vê rêwîtîyê da ku ji kolanên kevir yên Mêrdînê heta Pira Malabadê, ji Baxçeyên Hewselê heta kûrahîyên fezayê dirêj dibe. Rêzefîlm li şûna bersivên amade, temaşevanan vedixwîne ku ew pirsan û lêkolînê bikin û li bersivên xwe bigerin.







"Rojhilat û Rojava bi hev ra diaxive"




Di rêwîtîya Azad da el-Bîrûnî û Lévi-Strauss, Îbn Xeldûn û Durkheim, Îbn Heysem û Newton li kêleka hev dipeyivin. Rêzefîlm dîroka zanistê bi awayekî yek-navend û yek-deng rave nake. Ew, nîşanî temaşevanên ciwan dide ku erdnîgarîya wan jî tevkarîya zanistê kirîye.




"Çîrok bi hişê çêkirî hatîye xêzkirin"




Dîmenên projeyê bi amûrên hişê çêkirî hatine çêkirin. Senaryo, montaj, dûblaj, muzîk û mîksaj jî bi temamî bi keda mirovan hatîye amadekirin. Ekîba projeyê, hişê çêkirî wekî amûrekê dibîne ku astengîya li pêşîya çêkirina anîmasyoneka bikalîte ya bi zimanekî bidezawantaj ji navê hiltîne .

‘Meraqa bi zimanê dayikê’




Rêzefîlm ji cihekî hêsan dide rê, berhemên ku zarokên Kurdîaxiv bikarin bi zimanê xwe zanistê keşf bikin, pir kêm in. “Pirsên Azad” armanc dike ku bi Zarok TVya ku bi salan e bi zimanê zarokên Kurd weşanê dike, vê valahîyê hinekî dagire. Derhêner Ceren Asik Demîr di derheqê rêzefîlmê de wiha dibêje: “Her zarok bi pirsan mezin dibe; me jî xwest ku zarok bi zimanê xwe yê dayikê li bersivên van pirsan bigerin. Hêvî dikim ku meraqa Azad bibe meraqa her zarokê li ber ekranê.”




Her wiha qonaxa sêwirana dîtbarî û anîmasyonê ji alîyê derhêner Ceren Asik Demîr û Erdal Tîmûr ve hatîye birêvebirin. Senaryoya wê M. Dara nivîsîye. Kawa Cengîz Yildiz dengê xwe daye karakterê Azad, derhênerîya dublajê jî Cebar Alp kirîye. Kendal Adiguzel, Eylul Nazlier û Sîmyager jî muzîka anîmasyonê amade û îcra kirine.




(AY)

title: Aynur Sarıca: Women must play a founding role in the peace process
content:
Aynur Sarıca of the Jineolojî Academy drew attention to the role women must play in the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that pressure and attacks against the women's movement in Kurdistan were continuing.




Sarıca said women must not be confined to following the process or being represented on monitoring commissions, stressing that their participation in decision-making mechanisms was crucial to building a democratic society.




Sarıca said women had played an important role in shaping social life throughout history, but that the nation-state mentality and patriarchal structures continued to attack women's labour, identity and lives. She added that women's historical role had been pushed into the background in dominant narratives.







 







Sarıca said women had often been treated as spoils of war or as instruments for ensuring the continuation of a lineage during periods of war and conflict, but had fought throughout history to defend their existence against such attacks.




She said attacks on women's identity, children, labour and social life had continued through different methods as conflicts intensified in Kurdistan. She added that operations and detentions targeting the women's movement were intended to prevent the struggle for women's freedom from taking root throughout society.




Sarıca said: “Women have asserted their struggle for existence in every period by declaring, ‘We existed, we exist, and we will continue to exist.’ They have carried on this struggle through their identity, labour, way of life and social relationships. In the context of Kurdistan, as conflicts have intensified, we have seen attacks on women's identity, social life, children and labour increase through special warfare methods. The targeting of the women's movement, attempts to undermine its social foundations and attacks driven by a patriarchal mentality were intended to create a barrier preventing the struggle for women's freedom from spreading throughout society.”




‘Women must be active participants in commissions’




Aynur Sarıca said women's role in the Peace and Democratic Society Process needed to be reconsidered, stressing that women could not be confined to positions on monitoring commissions.




Sarıca emphasised that women were founding subjects of a democratic, ethical and political society.




Sarıca said: “The women's struggle and women's freedom are among the fundamental areas around which we organise. Drawing on this paradigm and ideology, we have organised, and continue to organise, around how women's existence, lives and struggles should take shape within society. In the course of a democratic struggle, women cannot simply remain observers or be limited to positions on monitoring commissions. On the contrary, women are the founding subjects of a democratic, ethical and political society. For this reason, we continue to insist that women establish commissions, participate in them and take an active role in decision-making mechanisms.”




Sarıca said commissions composed exclusively of men would lead to social problems being addressed once again through a patriarchal approach. She stressed that women's commissions needed to be considered in their legal, political and social dimensions.




Sarıca continued: “If the commissions to be established consist only of men, society will once again be shaped by codes that impose sexism. This would mean that provisions and laws concerning women, labour, children and society as a whole would once again serve the dominant mentality. This is why we insist and struggle for women to participate in commissions as active decision-makers. We approach this not merely as a legal or political issue, but as a whole, including its dimension of building social life. We do not adopt a fragmented approach; instead, we act on the basis of a comprehensive model of governance and democratic life.”




‘A democratic model of life must be developed as a whole’




Aynur Sarıca argued that addressing social problems in isolation created conditions for massacres, deaths and sexism, stressing the need to build a comprehensive democratic model of life.




Sarıca said women's role in the peace process should also be considered from this perspective and added: “We have seen that fragmented approaches lead to massacres, deaths, sexism and all forms of fascism. The logic of ‘divide and rule’ has prevailed. Our criticism is aimed at presenting an alternative that is the complete opposite of this approach. We want to rebuild a democratic model of life as a whole. For this reason, together with the Free Women's Movement (TJA) and all women's movements engaged in the struggle for women's freedom, we are demonstrating that women have a distinct role in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Women must not be objects who merely observe; they must be active subjects and architects of this process.”




‘Excluding women from decision-making deepens existing problems’




Aynur Sarıca said women's participation in politics and areas of struggle, and the expansion of that participation throughout society, were also important for reducing violence and femicide. She stressed that preventing women from taking part in decision-making mechanisms deepened existing problems.




Sarıca drew attention to the increase in femicides in 2026 and said: “When women's participation in politics and the struggle becomes widespread throughout society, violence and femicide decrease, and conditions emerge in which society as a whole has a say. However, there is also a mentality that prevents this from happening. Such incidents should decline during every process of resolution and negotiation, yet we have seen the opposite in the most recent period, with femicides increasing in 2026. One reason for this is that women are unable to participate in commissions as active subjects through their ideas, perspectives and practical involvement, or rather, that no space is created for them to do so. Instead, women continue to face attacks and interventions carried out through special warfare strategies.”




‘Women’s active participation creates the power to find solutions’




Aynur Sarıca said women's participation as active subjects in decision-making processes would create opportunities for solutions not only for women but for society as a whole. She added that women's struggle for rights, equality and democracy would contribute to establishing a model of free living.




Sarıca concluded: “Where women are active subjects, breathing space opens up for society. We are not talking about just one gender; children and society as a whole are also part of this. When women become active subjects, they ensure the continuity of social life. Demands for rights, equality and democracy bring freedom with them. Once a model of free and equal living is established, a focus for solutions emerges to address the problems that have been confined within perceptions imposed from outside. For this reason, we believe that when women take on an active role in the commissions to be established, they will emerge as a force capable of finding solutions to social problems.”

title: Peace Mothers join 'Tuesdays Against Executions' campaign
content:
The Kurdistan Peace Mothers issued a statement regarding their participation in the 'Sêşema Na ji bo Darvekirinê' ('Tuesdays Against Executions') campaign.




The statement drew attention to how Iran’s regime, through its unfair courts, sentences political prisoners and civilians to mass executions every day on baseless charges. It said: “With each passing day, the shadow of the executioner regime weighs more heavily on prisoners.”




Emphasizing that life, freedom, and human dignity are fundamental and inalienable rights, the statement stressed that no mother should be forced to live in fear of her child being executed. It continued: “Execution does not merely bring one person’s life to an end; it also condemns a family to suffer forever. An execution leaves a profound impact on a family for the rest of its life. We offer our support to families who have lost their loved ones.




We demand that the fate of the prisoners be clarified as soon as possible. We call on all families, human rights organizations, and defenders of freedom to be the voice of the prisoners until freedom is secured, and the truth comes to light.”

title: Police raid Halk TV: broadcast suspended, trustee appointed
content:
Police raided Halk TV’s headquarters in Istanbul in the early hours of Wednesday morning. A trustee was appointed, and its television broadcast was halted. While police searches of the building continued, the road where the channel is located was closed to traffic, and employees were denied entry to the building.




Reporting on the latest developments inside the building after police entered Halk TV, channel presenter Deniz Bayramoğlu said: “Halk TV Editor-in-Chief Suat Toktaş held talks with the head of the trustee board about continuing the broadcast, but the talks were inconclusive. The broadcast has been suspended.”




As part of the investigation, arrest warrants were issued for 17 people, and 11 people were reportedly taken into custody.




Halk TV Board Chair Cafer Mahiroğlu also announced the police raid on social media. Mahiroğlu said: “Kılıçdaroğlu, the leader of the annulment faction, and his team may be happy. The police are at Halk TV.”




Press organisations and unions protest the attack on press freedom




The appointment of a trustee to Halk TV and the suspension of its broadcast prompted protests from press organisations and journalists’ unions. DISK Basın-Iş, the Contemporary Journalists’ Association (ÇGD), and the Journalists’ Union of Turkey (TGS) condemned the decision as interference in press and freedom of expression.




DİSK Basın-Iş stated that the action against Halk TV brought to mind the intervention against TELE1 last year, adding that the jobs and futures of hundreds of media workers had also been put at risk. The union called on the public to defend press freedom, the right to access information, and the labour of journalists.




The Contemporary Journalists’ Association also described the appointment of a trustee and the suspension of the broadcast as a serious infringement of press freedom and freedom of expression. ÇGD stated that no media outlet in Turkey could any longer be assured of its right to broadcast freely and declared that it would continue its struggle for a free press and democracy.




The Journalists’ Union of Turkey, meanwhile, condemned the police raid on Halk TV and the interference with its broadcast. Describing the decision as arbitrary, TGS stated: “We will not accept this bullying! The press is free and cannot be censored!”

author: Brian Hioe
title: Taiwan Again Rolls Out the Red Carpet for an Authoritarian Monarch For National Day
content:
KING MSWATI III of Eswatini was recently in Taiwan for National Day. As a result, the red carpet was once again rolled out for the authoritarian monarch, who presides over Africa’s last absolute monarchy, by the Lai administration.

In particular, apart from Mswati III’s presence at National Day, President Lai Ching-te and Mswati III visited Taiwan’s Air Force Command. Lai touted support from Mswati III on establishing the Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park, as well as Eswatini’s role as Taiwan’s gateway into Africa. Eswatini is Taiwan’s only remaining diplomatic ally in Africa.

Ties between Eswatini and the Lai administration have been in the spotlight in recent years, especially after a dramatic visit to the country by Lai. In May, a planned trip by the Taiwanese president for King Mswati III’s 58th birthday and the 40th anniversary of his accession to the throne was abruptly canceled.

This occurred because countries that Lai would have passed over on his flight to Eswatini, Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles revoked overflight permissions shortly before Lai was to set out. This was largely interpreted as China flexing its muscles in terms of its influence in Africa, with the Lai administration suggesting that China threatened to revoke debt cancellation for Madagascar, Mauritius, and the Seychelles if they did not comply.

Lai still later traveled to Eswatini aboard Mswati III’s private aircraft. This took place with Lai abruptly traveling to Eswatini, then only announcing that he had arrived after the fact. Presumably, this was to minimize the space for China to react. Lai arrived in Eswatini by traveling on King Mswati III’s personal aircraft, a former China Airlines plane that was sold to the monarch in 2015. Lai later returned on the same aircraft, taking a winding route that tested the operational limits of the plane, but similar to the route taken by then-US Speaker of the House Nancy Pelosi during her August 2022 trip to Taiwan.

Still, one notes that–as is broadly the case with Taiwan’s diplomatic relationship with Eswatini–there was little criticism of Eswatini’s record on human rights afterward. Eswatini is an absolute monarchy. The constitution was voided in 1973, and political parties were banned, as a result of which free and fair elections still do not take place in Eswatini today. Although Mswati agreed to constitutional changes in 2005, he retains his grip on power. Under Mswati III’s rule, life expectancy has halved in Eswatini since 2000.

Pro-democracy protests rocked Eswatini in the summer of 2021, with the public calling for the right to vote. In the violence that followed, 28 were shot, with demonstrators alleging that at least twenty were killed. Tear gas was used by police against demonstrators, and Internet services were suspended, with a curfew declared in major urban centers, in which buildings were burned during the turmoil, including Manzini and Mbabane, as well as the industrial center of Matsapha.

Much as occurred during Taiwan’s authoritarian period, Eswatini also sees the killing of dissidents. In 2023, opposition politician Thulani Maseko was killed by unknown gunmen in a shooting widely suspected of being ordered by the monarchy. Maseko was a human rights lawyer and public intellectual. At the time, Mswati III stated, “People should not shed tears and complain about mercenaries killing them,” implying that he had ordered the killing.

Nevertheless, after the demonstrations, Taiwan announced that it would be donating 637 million NT to the government for reconstruction–an act that makes it complicit in the government’s crackdown on the protests. Either way, Taiwan simply chose to act as though the protests had never occurred.

Indeed, in spite of its human rights violations, Taiwan has continued to blithely engage in trade relations with Eswatini. And Mswati III’s visit to Taiwan and plans for the Taiwan Industrial Innovation Park are the latest such example. Still, in the absence of international criticism of Taiwan’s ties to Eswatini, there will be little incentive for the government to make any changes.

title: Fermiamo la propaganda di guerra, inceppiamo la macchina bellica, disertiamo gli eserciti
content:
La propaganda militarista continua a crescere ogni giorno sia a livello nazionale che internazionale.




Il messaggio delle istituzioni veicolato dai media è sempre più chiaro: dobbiamo prepararci alla guerra per difendere la nazione. L’aumento delle spese militari e delle missioni all’estero, il rafforzamento del potere del complesso militare-industriale, la capillarità della penetrazione dell’esercito nelle scuole e nelle università, la sempre maggior presenza dei soldati nelle strade delle città sono tutti segnali chiari della direzione in cui si sta andando. 




In questo quadro si inserisce la questione della reintroduzione della leva militare in vari paesi europei. Se in Germania questo processo è già in fase avanzata, nel nostro paese, per ora, il modello scelto è quello di un rafforzamento dell’arruolamento, aumentando la propaganda soprattutto negli istituti scolastici, preparando così il terreno per il futuro ad un’eventuale reintroduzione della leva militare.




In questo scenario è di vitale importanza continuare a praticare l’antimilitarismo in tutti gli ambiti sociali e in tutte le occasioni possibili.




Sosteniamo lo sciopero internazionale contro la guerra indetto dalla CIT Confederazione Internazionale dei lavoratori per il 30 ottobre e le manifestazioni del 31 ottobre. 




Indichiamo nel 4 novembre, giornata delle forze armate e dell’unità nazionale, una data significativa per sviluppare iniziative sui vari territori.




Appoggiamo le mobilitazioni che si stanno sviluppando a livello studentesco e territoriale contro il reclutamento per l’esercito e contro ogni ipotesi di reintroduzione della leva.
