Τρία χρόνια έχουν περάσει από την από την έναρξη των ναζιστικών βομβαρδισμών των σιωνιστών εναντίον των κατοίκων της Λωτίδας της Γάζας. Μέσα σε λιγότερο από δύο χρόνια το κράτος δολοφόνος του Ισραήλ, ισοπέδωσε πόλεις και χωριά που έμεναν 2,5 εκατομύρια πολίτες. Κατέστρεψε νοσοκομεία και σχολεία. Προκάλεσε λιμό στερώντας το φαγητό, το νερό και την ιατρική- φαρμακευτική περίθαλψη από τους κατοίκους της Γάζας. Ένα χρόνο τώρα εν μέσω εκεχειρίας, με πιο αργούς ρυθμούς, η γενοκτονία του Παλαιστινιακού λαού στη Γάζα συνεχίζεται. Ταυτόχρονα έχει κλιμακωθεί η πολιτική του αποικισμού της Δυτικής Όχθης και έχουν ενταθεί οι απειλές πλήρους προσάρτησης της. Αυτή η βάρβαρη πολιτική του Ισραήλ έχει δολοφονήσει πάνω από 75.000 Παλαιστινίους και τραυματίσει πάνω από 175.000 σε Λωρίδα της Γάζας και Δυτική Όχθη συνολικά.


Πέρυσι την άνοιξη, η ισραηλινή βουλή ψήφισε τον νόμο που επιβάλλει την θανατική ποινή στους Παλαιστίνιους επειδή αντιστέκονται στον κατακτητή της πατρίδας τους, απειλώντας άμεσα και την ζωή χιλιάδων πολιτικών κρατούμενων που βρίσκονται στις ισραηλινές φυλακές, πολλοί από αυτούς χωρίς καν τις στημένες δίκες των ισραηλινών δικαστηρίων.


Αυτό το φρικτό, γενοκτόνο καθεστώς απαρτχάιντ και εποικισμού, στήριξαν και στηρίζουν με όλα τα μέσα – στρατιωτικά, πολιτικά, οικονομικά- οι ΗΠΑ και η Ευρωπαϊκή Ένωση, μαζί και η ελληνική κυβέρνηση. Οι υποκριτικές φωνές κάποιων ευρωπαϊκών χωρών δεν ξεπλένουν το ΑΙΜΑ των δεκάδων χιλιάδων Παλαιστινίων, με το οποίο έβαψαν τα χέρια τους αμερικάνοι και ευρωπαίοι ιμπεριαλιστές. Είναι φωνές που ζητούν καλύτερη μοιρασιά στη λεία.


Η ελληνική κυβέρνηση, συνεχίζει και κλιμακώνει την πολιτική των προηγούμενων κυβερνήσεων. Έχει μετατρέψει τη χώρα σε πλατφόρμα πολέμου των ΗΠΑ -ΝΑΤΟ. Η «στρατηγική συμμαχία» με το γενοκτόνο Ισραήλ έχει μετατραπεί σε «εθνική γραμμή» για κυβέρνηση και δήθεν «αντιπολίτευση». Προσφορά στρτατιωτικών διευκολύνσεων, τριμερείς άξονες και εκτεταμένη στρατιωτική συνεργασία. Η «Ασπίδα του Αχιλλέα» που η ελληνική κυβέρνηση αγόρασε πρόσφατα από το Ισραήλ και για την οποία είναι σύμφωνοι κυβέρνηση και δήθεν «αντιπολίτευση», δεν μας προστατεύει. Είναι μαγνήτης πολέμου και αντιποίνων! Αυτή η πολιτική των εξοπλισμών για να υπηρετηθεί ο αντιδραστικός ανταγωνισμός των αστικής τάξης της Ελλάδας με αυτή της Τουρκίας, πολλαπλασιαζει τις πολιτικές της ακρίβειας, της φτώχειας και της καταστολής από τις οποίες στενάζουν οι εργαζόμενοι και η νεολαία.


Σε μια τέτοια συγκυρία έρχεται ο αμερικανός ΥΠΕΞ, Μάρκο Ρούμπιο. Για να προωθήσει τα πολεμικά σχέδια των ΗΠΑ και να απαιτήσει από την άρχουσα τάξη και την κυβέρνησή της απόλυτη ευθυγράμμιση και την ακόμα πιο βαθιά εμπλοκή σ΄αυτά. Για να επιβεβαιώσει την στήριξη των ΗΠΑ στο Ισραήλ και στους άξονες με την χώρα μας και την Κύπρο. Για να επεκταθεί κι άλλο το δίκτυο των βάσεων του θανάτου στη χώρα μας, αυξάνοντας κι άλλο τους κινδύνους για τον λαό μας.


Οι λαοί όλου του κόσμου, ο δικός μας λαός, είναι με την πλευρά του δίκαιου αγώνα του λαού της Παλαιστίνης και της Παλαιστινιακής Αντίστασης για ΛΕΥΤΕΡΗ και ΑΝΕΞΑΡΤΗΤΗ πατρίδα! Το διεθνές κίνημα αλληλεγύης είναι που έχει οδηγήσει σε πρωτοφανή ποσοστά αρνητικής στάσης απέναντι στο Ισραήλ παγκόσμια αλλά και σ’ αυτά που συνέβησαν στον ΟΗΕ. Και όση λάσπη και αν ρίξουν τα παπαγαλάκια του συστήματος, όσα μέτρα καταστολής και να πάρουν, ο λαοί, ο δικός μας λαός θα είναι με το δίκιο! Γι αυτό και θα κυματίζουμε την παλαιστινιακή σημαία, ως σύμβολο ΑΝΤΙΣΤΑΣΗΣ και ΠΑΛΗΣ ΓΙΑ ΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΙΑ ενός λαού!


Γιατί γνωρίζουμε καλά ότι αγώνας αυτός είναι και δικός μας αγώνας. Είναι ο αγώνας που κάνουμε εμείς οι εργαζόμενοι/ες και οι νέοι/νέες για να έχουμε ζωή, δουλειά και σπουδές με δικαιώματα και ελευθερίες. Είναι αγώνας ενάντια στον πόλεμο, τον φασισμό και τον ιμπεριαλισμό!

Εργατικό Κέντρο Πάτρας










 Ανεπιθύμητη η επίσκεψη Ρούμπιο στην ΕΛΛΑΔΑ 

 Οι εργαζόμενοι, ο λαός μας έχουν χρέος να εκφράσουν αγωνιστικά την αντίθεσή τους απέναντι σε αυτήν την επίσκεψη. Είναι χρέος στις οικογένειές μας στο μέλλον το δικό μας και των παιδιών μας να τον υποδεχτούμε με μαζικές κινητοποιήσεις!










Να ακουστεί δυνατά ότι ο λαός μας δεν δίνει τη συγκατάθεσή του να γίνεται η χώρα μας ορμητήριο θανάτου και στόχος αντιποίνων. 

 Ο Ρούμπιο έρχεται για να εξασφαλίσει για τις ΗΠΑ και το ΝΑΤΟ διευκολύνσεις σε λιμάνια, αεροδρόμια και στρατόπεδα για τα πολεμοκάπηλα σχέδιά τους.










Η κυβέρνηση ετοιμάζει για τον λαό και τα παιδιά του, την «πατρίδα» της μεγαλύτερης εμπλοκής στα ευρωατλαντικά σχέδια για τα συμφέροντα του κεφαλαίου. 

 Οι «εθνικοί» στόχοι του κεφαλαίου για το 2030, πίσω από τους οποίους στοιχήθηκαν στη ΔΕΘ όλα τα αστικά κόμματα, περνάνε μέσα από τη μεγαλύτερη συμμετοχή στον πόλεμο και σε όλα τα ανοιχτά του μέτωπα ακριβώς για να μπορέσει η ελληνική αστική τάξη να πάρει κομμάτι από τη πίτα.










 Κάθε γύρος αυτού του «διαλόγου», από το 2018 με την κυβέρνηση ΣΥΡΙΖΑ με πρωθυπουργό Τσίπρα ως σήμερα με τη ΝΔ, άφησε πίσω του περισσότερες βάσεις και μεγαλύτερους κινδύνους, διεύρυνση της χρήσης της Σούδας το 2019, επ’ αόριστον επέκταση της συμφωνίας το 2021 με αναβάθμιση σε Αλεξανδρούπολη, Λάρισα, Στεφανοβίκειο. Αυτές οι πολιτικές διαμόρφωσαν το αεροδρόμιο της Ανδραβίδας κεντρικό κόμβο για τους ΝΑΤΟικούς σχεδιασμούς. Ασκήσεις όπως Ramstein Flag 2024, η προετοιμασία για υποδοχή F-35 δείχνουν τον ρόλο που αναθέτουν στο αεροδρόμιο η κυβέρνηση και το ΝΑΤΟ. 

Άλλωστε, αποτελεί ήδη σημείο μεταστάθμευσης των δυνάμεων που κινούνται προς Ανατολική Ευρώπη και Μέση Ανατολή.










 Η εργατική τάξη έχει δείξει ότι μπορεί να σταθεί εμπόδιο στα πολεμικά τους σχέδια. Ο λαός και η νεολαία της περιοχής, έδωσαν μεγάλες μάχες και συγκρούσεις που έγιναν στη βάση του Αράξου, με σύνθημα «να κλείσει ο Άραξος, να φύγουν τα πυρηνικά», γι΄ αυτό και καταφέραμε να απομακρυνθούν το 2001.










 Οι λιμενεργάτες της ΕΝΕΔΕΠ στον Πειραιά μπλόκαραν φορτία πολεμικού υλικού για το Ισραήλ και στις 6 Φλεβάρη συντονίστηκαν με λιμενεργάτες σε 20 λιμάνια 7 χωρών της Μεσογείου και της Ευρώπης.










 Στις 30 Οκτώβρη, πάνω από 45 λιμάνια ετοιμάζονται για τη 2η Διεθνή Μέρα Δράσης με αγωνιστικές, απεργιακές κινητοποιήσεις!










 Αυτός είναι ο δρόμος! Κανένας εργάτης συνένοχος στο έγκλημα για τα κέρδη που είναι βουτηγμένα στο αίμα και τη φτώχεια των λαών. Κανένας Έλληνας στρατιώτης στα πολεμικά μέτωπα! author: Fozzie
title: Part IV: The Production of Relative Surplus-Value
content:
Harry Cleaver's study guide to Marx's Capital volume 1, chapter 18.



































    Submitted by 

Fozzie

 on October 6, 2026
  
















































































































































































































Outline of Marx’s Analysis




 

Marx’s formulae 

 – 

s/v

 = surplus-value/(value of 

LP

) = (surplus labor)/(necessary labor) 

 Classical political economy formulae 

 – (surplus labor)/(working day) = surplus-value/(value of product) = (surplus product)/(total product)

 – working day, value of product, total product = 

s+v

 in Marx’s terms (leaves out 

MP

 or 

c

) 

 Political economy formulae 

 – understates rate of surplus-value

 – conceals exchange of wage for 

LP

 

 – creates the illusion of sharing according to contribution vs actual antagonism 

 

v

 = paid labor, 

s

 = unpaid labor, popular expressions for (surplus labor)/(necessary labor)

 capital = command over unpaid labor




Commentary




In this chapter Marx, pauses a moment before the section on wages, to juxtapose his own formulations to those of classical political economy and to critique the latter in ways that foreshadow the critiques he will make in the next three chapters.




By always comparing surplus value (or product) to the total value (or product), classical political economists portrayed the relationship between workers and capitalists in ways that 1) hid the existence of exploitation and 2) created an illusion that labor was getting its fair share. The existence of exploitation was hidden by making it appear that each factor of production, i.e., labor and capital, is rewarded according to its contribution to production. So, surplus value, 

s

, appears to equal capital’s contribution and 

s/(s + v)

, its share, while by implication, variable capital, 

v

, appears to equal labor’s contribution and 

v/(v+s)

, its share. Within a few decades after 

Capital

 was published, neoclassical economists, having substituted utility for labor value, would use the same trick but with fancier mathematics.




Mathematical concepts such as production functions, e.g., 

Q = f(K, L)

, permitted the use of calculus to derive marginal products for 

K (dQ/dK)

 and 

L (dQ/dL)

 and with a few more assumptions, conclude that wages = market value of 

dQ/dL

 and profits = the market value of 

dQ/dK

. In the development of this theory of production, the labor theory of value of the classical political economists was set aside, so the only “value” left was money price determined by markets. Yet the conclusion was essentially the same, both the old formulae and the new ones hid exploitation by reducing the antagonistic social relations of production to engineering-like technical relations among things.

(1)




For Marx, by formulating the value of labor as one part of the working day, the classical political economic formulation understated what was for him the essential issue: how much of workers’ time toiling produced the means of consumption they needed (or their value/money equivalent) and how much of their work time produced the means of production (or their value/money equivalent) capital needed. Clearly, both formulations of the rate of surplus-value, the classical one, 

s/(v+s)

, and his own, 

s/v

, are possible measures of capital’s share of the total new value created. He preferred 

s/v

 because it provided a more direct representation of the division of workers’ days. When he notes how 

s/(v+s)

 is a “mode of presentation which arises, by the way, out of the capitalist mode of production itself”

 

(2)

 and promises to return to the point later on, odds have it that he was thinking about the parallel between 

s/(v+s)

 and 

s/(c+v)

, the rate of profit. He did return to juxtapose the rate of profit to the rate of exploitation in material included in Volume III of 

Capital

 where he presents the rate of profit as expressing capital’s preoccupation with the rate of return on its investment 

(c+v)

 and the rate of exploitation as expressing the degree to which workers are being exploited, i.e., forced to produce products and value for someone else.

(3)




Commenting on the “popular expression” that juxtaposes unpaid to paid labor, instead of surplus to necessary labor, Marx affirms the reasonableness of that way of talking about exploitation in money terms. By pretending to buy labor, rather than labor-power, capitalists argue that all labor is paid for. But as workers grasp intuitively and Marx’s analysis in 

Chapter 6

 demonstrated, although fluctuations in supply and demand can push wages above, or drive them below the value of labor-power, on the average workers are only paid wages equivalent to the amount of work that produces the value of their labor-power and capitalists arrogate to themselves the fruits of all excess labor beyond that—with no compensation to those performing it. He concludes, “Capital, therefore, is not only command over labour, as Adam Smith thought. It is essentially the command over unpaid labor. All surplus-value . . . is in substance the materialization of unpaid labor time.” 

(4)

 But what is the importance of this command over unpaid labor time? We have seen how Marx’s focus is on one, and only one, use of surplus-value, or unpaid labor time: investment, i.e., employing it to impose more work in the future!




Footnotes




1

 It would not be until the 1960s, when economists at Cambridge University in England, building on the work of Piero Sraffa (1898&ndash1983), attacked these formulations and forced neoclassical economists to admit that they were built on logical flaws, e.g., they pretend to 

derive

 the price of capital but to do so they must 

assume

 the price of capital in order to aggregate heterogeneous capital to come up with "

K

". See G. C. Harcourt, 

Some Cambridge Controversies in the Theory of Capital

, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1972. 

 

2

 

Capital, Vol. I

, p. 670. 

 

3

 

Capital, Vol. III

, Part One, Chapter 3: "The Relationship between Rate of Profit and Rate of Surplus-Value". 

 

4

 

Capital, Vol. I

, p. 672.

title: French Youth Take the Streets against a Bleak Future : A Report
content:
This past week, thousands of teenagers have taken the streets of France, clashing with police as they demonstrate against the deplorable conditions in their high schools and a rapidly collapsing future. This is a promising sign, shifting attention from the seemingly unstoppable rise of the extreme right to the question of what people can do on a grassroots basis to defend themselves. Our correspondents in Paris explore the situation in detail.







Another unprecedented summer of record 

heatwaves

, 

droughts

, and 

wildfires

 throughout Europe underlines the desperate situation we are all facing today, while politicians of all stripes and their techno-industrial sponsors continue to turn a blind eye, forcing us down the path to catastrophe in the name of progress.




Hoping to turn the page on these environmental disasters, the French government has hurriedly shifted focus to other priorities. The coming months represent a crucial transition for Emmanuel Macron and his government, as they will bring Macron’s second term to a close, opening a new political era in France. Candidates are already battling to succeed Macron in power at the beginning of May 2027.




In the midst of this political spectacle, during an increasingly 

menacing surge

 in the popularity of the National Rally (formerly, the National Front), the extreme-right party, it is especially meaningful that teenagers have started to organize at a grassroots level to defend themselves. This organizing gained momentum last week, when blockades of high schools, demonstrations, and riots erupted across France, taking everyone by surprise.







 




Students clash with police forces in Montpellier on October 2, 2026.













Licensed to Kill?




Since Macron was elected President for the first time in May 2017, the political discourse in France has been even more dominated by an emphasis on authoritarian and far-right ideologies in terms of security, immigration, and economic and social issues.




This political shift towards an even more aggressive form of governance has led to increasing state violence targeting the social movements and uprisings that have emerged since. From the eviction of the 

ZAD

 at Notre-Dame-des-Landes in 2017 to the 

riots

 following the murder of Nahel in 2023, not forgetting the 

Yellow Vest

 sequence and the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown experimental 

doctrines

, we have experienced a headlong plunge into a world of surveillance, repression, and loss of individual freedoms. This has become today’s new normal.




It was in this already suffocating context that last July, the French government decided to vote on a new bill giving police officers more latitude to use their firearms without consequences—a demand that the far right has promoted for years. If voted through, this legislation could set a 

dangerous precedent

, as it would establish “a presumption of ‘legitimate use of arms’ by police and gendarmes ‘in the exercise of their duty’.”







 




Police arrest a student in Lyons on October 1, 2026.










In other words, not only will police officers be able to freely use their weapons if in any situation they claim to fear for their lives or the lives of others, but authorities will no longer have to prove that the officers acted within the framework of the law, as they are required to do today. It will be up to the victims and their families to provide evidence that the use of firearms was not justified. We can already see how this new law represents a legislative tool enabling law enforcement agents, and therefore, the state, to cover up future murders.




Unwilling to let such a law pass without resistance, political opponents and radicals, who had rightly rebranded this law the “license to kill,” decided to organize massive demonstrations and events throughout France on the weekend of September 18 to 20. 

Thousands

 of people took part in these protests in different major cities alongside traditional leftist politicians, rights groups such as Amnesty International and the League of Human Rights, and various lawyers and magistrates’ unions.




In the meantime, another call for action reusing all the codes of the Yellow Vest movement spread online. The origins of this call remain obscure, as some national 

newspapers

 have raised the possibility that AI-generated accounts had flooded social media platforms with this rumor on purpose. Nevertheless, media and politicians began commenting on this potential resurgence of the Yellow Vest movement due to the rise of fuel prices and the overall increase of living costs. Rumor or not, the call to take the streets on October 17, 2026 has spread and only the future will tell us if people’s desperation and anger will be able to give birth to another inspiring moment.







 




Police forces welcome students blocking their high school with clouds of tear gas in Lille on September 30, 2026.










Growing Frustrations…




Since mid-September, another form of discontent has been slowly spreading within another part of society. Tired of their working conditions, some high-school students decided to block access to their schools in order to make their voices heard. During the early stages of what became a national movement a few days later, only a few high schools were blocked here and there. This did not create any real impact or worry the authorities.




Among the students’ various demands, we can summarize the following points:







Reduce the number of students per class.







For years now, the number of students per class has gradually increased to the point that it is not unusual for a teacher to have an average of between 30 to 35 students in a classroom. This is impacting the capacity for every single student to learn at their own pace.







Reduce the number of school hours per week.







Even if France is known for having numerous and long school breaks throughout the year, students usually spend a long day at school—sometimes from 8 am until 6 pm—adding up to 28 or 35 hours of teaching per week, depending on the high school level and options.







Improve high school infrastructure.







Just like the state’s territorial management, high schools reproduce social inequalities. Some high schools located in rich districts have no infrastructure issues, while high schools located in low-income areas are falling apart. For example, some high schools have constant bathroom issues, some have no heat during winter and no proper insulation, some have roofs that leak when it rains.







Put an end to “ParcourSup.”







“ParcourSup” is the name of an online platform that students have to use during their final year to list what they would like to do after the school year. Created in 2018, this platform allows students to list their “wishes” and apply to different post-secondary education options such as universities, colleges, vocational and trade schools, and the like. Run by algorithms, this platform has been criticized since its implementation for the opacity of the criteria according to which it fulfills or thwarts students’ wishes. The platform creates considerable stress and competition among students, as those with better grades can be accepted more easily while the others might find no options whatsoever after high school, proving once more that this form of computerized selection increases social disparities and inequalities.







Engage more substitute teachers to maintain continuity in learning.







Students have been complaining that when one of their teachers is sick, there is often no substitute teacher available to take over in order to assist them in continuing to learn. This creates situations in which students sometimes don’t have a teacher for weeks in a specific discipline, even if it will be part of their national high school diploma exam.







 




Students burning trash bins in front of a high school in Lille on October 1, 2026.










All the 

previous points

 made by students are the direct result of years of educational restructuring, public spending cuts, and neo-liberal reforms. More and more, public schools are managed like private companies and forced to compete with one another to be more efficient.




This is not to say that without public spending cuts and neo-liberal reforms, the school system would be desirable. Under capitalism, the school system is a tool for the state to coerce us, to crush our individuality, to subdue our rebellious spirits and desires in order to reduce us to a docile workforce that can be exploited for the rest of our lives.







 




Police forces moving towards a burning barricade in Saint-Denis on October 1, 2026.










…Burst into Flames




By Monday, September 28, word had finally spread among students to coordinate actions on a larger scale. Early that morning, students started blocking the entrances of their schools, creating makeshift barricades out of whatever they could find nearby and in some cases by setting trash containers ablaze. Some of these blockades might have been the initiative of student unions or small political organizations, but in other cases, these actions were clearly personal initiatives on the part of small groups of highly motivated individuals. Viral images on social media likely helped to spread the word, creating a domino effect among teenagers: “Look at what the other high school is doing. Let’s do it, too!” This first day of action set the tone for the rest of the week as the movement spread beyond Paris and its suburbs.




The following day, while teachers, health care workers, firefighters, and other people from the public sector went on strike and 

demonstrated by the thousands

 in various cities against the next government budget cuts and in favor of better wages and working conditions, high-school students increased the pressure by protesting in front of some 400 schools throughout France, fully blockading approximately 40 of them.




Without hesitating, Laurent Nuñez, the current Interior Minister and former Prefect of Police of Paris from 2022 to 2025, decided to repress this emerging movement via brute force. Police were sent to high schools to crush the blockades and disperse the crowds of teenagers. Unsurprisingly, this strategy provoked confrontations between high-school students and heavily equipped police forces.




During the clashes, police used numerous tear gas canisters and shot rubber bullets at students while groups of teenagers and young adults resisted by throwing stones, bottles, fireworks, and other projectiles. By the end of the second day of actions, more than 400 individuals had been arrested across France, with two thirds of those arrests leading to police custody, according to 

official sources

.







 




Police forces in front of a burning barricade in Lille on September 30, 2026.










Nevertheless, the brutal repression didn’t undermine the determination of the students, who decided to continue the movement, blocking the schools on a massive scale on Wednesday, September 30. Clashes with law enforcement continued to escalate while blockades and other actions spread to numerous major cities, forcing the Interior Minister to officially recognize that same night that despite his repressive strategy, the student movement was gaining momentum and expanding. On September 30, police arrested 

625 individuals

 during the clashes. The first evidence of police brutality circulated online, as at least three students were severely injured by police ammunition.




On Thursday, October 1, the students continued to organize. For the first time since the beginning of the movement, some university students decided to join the struggle—even if they were not as numerous and determined to act as their younger accomplices. Fully 900 demonstrations, riots, and blockades took place 

all around France

. Authorities reported arson attempts both outside and inside some buildings; due to some extensive fire damage, a high school in Nantes will remain closed for a whole month. That day, students were able to shut down at least 160 high schools and to block access to 30 universities. This intense day of action resulted in almost 2000 new arrests, raising the total number of students arrested and detained since the beginning of the week to nearly 3000.







 




The Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes on October 1, 2026. After the arson, the high school will remain closed for at least a month.










Defending Power at Any Cost




That night, the government realized that its inability to control student unrest was drawing it towards another political crisis.




In order to regain control of the situation, the authorities made several hasty decisions:










The current Prime Minister called a crisis cabinet meeting for the following day to discuss possible plans and strategies to put an end to this unrest, on the grounds that the situation had shifted from a student movement characterized by school blockades to an unruly situation of urban violence.










The Minister of Education announced publicly that 400 high schools would be closed on Friday for “safety reasons,” either because the safety of the working personnel and students could not be assured, or simply on account of property damage. Students who can’t go to their schools will be following their classes online. In doing this, the government is reusing some of the strategies implemented during the COVID-19 pandemic in a different context.










The Minister of Education also announced that, the following day, he would meet with student unions and political organizations to hear their demands and find collective solutions in order to end the crisis. By meeting so-called spokespersons, the government wants to weaken the movement by dividing “good” students with legitimate requests from “rioters” and “violent individuals.”










The Interior Minister presented law enforcement agencies with an official list of all the high schools considered “high risk” by its intelligence services. In Paris alone, there were 13 high schools on this list. This suggests that the government has identified potential threats to the reigning order and is preparing to do everything in its power to neutralize these threats.










The Minister of Justice gathered attorneys general in order to discuss the proper legal response to adopt in order to prosecute all the students in custody. It is highly possible that the government will try to process these cases as fast as possible in courts, requesting harsh legal repercussions in order to make an example of these brave young individuals.










Nonetheless, all these announcements barely curbed the momentum of student unrest. Actions, blockades, and clashes with police continued across the country on Friday, October 2 before a well-deserved weekend.







 




A police officer attempts to destroy a burning barricade in Aubagne on October 2, 2026.










After a full week of political unrest involving intense property destruction, confrontations with law enforcement, and repression, and while the first trials were getting underway, political leaders of every stripe sought to use this situation to their own advantage, reaffirming their various positions.




While Marine Le Pen, the leader of the far-right party National Rally, emphasized the supposed need to create a new “anti-rioter” law in order to repress those who commit property destruction and resist police, the Macron government criticized the “violence” that took place and played on the classic dichotomy between “good ways of protesting” and “unforgivable ways of protesting”—while at the same time accusing the so-called “far-left” statist party of being responsible of all these events.







 




Clashes between students and police forces in Brest on October 2, 2026.










On Sunday, October 4, the 

government officially announced

 that the following day, more than 400 high schools in France would remain closed as security conditions still could not be assured. The Minister of Education declared that “24 schools had been burnt or ransacked and 78 education staff members injured” since the beginning of the movement.







 




Riot police arrest a demonstrator in front of a high school in Toulouse on October 2, 2026.













 




Students running away from tear gas in the streets of Lyons on October 2, 2026.










What Now?




Right now, information is flooding 

media outlets

 about the events of Monday, October 5. So far, it is estimated that almost 1000 individuals were arrested today, 589 schools experienced protests or blockades—240 schools in the Paris region alone—and 65 law enforcement agents were injured during confrontations with demonstrators. This suggests that the movement is not slowing down.




We are deeply saddened to learn that on October 5, in Lens, a 15-year-old boy 

lost his hand

 after picking up a stun grenade that law enforcement officers used to attack protesters. One of the three teenagers injured last week suffers from a broken jaw, having been shot point blank with a grenade launcher. Currently, the 14-year-old boy can’t open his mouth, as all his bottom teeth were knocked out by the impact and all his upper teeth are broken. Another 16-year-old teenager injured last week lost an eye after an officer shot him in the face with a rubber bullet.




Unfortunately, as the government is not willing to back down and wants to regain control by any means necessary, police violence will only continue to escalate. More and more serious injuries are likely to occur in the next days of confrontations. So far, according to official sources, 215 students have been injured since the beginning of the movement, as well as 85 educational staff members and—supposedly—715 law enforcement officers. These figures are skewed to over-represent police: the state does not distinguish “offensive” injuries such as bruised knuckles from inflicted injuries, while most demonstrators who are injured do not dare to seek treatment for their wounds or, if they do, conceal the fact that they were injured by police violence. Injuring and mutilating people both physically and psychologically is the only solution the state has found to preserve the fragile illusion of order. The police and the government are not here to protect us.




Since the beginning of the student unrest, 5060 people have been arrested, including 4406 minors and 654 adults. As of today, 1802 individuals are facing charges: 1483 minors and 319 adults. Of those, 14 are in pre-trial detention—10 adults and 4 minors.







 




A burning barricade in Aubervilliers on October 2, 2026.










Right now, people are holding their breath on the eve of the Third Act of this high school movement. On Tuesday, October 6, there is 

another call

 to 

join students in the streets

. Several sectors are already planning a variety of blockades elsewhere in France in solidarity.




No one can predict what will happen next or if the current political unrest will continue to gain momentum, reinventing and extending itself until October 17, the next day that there is a national call to take the streets. No one knows if the movement will find its resources to survive the brutal state and police repression that it is experiencing.




All we know for certain is that nothing is written in advance. The courage of the students taking part of this movement should inspire all of us to act now and to continue to push forward in order to fight against all odds for a better world!







 




Confrontations in Cran-Gevrier between students and police forces on October 1, 2026.










Further Reading




These articles, written in French, explore these events further:







À nos enfants et lycéens




Brûle ton lycée













 




A makeshift barricade in the streets of Paris on October 2, 2026. The graffiti refers to the extreme-right National Rally party.

author: Katja Diehl
title: Part 1/3: Vom „schlechten Weg" zum elektrischen Tuk Tuk: Graubünden zeigt, was geht.
content:
Es ist zwar erst ein paar Tage her, aber aus den Erlebnissen werden schon Erinnerungen.


Meine Delegationsreise in die Schweiz, genauer gesagt nach Graubünden, hat mich mit Energie „vollgepumpt”, dieses Format zu verstetigen. Dieser Wissenstransfer ist nur möglich, wenn Menschen sich begegnen. Die Gruppe lernte hautnah beim „Erfahren“ der gerechten Mobilität, wie Expert*innen vor Ort diese gestaltet hatten - aber auch die Gastgebenden konnten von der Gruppe und ihren Hinweisen profitieren.




Hier ein Rückblick auf unseren ersten Tag, den wir mit einer Führung „in die Vergangenheit“ begannen. Während Autobahnen in Deutschland eher geschichtslos sind, da sie erst mit dem Aufkommen des Automobils entstanden sind, können die Wege in Graubünden, auf denen sich heute sowohl Autos als auch Waren bewegen, auf eine Geschichte zurückblicken, die bis in die Römerzeit zurückreicht. „Viamala” (zu Deutsch: „schlechter Weg”) war ein berüchtigtes Teilstück beim Überqueren von Alpenpässen, da es sehr gefährlich war. In Thusis, unserer ersten Station, wurden die erschöpften Pferde seinerzeit gegen frische ausgetauscht.




In Deutschland undenkbar:


Ein 150-Seelen-Dorf wird mittels einer elektrischen Seilbahn an das Nahverkehrsnetz angeschlossen. Die Fahrt mit der Gondel dauert nur sieben Minuten, mit dem Bus hingegen 40 Minuten. Die Fahrgastzahlen erreichten innerhalb kurzer Zeit Rekordniveau, da dieses Angebot auch für Tourist*innen ein Ziel erschloss, das sie zuvor vielleicht nicht auf der Karte hatten. Die Bahn fährt bis tief in den Abend, danach kann das Publicar, ein Rufbus, bestellt werden. Ein Traum.




Krönender Abschluss des Sonntags war die Begrüßung durch Remi Crameri, Gemeindeammann von Thusis, mit ihm durfte ich bereits am Donnerstag einen Talkabend über Mobilität gestalten. Er berichtete uns von einer anstehenden Ratssitzung, in der das Gesamtkonzept des Verkehrs im Kanton Graubünden bis in die Dörfer hinein aufeinander abgestimmt werden soll, um weitere Verbesserungen zu erzielen. Ein besonderes Highlight für ihn ist das Projekt mit Elektro-Tuk-Tuks. Diese sollen Tourist*innen bequem vom Bahnhof Thusis in die Viamala-Schlucht bringen. Das zeigt, wie wichtig der Tourismus für eine gerechte Mobilität ist.




Die nächste Delegation ist bereits terminiert, kommentiere einfach LUXEMBURG, dann schicke ich dir den Stand der Planungen gern zu! Das besondere Highlight hier: Der ehemalige Verkehrsminister und "Vater" des kostenlosen ÖPNV in Luxemburg, François Bausch, wird unser lokaler Guide sein.




Danke an alle, die dabei waren - ich hoffe für uns alle, dass ich diese Konzept ausweiten kann. Es funktioniert umwerfend gut!

author: CNT Granollers
title: La seguridad de las personas trabajadoras debe estar por delante de los beneficios
content:
Desde la CNT del Vallès Oriental queremos denunciar la gestión del episodio de lluvias intensas y, especialmente, la carencia de medidas suficientes para garantizar la seguridad de las personas trabajadoras de la comarca.




Cuando las autoridades activan avisos y alertas por fenómenos meteorológicos adversos, no es suficiente con informar a la población. Es necesario adoptar medidas preventivas que eviten que miles de personas se vean obligadas a desplazarse por las calles y carreteras para llegar a sus puestos de trabajo en unas condiciones potencialmente peligrosas.







Las empresas y la patronal también deben asumir su responsabilidad en materia de prevención de riesgos laborales.







Consideramos especialmente grave que no se haya paralizado o restringido la actividad económica cuando las condiciones meteorológicas y avisos existentes podían comportar riesgos para los desplazamientos y para el desarrollo de determinadas actividades laborales. La protección de la vida y la integridad física de las personas trabajadoras debe estar por delante de cualquier consideración productiva o económica.




Pero la responsabilidad no recae únicamente sobre las administraciones. Las empresas y la patronal también deben asumir su responsabilidad en materia de prevención de riesgos laborales. No es aceptable que, ante un episodio meteorológico adverso, se mantenga la presión para que las plantillas acudan presencialmente a los centros de trabajo como si no estuviera ocurriendo nada. Las empresas deben evaluar los riesgos, activar medidas preventivas y, cuando las circunstancias lo requieran, detener la actividad o facilitar alternativas que eviten exponer a las personas trabajadoras a riesgos innecesarios.




La patronal no puede reclamar que la actividad económica se mantenga a cualquier precio mientras los costes y riesgos de esta decisión recaen sobre las personas trabajadoras. No puede hablarse de normalidad productiva cuando llegar al puesto de trabajo puede implicar poner en riesgo la integridad física. La prevención no puede quedar subordinada a los intereses empresariales ni a la necesidad de mantener sus ritmos de producción.




También queremos poner el foco en el momento en que se hizo llegar la alerta a la población. Una alerta que llega cuando miles de trabajadores y trabajadoras han salido ya de casa y se encuentran desplazándose hacia sus centros de trabajo pierde buena parte de su función preventiva. La información ante un episodio meteorológico adverso debe ser suficientemente anticipada para que las personas puedan tomar decisiones seguras y para que empresas y administraciones puedan activar medidas preventivas con tiempo.




Ante este tipo de episodios, es preciso recordar que las personas trabajadoras tienen derechos que las empresas deben respetar. El artículo 37.3.g del Estatuto de los Trabajadores reconoce un permiso retribuido de hasta cuatro días cuando no sea posible acceder al centro de trabajo o transitar por las vías necesarias para ello, ya sea por las recomendaciones, limitaciones o prohibiciones de las autoridades o por una situación de riesgo grave e inminente. Ningún trabajador o trabajadora debería tener que escoger entre proteger su integridad física y conservar su salario. Ante una situación de riesgo, el derecho a la seguridad debe prevalecer sobre la obligación de acudir presencialmente al puesto de trabajo. Y las empresas deben informar adecuadamente a sus plantillas sobre estos derechos, en lugar de exigir una normalidad laboral que las condiciones meteorológicas no permiten.




No podemos normalizar que, ante una situación meteorológica adversa, la responsabilidad recaiga individualmente sobre cada trabajador o trabajadora, obligándole a decidir entre exponerse a un riesgo durante el desplazamiento o arriesgarse a sufrir consecuencias laborales por no acudir a su puesto de trabajo. La prevención de riesgos no puede convertirse en responsabilidad individual de quien trabaja: es una obligación empresarial.




La seguridad no puede llegar después del horario de entrada al trabajo. Cuando existe riesgo, prevenir también significa detener.




Desde la CNT del Vallès Oriental continuaremos defendiendo que ninguna actividad económica puede justificar poner en riesgo la integridad de las personas trabajadoras. Los beneficios empresariales no pueden estar por encima de nuestras vidas.




La entrada 

La seguridad de las personas trabajadoras debe estar por delante de los beneficios

 se publicó primero en 

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Girard Mariano Lopez
title: Taipei Gay Bar Raid Sparks Protest, Scrutiny Of City’s Commitments to LGBTQ+ Rights
content:
A POLICE RAID on a longstanding gay bar in Taipei sparked a lightning protest and demands for independent oversight after patrons alleged humiliation and discrimination, prompting disciplinary action against officers and an apology from the mayor weeks before the city’s annual Pride celebrations.

About 100 to 200 people gathered at 1 p.m. Oct. 4 outside a police substation near Red House, a landmark in Taipei’s LGBTQ+ district. After speeches, demonstrators marched through the busy neighborhood to the Ximending Police Station which reportedly dispatched the order to raid the gay bar, demanding an explanation and apology for the previous afternoon’s operation at Commander D.

The dispute has drawn scrutiny of police treatment of sexual minorities and intensified questions about whether Taipei’s promotion of LGBTQ+ inclusion abroad is reflected in its policing at home.

Officers entered the BDSM-themed bar Oct. 3 with what police described as a court-issued search warrant obtained under prosecutors’ supervision following complaints about suspected sexual offenses. Police said the establishment had received 13 complaints this year.

Authorities said 51 people were referred for suspected violations of the Social Order Maintenance Act and the operator for a suspected criminal offense. That account differed from protest speakers’ figure of 59 people taken for questioning.

Protest organizers said the operation lasted nearly five hours. They alleged officers refused to show customers the warrant, ordered people to squat and restricted conversation and cellphone use. Patrons also reported being prevented from putting on clothing before being taken to the police station.

Organizers said officers directed derogatory comments about sex toward a wheelchair user and handcuffed the manager, who they alleged was ordered to kneel after protesting police conduct.

Police initially denied insulting disabled patrons and maintained that officers followed lawful procedures. By Oct. 5, however, authorities acknowledged inappropriate remarks by four officers after reviewing recordings. Each received two reprimands, the supervising investigation chief received a demerit, and the Wanhua precinct chief requested two reprimands for inadequate supervision.

Police maintained that the warrant had been displayed, leaving conflicting accounts about whether customers were adequately informed of the search’s basis.

The operation followed a September council exchange in which Democratic Progressive Party Councilor Hung Chien-yi raised allegations that minors were entering the establishment and being treated as sexual playthings. Mayor Chiang Wan-an subsequently ordered police to investigate.

Commander D denied the allegations, saying it checked identification and ages at entry. The bar, which said it had operated for 14 years, distinguished private interactions between adult customers from activities arranged or directed by its management and said it would cooperate with lawful investigations.

Although speculation linked the raid to drugs, police publicly described its basis as suspected sexual offenses. At Sunday’s protest, Green Party city council candidate Wang Chen-ting rejected suggestions that the operation uncovered illegal drugs.

Wang said medications examined by officers included HIV prevention drugs and produced no positive drug findings. Wang also alleged that records showed eight police inspections of the venue within 15 days the previous month.

People taken for questioning were denied food and water for hours and faced leading questions about sexual activity, Wang said.

Protest organizers also reported police visits to Hunt and Locker Room, two other gay venues, that night. They demanded an explanation of the legal justification for the operations and questioned whether queer gathering places were being subjected to discriminatory scrutiny.

Outside Ximending Police Station, demonstrators called for the police chief to come down, explain the operation and apologize. Instead, Wanhua internal affairs officer Lin Sheng-wei addressed the crowd, promising an investigation and disciplinary action where warranted, without offering an apology.

“If our colleagues are at fault, they should be disciplined,” Lin said.

Organizer Yang Kang concluded by handing Lin a copy of Taiwan’s Code of Criminal Procedure, underscoring protesters’ demand that officers follow legal safeguards when exercising police powers.

Chiang, of the Kuomintang, initially defended the operation’s legal authorization while ordering a review of possible misconduct. On Oct. 5, he apologized and said police discipline must be strengthened to prevent officers from engaging in discrimination.

His Democratic Progressive Party challenger, Puma Shen, said lawful investigations still required scrutiny of police methods and equal respect for everyone’s dignity.

“Taipei’s diversity and inclusion should not be visible only on the day of the Pride parade,” Shen wrote, arguing that those values must extend to everyday policing and city institutions.

The controversy unfolded amid a separate election dispute over drug policy. Shen cited needle exchanges and methadone treatment in defending harm-reduction approaches, while Chiang accused him of blurring distinctions between illegal drugs and medication. Chiang said Oct. 4 that he continued to support methadone treatment and access to clean needles.

At the protest, Chiang Shu-hung, representing a Taiwanese sex workers’ rights organization, questioned whether the approaching election had contributed to the crackdown. No evidence presented established an electoral motive for the raid.

The mayor’s LGBTQ+ record had already become a campaign issue after critics questioned a photograph used in his Harvard University presentation. They said an image from a Halloween appearance had been presented as evidence of his participation in Taipei Pride.

City officials rejected accusations that Chiang had fabricated his attendance, producing a separate photograph and schedule records that they said showed he attended both events that day.

For LGBTQ+ advocates, the raid raised concerns extending beyond the election.

A coalition of more than 50 organizations, including the Taiwan Tongzhi Hotline Association, demanded an independent investigation, preservation, and lawful disclosure of enforcement recordings, and clear policing guidelines for LGBTQ+ venues. It also sought enforceable protections against discrimination and an end to stigmatizing descriptions of queer sexuality.

The groups said additional training alone could not resolve questions about coercion, procedural safeguards and accountability. Police should investigate specific suspected offenses, they argued, rather than treat sexual orientation, bodily expression or BDSM practices as evidence of criminality.

At the protest, hotline representative Kao Chih-lung linked the raid to earlier police harassment of gay gathering places, including Taipei’s parks and venues in the 1990s. The coalition also cited a 2025 search of a gay establishment in Taichung that it said subsequently closed.

Those experiences, advocates said, made the Commander D operation more than an isolated dispute. It revived memories of surveillance, public exposure, and humiliation among people who had relied on queer venues for community and safety.

With Pride approaching, the groups accused Taipei of promoting LGBTQ+ culture as an international tourism asset while failing to protect the people who sustain it. They warned that discriminatory enforcement undermined the city’s assurances that queer residents and visitors could gather safely.

A search warrant, they said in their joint statement, must never become blanket authorization to violate human rights or treat an entire community as inherently criminal.

author: Unknown
title: Çelik: Peace requires a democratic state
content:
Debate over a new period aimed at resolving the Kurdish question continues in Turkey. The process, which followed statements by Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) leader Devlet Bahçeli in October 2024 and began with the Call for Peace and Democratic Society issued by Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan on 27 February 2025, has remained on the public agenda for nearly two years.




Different sections of society have expressed a range of views on the process and the resolution of the Kurdish question, while expectations for peace have also continued to be debated over the past two years.




Reis Çelik, director of Let There Be Light (Işıklar Sönmesin), one of the first films to address the resolution of the Kurdish question in Turkey, spoke to ANF about the current state of cinema in Turkey and his views on the Peace and Democratic Society Process.




As a socialist, I am more inclined to tell the stories of what society experiences




Çelik said art was a field that gave voice to what remained unsaid and documented every aspect of life through different forms: “The primary function of art is to say what is left unsaid, to do what cannot otherwise be done, and to document every aspect of life through different means. Music does this, painting does this, sculpture does this, and literature does this. Cinema shows this courage more than any of them.




I am a storyteller. I do not insist on saying, ‘I am going to make political cinema’; I bear witness to my time. With so much injustice, corruption and poverty before me, what else could I think about? Of course, society also needs different things. One person makes people laugh, another makes them cry, and another tells stories about social problems. As a socialist, I suppose I am more inclined to tell the stories of what societies go through.”




Cinema was the most powerful language for saying there is a Kurdish question in this country




Reis Çelik said that when he made Let There Be Light, the state pursued an approach that denied the existence of the Kurdish question, while the arts were also under pressure. Çelik described the difficulties he faced during filming and his struggle to secure a theatrical release: “It was clear that the state’s general approach was to deny the Kurdish question. The arts had also been intimidated into silence. We were going through a period when saying, ‘There is a Kurdish question in this country,’ was considered a crime. It was a dark period in which unsolved killings had reached their peak.




I worked as a journalist for many years and spent time in conflict zones. The reports and photographs we produced as witnesses were being twisted and distorted beyond recognition. During that period, I left journalism and publishing because I wanted to tell what I had to say without allowing anyone to distort it. I decided that cinema was the most powerful language through which I could say that there was a Kurdish question in this country.




With Let There Be Light, I tried, in the simplest terms, to show ordinary people that there was a Kurdish question in this country. We wanted to shoot the film in actual conflict zones, but we were not given permission. The General Staff even sent instructions throughout the region stating that permission had not been granted for the film and that its production should be prevented. To some extent, we shot the film secretly. We tried to disguise it as though we were making a different film. We stayed in caves and did not go into the towns. We came close to freezing. Many of our colleagues needed treatment for years afterwards. Towards the end, our presence in the region was discovered and we faced serious difficulties.




A governor took the initiative and had us escorted safely out of the region. I later learned that he was the first Alevi governor to have served in Turkey. Getting the film into cinemas was also extremely difficult. Because I had worked as a journalist for many years, I was able to approach political figures I knew and eventually secure permission for the film to be shown in cinemas, albeit on a limited basis. My aim was not to become the ‘victimised, heroic director’ of a banned film. Nor was it to sell myself to the machinery of the imperialist Western world. What I wanted was to confront people with their own reality.”




Audiences were subjected to identity checks outside cinemas




Çelik said: “The film was released across Turkey with only four prints. Two were shown in Istanbul, one in Ankara and one in Izmir. Something nobody had expected happened: audiences began turning up in record numbers. For the first time in a long while, long queues formed outside cinemas. After a while, police began checking people’s identification at cinema entrances before allowing them inside. Those they did not approve of were denied entry. If people inside ululated or chanted slogans, the screening was stopped and the audience was removed. Tensions rose even further when the film reached cities in the east and southeast.




There were arrests, protest marches and other incidents. At the same time, the film’s release became a major story across the media. The right-wing press wrote that ‘the PKK had commissioned a film’, while the organisation’s side criticised it because ‘the PKK is not mentioned by name’. I had expected all of this. What mattered to me was that people had embraced the film and were confronting the reality that ‘there is a Kurdish question in this country’.




Lawsuits were also filed. There were Kurdish conversations and laments in the film, and it portrayed the state as a party to a war that it did not recognise as such, among other things. My own situation was rather difficult. We were living through a period when something could happen to me at any moment. My friends eventually took me to Germany for a while. The whole process dragged on like that.”




Much of the arts community appeared left-wing but had been intimidated




Reis Çelik also addressed why relatively few films had been made about the Kurdish question: “Given the pressure and censorship that the state had historically imposed on literature and the arts in Turkey, making films like this was almost impossible. What happened to Yılmaz Güney and other artists was already there for everyone to see, even though they had not addressed these issues so explicitly and directly. Another reality is that cinema is a very expensive art form. Making a film requires substantial investment. A producer will not take the risk unless they can clearly see a future for the project. Naturally, finding a producer willing to invest in a project dealing with a subject as sensitive as the Kurdish question was almost unimaginable.




Another problem was that much of the arts community appeared left-wing and democratic, but in reality, so to speak, the vast majority had been intimidated and driven into their corners. Some were actually ‘social fascists’. At the time, even the word ‘Kurd’ made them uncomfortable. We had enormous difficulty finding actors for the film. You would be surprised if I listed all the people whose doors I knocked on only to be turned away. Yet when circumstances became easier, they all suddenly became sympathetic to the Kurds.




In other words, we have an ‘intellectual’ community that has become remarkably skilled at turning into a bird when it sees a cliff and a fish when it sees water. All of this has obstructed the production of films offering new perspectives in this field.”




Those who are fighting are the ones who can end wars




Çelik also spoke about the talks between the Turkish state and the Kurdish movement and the new period: “Thirty years have now passed since Let There Be Light was released in cinemas in 1996 and sparked widespread debate. Some of the issues discussed between the soldier and the guerrilla in the film are now being discussed in the Grand National Assembly of Turkey. An internal conflict has been going on in these lands for nearly 50 years. The Turkish state has finally reached the point of acknowledging, ‘Yes, there is a Kurdish question in this country.’ The forces in the mountains, meanwhile, have concluded that the armed struggle has reached the limits of what it can achieve.




As the government was searching for a new political path to secure its continuity, its coalition partner presented it with the most unexpected option: ‘Let us bring the period of armed conflict over the Kurdish question to an end. Let Founding Leader Abdullah Öcalan come and guide this process through Parliament.’ This unexpected proposal from the leader of the ultranationalist-nationalist wing, which had been at the forefront of the conflict for nearly half a century, had the effect of an earthquake. What surprised people most was that such an initiative had come from the nationalist camp.




In my view, this was not surprising. Wars, conflicts or, in the simplest sense, fights can only be ended by those who are actually fighting. Who was fighting the PKK? The military, the police and, in civilian life, predominantly the ultranationalist-nationalist camp. The proposal to ‘stop’ came from that same camp. Ultimately, the will to bring it to an end lies in the hands of these two forces.




The Turkish Republic needed to end this war because it had understood that it could not destroy the will of a people. It needed to end it because it had realised that it could no longer bear the cost. It needed to end it because it had seen that the imperialist world was beginning to rearrange the balance of power in the Middle East and had realised that remaining within these borders required finding a way out through this process. Finally, a government that had collapsed politically and economically needed a new move to prolong its survival for a little longer.




The forces in the mountains also needed this transformation. First, they had sufficiently demonstrated to the state that the Kurds were not ‘Kart-Kurt’, as they had once been dismissively portrayed. Second, the movement had grown to such an extraordinary scale and developed so many branches that the possibility of parts of it slipping beyond control had become increasingly apparent. With an organisation rooted in socialist principles conducting a struggle across such a vast area, it had become inevitable that imperialist power interests would penetrate the process and create the potential for outside influence. Most importantly, everyone had come to realise that the Kurdish people no longer had the strength or patience to continue bearing such a heavy cost.




All of this made it necessary to sit down at the negotiating table. Attempts had been made before, mistakes were made and the talks collapsed. In this latest process, no one can afford to make another mistake. Every side knows very well what another failure could cost.”




Peace must be based on a social state




Reis Çelik also criticised the way Kurds were portrayed in cinema: “I am deeply uncomfortable with expressions and definitions such as ‘Kurds are our brothers too’, ‘Kurds are also citizens of this state’, ‘Kurds also have the right to have a say’, or ‘Kurds too can speak their own language and sing their own songs’. I detest this top-down, state-centred approach in films and other forms of art, as though rights were something to be handed out as a favour. The word ‘also’ carries an underlying sense of separation. Saying ‘they too’ is condescending.




The arts community thinks it is embracing the issue when it produces films using this kind of language. Consciously or unconsciously, people define their own social group as a superior identity. Films and other artistic works need to properly convey the idea that social peace can be achieved by accurately reflecting an understanding of the ‘democratic state’ through artistic production.”




Reis Çelik said peace needed to be built on the principles of a social state and concluded: “Everyone who is a citizen of this country is subject to compulsory military service. Flags were hung outside the homes of tens of thousands of our people who were killed in this war. Some of those homes were built of mud brick, some were unplastered and others were plastered. Some mothers sang their laments in Turkish, others in Kurdish.




Peace between the mud-brick home and the unplastered home means addressing Turkey’s economic inequality. That is also extremely important. This must be a peace founded on the principles of a social state, which is essential. Peace between identities and affiliations, meanwhile, is the peace that comes with an understanding of a democratic state.”

title: Kobanê students react to the Ministry of Higher Education’s decision
content:
Kobanê students gathered in front of Kobanê University to protest the Syrian Ministry of Higher Education’s decision to close the faculties and academies and turn them into part of Aleppo University, demanding that their right to study at Kobanê University be upheld.




The students made several demands of the Kobanê University administration and called for their demands to be taken into consideration and followed up.




The students listed their demands as follows:




1. The preservation of all existing faculties, institutes, and departments




2. Guaranteeing Kobanê students’ right to receive their education in the city where they live




3. Preserving and continuing the experience of education in Kurdish




4. Guaranteeing students’ education and preventing them from suffering academic losses




5. Ensuring the full participation of students in decisions to be made concerning the future of the university




6. Preserving the name “Kobanê University”




7. Preserving the distinct character of Kobanê University throughout the process of organization and integration.




The statement concluded with the following: “As Kobanê students, we are not asking for special privileges. We simply want our rights to receive an education at the university and to equal opportunities to be protected, as well as the city’s access to university education and professional training opportunities.”

Όπως ίσως έχετε δει στα 2 δελτία τύπου που έχουν δημοσιευτεί (

ενδεικτικά το 1ο εδώ

), πρόκειται για ένα εκτεταμένο έργο-κλειδί σε όλη την Πελοπόννησο που αφορά την ηλεκτρική διασύνδεση Υπερυψηλής Τάσης (400 kV) με τη Φωκίδα, για το οποίο μέχρι τώρα τηρούνταν σιγή ιχθύος! Αν και τυπικά η διαβούλευση της Μελέτης Περιβαλλοντικών Επιπτώσεών (ΜΠΕ) του έληξε στις 4/8/2026, συνεχίζει η ανάρτηση των αντιρρήσεων και, όπως μας βεβαίωσε εξειδικευμένος δικηγόρος, οι αντιρρήσεις γίνονται δεκτές ώσπου να αποφανθεί η αδειοδοτούσα αρχή.




Το ενιαίο βιομηχανικό σύμπλεγμα συνολικής ισχύος 1.849,875 MW αποτελείται από 460 MW Φωτοβολταϊκών Σταθμών, 44,5 MW Αιολικών Σταθμών (συνολικά 51 Ανεμογεννήτριες), αμφότερα με Συσσωρευτές (

μπαταρίες λιθίου 

φωσφορικού σιδήρου

) ισχύος 1.345,375 MW (εσφαλμένα η ΜΠΕ ενίοτε αναφέρει αυτήν ως τη συνολική ισχύ του έργου) και δυνατότητα αποθήκευσης ηλεκτρικής ενέργειας εγγυημένης χωρητικότητας 2.690,75 MWh. Δεσμεύει συνολικά ως Περιοχή Ενδιαφέροντος (πολύγωνα έργων) μια τεράστια εδαφική έκταση 46.399.096,62 τ.μ. (46.399 στρεμμάτων), και με επέμβαση (για τα κυρίως και συνοδά έργα) επί δασών και δασικών εκτάσεων τουλάχιστον σε 5.452.486,05 τ.μ. (5.452,5 στρέμματα).




Το έργο παραβιάζει, μεταξύ άλλων, τα Χωροταξικά Πλαίσια των Περιφερειών Πελοποννήσου και Δυτικής Ελλάδας, τη Δασική Νομοθεσία, την Ειδική Περιβαλλοντική Μελέτη 10β για περιοχές της Πελοποννήσου και το Ειδικό Χωροταξικό για τις ΑΠΕ, προκαλώντας ένα σωρευτικό ΑΛΛΑ ΚΑΙ ΑΝΕΠΙΤΡΕΠΤΟ πλήγμα στην Πελοπόννησο!




Σύμφωνα με τη ΜΠΕ του έργου:




– 

Καταλαμβάνει ζωτικές καλλιεργούμενες εκτάσεις, βοσκοτόπους και μελισσοκομικά πεδία, αλλάζοντας τις χρήσεις γης και με κίνδυνο καταστροφής τους και των υδροφορέων από τα τοξικά υλικά των ανεμογεννητριών, των πάνελ και των μπαταριών, με σοβαρότατες επιπτώσεις στην παραγωγή των ΠΟΠ προϊόντων: Μέλι Ελάτης Μαινάλου Βανίλια, Φέτα Καλαβρύτων, Φέτα Ερύμανθος, Φέτα Τρίπολης, Οίνος Μαντινεία, Μήλα Ντελίσιους Πιλαφά, των ΠΓΕ προϊόντων: Φασόλια Βανίλιες Φενεού, Φάβα Φενεού, Οίνος Ηλεία, Οίνος Αχαΐα, Οίνος Πλαγιές Αιγιαλεία, αλλά κα της ροδοζάχαρης Αιγίου, της πατάτας Βαλτεσινίκου και πλήθος άλλων προϊόντων όπως τα εξαιρετικά τοπικά μέλια, το παρθένο ελαιόλαδο κ.ά.




–

 Μέρος του χωροθετείται στο εγγεγραμμένο Γεωπάρκο στον Κατάλογο Παγκόσμιας Κληρονομιάς της UNESCO Χελμός (αν και η ανακριβής ΜΠΕ άλλοτε ισχυρίζεται ότι χωροθετείται εκτός)




–

 Αποκρύπτονται συστηματικά οι γεωγραφικές αποστάσεις κάθε υποέργου από τα 7 συνολικά, ωστόσο τα υποέργα εκτείνονται εντός Natura 2000 όπως ο Κορινθιακός Κόλπος και επηρεάζουν, λόγω κατάληψης ή γειτνίασης: Όρος Χελμός και Ύδατα Στυγός, Όρος Μαίναλο, Όρη Αρτεμίσιο και Λύρκειο, Λίμνη Τάκα, Όρος Ερύμανθος, Όρη Μπαρμπάς, Κλωκός και Φαράγγι Σελινούντα, Όρος Χελμός (Αροάνια) – Φαράγγι Βουραϊκού και Περιοχή Καλαβρύτων, Αισθητικό Δάσος Καλαβρύτων, Σπήλαιο Καστριών, Όρος Παναχαϊκό – Σύραγγες Παναγοπούλας, Όρος Ολίγυρτος σε Σημαντικές Περιοχές για τα Πουλιά: Όροι Χελμός και Βουραϊκός, Όρος Μαίναλο, Όρη Μπαρμπάς, Κλωκός και Φαράγγι Σελινούντα, Όρος Κυλλήνη (Ζήρεια), Θίνες Κυπαρισσίας (Νεοχώρι – Κυπαρισσία), Θίνες και παραλιακό Δάσος Ζαχάρως, Λίμνη Καϊάφα, Στροφυλιά, Κακόβατος. Επιπλέον, το έργο χωροθετείται εντός ή πλησίον δεκάδων προστατευόμενων Βιοτόπων, Σημαντικών Περιοχών για τα Πουλιά και Καταφυγίων Άγριας Ζωής.




–

 Θίγονται μεταξύ άλλων, τα προστατευόμενα Τοπία  Ιδιαίτερου Φυσικού Κάλλους (ΤΦΙΚ): Καρύταινα, Δημητσάνα, Στεμνίτσα και Φαράγγι Λούσιου, Κορυφές Όρους Μαίναλο, Λόφος Στόχος Νεστάνης (Τσιπιανών), Κερασιά – Βλαχοκερασιά Αρκαδίας, «Χώρος μάχης Βερβαινών», Πηγές Ποταμού Λάδωνα, Φαράγγι Βουραϊκού, Μονή Μακελαριάς – Βράχος – Γερακοβούνι – Λίμνη Ρακίτα, Πηγές Ποταμού Αροανίου, Μπουφούσκια Αιγίου, Φαράγγι ποταμού Νέδα, Παραπόταμοι Αλφειού, Λίμνη και Δάσος Καΐάφα, Κοιλάδα Φενεού, Μετέωρα Κορινθίας, Υψώματα βόρεια του χωριού Στενό Κορινθίας, Υψώματα Ελληνικού, Βουνό Παναγιάς Κορυφής, Υψώματα Λυγιάς. Να ειπωθεί επίσης ως Προστατευόμενο Τοπίο και Προστατευόμενος Φυσικός Σχηματισμός έχουν χαρακτηριστεί: το Φαράγγι της Νέδας (ΦΕΚ 3019/Β/08-05-2023) και η Μίνθη (ΦΕΚ Δ 192/Δ/17-03-2026)., που μαζί με την Αρχαία Ήλιδα, το Ναό Επικούρειου Απόλλωνα πλησίον Φιγάλειας και την Αρχαία Ολυμπία συνιστούν μέρος του Παρράσιου Πάρκου Πολιτιστικής Κληρονομιάς (ΦΕΚ Δ 192/17-03-2026).




– 

Αποφεύγεται η μέτρηση του θορύβου με τη νόμιμη κλίμακα του Ειδικού Χωροταξίκού για τις ΑΠΕ ώστε να αποφευχθεί η καταγραφή του μόνιμου βουητού, παρότι μέρος του ασύλληπτου έργου που χωρίζεται σε 7 υποέργα εγκαθίσταται σε απόσταση 277 μ. από σπίτια, όπως αναφέρει και στην αρνητική του γνωμοδότηση ο Δήμος Καλαβρύτων.




–

 Αποσιωπώνται όχι μόνο οι διαστάσεις του πρωτογενή τομέα αλλά και τα δίκτυα ήπιου τουρισμού που στηρίζουν τις τοπικές κοινωνίες, παρότι μέρος του χωροθετείται εντός ή διασπά και υποβαθμίζει μόνιμα:  το Ευρωπαϊκό μονοπάτι Ε4,  το Εθνικό Μονοπάτι Ο31, το Τμήμα (Ζυγοβίστι – Ελάτη) και τα Τμήματα 7 & 8 (Μαγούλιανα – Βαλτεσινίκο – Λαγκάδια) του δικτύου μονοπατιών του Μαινάλου (Menalon Trail) μήκους 75 χλμ. με ευρωπαϊκή πιστοποίηση τα Μονοπάτια Αρκάδων Ποιμένων, τα Αρκαδικά Μονοπάτια (Arcadia trail), το Μονοπάτι του Ερμή (Hermes Trail) που ανήκει στα Mythical Trails της Περιφέρειας Πελοποννήσου, το πελοποννησιακό τμήμα του Μονοπατιού του Ηρακλή, το μονοπάτι Αλωνίσταινα – Κολοκοτρωναΐκα Λημέρια – Λιμποβίσι. το πεζοπορικό δίκτυο του Ερυμάνθου-Χελμού-Αφροδισίου-Ολιγύρτου και της Ζήρειας, το Αναρριχητικό Πεδίο Νεστάνης, το Πεδίο Αλεξιπτώτου Πλαγιάς (Ανεμοπτερισμός) στο Σκιαδοβούνι Ερυμάνθου και ο αγώνας ορεινού τρεξίματος Ηράκλειος Άθλος.




Αυτά και άλλα πολλά, όπως τυχόν αναφλέξεις των μπαταριών ή βραχυκυκλώματα στα δίκτυα μέσης/υψηλής και υπερυψηλής τάσης που θα διασχίζουν την Ηλεία, την Αχαΐα, την Αρκαδία και την Κορινθία και, συνδυαστικά με τα αιολικά, θα ακυρώνουν την εναέρια δασοπυρόσβεση, τα διατυπώνουμε στο κείμενο αντιρρήσεων Δ11.




 Η ανταπόκρισή σας, καθώς και η κοινοποίηση του παρόντος σε άτομα και φορείς που ενδιαφέρονται να συμμετέχουν στη διαβούλευση ώσπου να αποφασίσει η αδειοδοτούσα αρχή, είναι παραπάνω από αναγκαίες.




Τέλος, αν έχετε κάποια ειδίκευση ή τοπική γνώση που θεωρείτε ότι μπορεί να συνεισφέρει στη συντακτική ομάδα των αντιρρήσεων, μη διστάσετε να επικοινωνήσετε μαζί μας.

author: Wanessa Celina
title: Senado deve avaliar PEC do fim da escala 6×1 no Plenário após primeiro turno das eleições
content:
Após o primeiro turno das eleições, o Senado Federal volta a discutir o fim da escala 6×1 a partir desta terça-feira, 6 de outubro. A Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC) 221/2019 reduz a jornada de trabalho para 40 horas semanais, com a possibilidade de dois dias de repouso remunerado. 

O Plenário realiza sessões para debater a PEC também na quarta-feira e na quinta-feira, 8 de outubro, a partir das 14h.




A análise entra na agenda do Plenário após negociações na última semana entre o presidente Lula e a cúpula do Senado para destravar o andamento da PEC. Em nota à imprensa, postada na Agência Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (UNIÃO-AP) afirma que a decisão surge a partir da “ampla relevância para a sociedade brasileira”.




Também nesta terça-feira, 6, cumprindo a Medida Provisória nº 1.394/2026, assinada por Lula, as empresas de apostas e as fintechs deverão terminar suas atividades

 e informar às instituições financeiras sobre os saldos dos clientes que não sacaram seu dinheiro até essa segunda-feira, prazo final para brasileiros sacarem o dinheiro dos aplicativos. Entre os dias 9 e 14 de outubro, as empresas deverão restituir dinheiro aos apostadores.




Corrida Eleitoral




Com a definição de um segundo turno entre o presidente Lula (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) para a presidência da República, os outros candidatos começam a discutir seu apoio para o segundo turno, dia 25 de outubro. O candidato Augusto Cury (Avante) disse que não pretende continuar na política e declarou que não vai apoiar ninguém para o segundo turno.




O mesmo ocorreu com Renan Santos (Missão), que não declarou seu apoio, mas, em live na segunda-feira, 5 de outubro, afirmou que seus eleitores podem escolher em quem votar. Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) comunicou que não irá declarar seu apoio sem antes se reunir com o presidente do partido, Gilberto Kassab. Sem posicionamento direto de apoio ao candidato Flávio Bolsonaro, Romeu Zema (Novo) declarou que vai estar contra o PT.




Com um período mais curto para o segundo turno, Lula, que teve 45,16% dos votos, em seu discurso pós-apuração declarou que irá começar com uma nova campanha. Para o presidente, o segundo turno irá mostrar “a verdadeira democracia do Brasil”. 

Nesta segunda-feira, 5, o presidente se reuniu com apoiadores para discutir novas estratégias de campanha.




Em contrapartida, 

Flávio Bolsonaro comemorou o resultado nas urnas. Nesta segunda-feira, o senador se encontrou com o deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) e com o governador de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos)

, ambos reeleitos, para discutir sobre as estratégias de campanha para o segundo turno.




Estão na agenda da semana de 6 a 10 de outubro:







TSE:







Salvo-conduto (06/10):

 último dia em que o documento de salvo-conduto, emitido pela Juíza Eleitoral, protege a integridade de eleitores que sofreram ameaças ou agressões para influenciar seu voto.




Eleitor pode ser preso (06/10):

 Fim do período em que eleitores não poderiam ser presos.




Justificativa do mesário (07/10):

 último dia para os mesários justificarem abandono do trabalho durante a votação.




Cadastramento (08/10):

 início do cadastramento das Mesas Receptoras de Justificativa e alocação temporária de seções para o segundo turno.




Propaganda eleitoral (09/10):

 Início da propaganda eleitoral nas rádios e na televisão.




Fundo Especial de Financiamento de Campanha (FEFC) (09/10):

 Último dia para a transferência, pelas agremiações, de recursos do FEFC destinados às candidatas e aos candidatos a cargos majoritários que concorram ao segundo turno.




Candidatos não podem ser presos (10/10):

 A partir desta data, candidatos que vão disputar segundo turno não podem ser presos, exceto em prisão em flagrante.
















STF:







Exclusão de créditos (RE 835818, 07/10, 14h):

 Recurso Extraordinário avalia se há possibilidade de exclusão os créditos presumidos de Imposto de Circulação de Mercadorias e Serviços – ICMS, do cálculo do PIS e da Cofins.




Subordinação dos policiais penais (ADI 7781, 07/10, 14h):

 Ação direta discute constitucionalidade da lei de São Paulo em subordinar a polícia penal à Secretaria de Segurança da Administração Penitenciária.




Cargos em Comissão (ADI 7512, 07/10, 14h):

 Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade questiona a validade da lei amazonense, Lei Estadual 3.147/2007, que estabelece 10% dos cargos em comissão para servidores de carreira.




Expurgos inflacionários (RE 1141156, 07/10, 14h):

 volta a julgamento recurso extraordinário que discute a validade da inclusão dos expurgos inflacionários na correção monetária de depósitos judiciais.




Adicional de Insalubridade (ADPF 1181, 07/10, 14h):

 Governo Estadual do Espírito Santo entra com ação contra decisão da Justiça do Trabalho em obrigar o governo a pagar adicional de insalubridade de 20% para merendeiras e auxiliares de serviços gerais terceirizados da rede pública de ensino.
















Agenda da semana da

 

Pública

 

é um serviço apresentado aos leitores, concebido com base nas informações dos portais da Câmara, Senado e STF.
