author: Bruno Fonseca
title: Como o agro e o interior podem explicar diminuição de votos para Lula
content:
O domingo do primeiro turno terminou com uma surpresa, ao menos para quem acompanhava a maioria das pesquisas eleitorais e também para os próprios candidatos. “Confesso que estava convencido de que iria ganhar no primeiro turno”, 

disse

 Lula ontem. O atual presidente marcou 3,3 milhões de votos a menos do que no primeiro turno de 2022, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro conseguiu 5 milhões de votos a mais que seu pai, Jair.




O resultado pode ser explicado por vários fatores: como a 

Agência Pública

 

mostrou

, 

escândalos políticos podem ter favorecido o desejo “antissistema” que – apesar de ser uma grande contradição –, é usado politicamente por Flávio e bolsonaristas.

 O caso do Master, inclusive, não foi capaz de impedir que muitos políticos diretamente citados nas investigações e vazamentos ligados ao banco 

conseguissem

 se reeleger. Isso inclui o próprio Flávio, investigado por suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro, corrupção e evasão de divisas em relação ao financiamento do filme Dark Horse, sobre seu pai. Flávio pediu dinheiro diretamente para Daniel Vorcaro, trocou dezenas de mensagens com o ex-banqueiro e marcou encontros com ele.




Além dos escândalos políticos, outras variáveis ajudam a entender a diminuição de votos de Lula e o crescimento de Flávio, e elas ficam evidentes no próprio mapa do Brasil. Levantamento de dados feito pelo cientista político Marco Antonio Faganello, pesquisador do Centro de Política e Economia do Setor Público da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV/CEPESP), mostra que 

Lula perdeu mais votos em municípios que não são capitais, e essa perda é ainda mais gritante em cidades menores onde a participação do agro na economia é grande.

 “Onde o agro está em mais de 50% no PIB, no conjunto, Lula perdeu 8% dos votos em relação a 2022”, aponta.




A análise de Faganello mostra que municípios pequenos do interior, com alto PIB per capita, proporção de moradores que se declaram brancos e jovens mais alta e com grande atividade agropecuária estão onde Lula mais perdeu votos proporcionalmente a 2022. É esse o tipo de perfil de vários municípios de Goiás, estado onde a diminuição dos votos para Lula foi a mais significativa na proporção com 2022.




O pesquisador também aponta que o Nordeste, apesar de ser um reduto tradicional de Lula e não ter registrado uma queda significativa nos votos para o atual presidente, foi onde Flávio mais avançou. “A direita cresceu nos nove estados do Nordeste. Flávio superou o resultado de Bolsonaro em 98% dos 1.794 municípios da região. No Nordeste, Lula perdeu poucos votos, mas a direita cresceu em todos os estados: de 27% para 30,9% dos votos válidos”, detalha.




Na entrevista, Faganello também avalia como a abstenção, apesar de ter sido recorde, não parece ter impactado a perda de votos de Lula no Brasil como um todo, com exceção de Salvador, onde a 

ausência de eleitores

 impactou a votação do petista. Além disso, para o pesquisador, a proporção de evangélicos entre a população pode não explicar essa mudança. Contudo, Faganello ressalta que ainda há dados que o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral deve divulgar que podem detalhar esses aspectos.




Confira os principais trechos da entrevista aqui.
















Marco Antonio Faganello é cientista político e pesquisador do Centro de Política e Economia do Setor Público da Fundação Getúlio Vargas (FGV/CEPESP)




Na sua análise, você conclui que Lula teve menos votos em 2026 em relação ao primeiro turno de 2022 em 98% dos municípios do Brasil. Mas isso aconteceu diferente nas cidades pequenas e nas capitais e também a partir de outros fatores, como atividade agropecuária. Você pode explicar melhor essa diferença?




Estamos falando em votação proporcional, isto é, no quanto os votos que foram para o Lula em 2022 aumentaram ou diminuíram em 2026, proporcionalmente. 

Os dados mostram que essa queda foi maior sobretudo nos pequenos municípios e nos municípios ligados ao agro, além de ter um recorte por região do país. São esses os três principais fatores: tamanho, agro e região.




Sobre o tamanho dos municípios, quanto menor, mais Lula perdeu votos em relação a 2022. Nos municípios com até 5 mil habitantes, ele perde cerca de 7% [comparando 2026 a 2022]. Nos com mais de 500 mil habitantes, ele perde só 1%.




É importante ressaltar que isso é uma faceta, porque se você olha pra outro lado, em números absolutos, esse contingente de municípios pequenos não contribui tanto para a diminuição dos votos do Lula.




Se você aumentar esse grupo para municípios com até 50 mil habitantes, você chega a 50% da perda de votos que Lula teve entre 2022 e 2026. Já por outro lado, o Flávio ganhou votos nesses mesmos municípios em que o Lula perdeu. Ou seja, o voto que o Lula perdeu foi pro Flávio.

 Os demais candidatos desidrataram demais, não chegaram a influenciar essa conta.


































Explique mais sobre esse recorte da presença do agro nos municípios. Você comparou a porcentagem da participação da atividade agropecuária no PIB municipal? Você pode citar alguns exemplos?




Isso, eu peguei a porcentagem da atividade agropecuária no PIB municipal. Para se ter uma ideia, 

em municípios onde essa porcentagem está em menos de 5% do PIB, Lula perdeu 2% no conjunto de votos. Mas onde o agro está em mais de 50% no PIB, no conjunto, Lula perdeu 8% dos votos em relação a 2022.

 Esses municípios pegam só 2% da população brasileira.




É interessante que, cruzando porte [da cidade] e agro, você vê que, nos municípios bem pequenos, de até 5 mil habitantes e que têm mais de 50% de PIB no agro, Lula perdeu 9% dos votos. Já entre os pequenos que têm menos de 5% do PIB no agro, Lula perdeu bem menos votos, menos de 4%. E essa perda de votos do Lula foi para o Flávio, não virou abstenção.




Isso levanta a hipótese de uma afinidade ideológica forte em municípios muito pequenos e com alta participação do agro. Uma pergunta ainda a se fazer é porque isso não pesou tanto em 2022 quanto em 2026.




E como a diferença entre as regiões do país e dos estados entra nessa conta?




No Sul e no Centro-Oeste foram onde aconteceram as maiores perdas de votos para Lula. Mas existe uma queda generalizada no país: parece que o que foi conquistado em 2022 se perdeu.




Foram 3 milhões de votos a menos que no primeiro turno de 2022. Não é uma flutuação gigantesca, mas nas últimas eleições é isso que tem acontecido, uma proporção de votos menor, que fica no meio, que fica flutuando. E quem decide a eleição são justamente essas pequenas flutuações.




E sobre a abstenção? Você aponta que ela não teve efeito na perda de votos para Lula. Por que?




A abstenção aparece como algo generalizado no país. Onde você teve mais abstenção, Lula não perdeu mais votos. 

A abstenção não parece ter relação nem com agro, nem com região do país.

 Ela bateu recorde em números absolutos, mas não foi uma variável que ajude a explicar a perda de votos de Lula.




Na sua análise, você aponta que o fator da religião evangélica não pesou nessa diminuição de votos do Lula. Por quê? E outros fatores, como entraram?




A porcentagem de evangélicos na população dos municípios não aponta uma mudança significativa de 2026 para 2022, Lula nem perdeu nem ganhou votos nas cidades a partir desse recorte – ele já não tinha [esses votos].




Já quanto mais jovem a população do município, mais o Lula perdeu votos. Quanto mais branco, também, e renda per capita do município também influencia. Quanto maior a renda, mais o Lula perdeu.




E teve uma diferença muito gritante entre capital e interior: Lula quase não perdeu nada na maioria das capitais, mas bastante em cidades que não são capitais.




Então dá pra dizer que entre os municípios onde o Lula mais perdeu votos existe um perfil comum? Municípios com grande participação do agro na economia, com população mais branca, mais jovem e com PIB per capita maior?




Sim.




E o contrário, onde o Flávio ganhou votos em relação a Jair?




O PL [votos para Flávio] ganhou 5 milhões em relação a 2022, em todo o país. E desse total de ganhos que o Flávio teve em 2026, 32% vieram do Nordeste. Foi onde ele mais avançou.




A direita cresceu nos nove estados do Nordeste. Flávio superou o resultado de Bolsonaro em 98% dos 1.794 municípios da região.

 No Nordeste, Lula perdeu poucos votos, mas a direita cresceu em todos os estados: de 27% para 30,9% dos votos válidos (mais 1,6 milhão de votos). O maior ganho, em pontos percentuais, foi no Ceará e no Maranhão.


































Você também aponta que o Lula cresceu em 102 municípios – há algum padrão nestas cidades?




Lula ganha mais percentualmente em municípios de regiões variadas, Sobral, no Ceará; Macapá, no Amapá; Belém, no Pará; Niterói, no Rio de Janeiro; Aracaju, em Sergipe; Recife, em Pernambuco; Santos, em São Paulo; Rio Branco, no Acre; Fortaleza, no Ceará; e até na cidade do Rio de Janeiro. No geral são cidades grandes e médias.




Já Lula perdeu mais em várias cidades de Goiás, ali perto de Rio Verde. Depois em municípios do Tocantins e do Rio Grande do Sul.




Olha que curioso: Lula perde mais [votos proporcionalmente] na Bahia, com 3,6%, que em São Paulo, 3% [entre 2026 e 2022].




Na Bahia, Salvador concentrou 38% da perda de votos de Lula no estado, mas só 6% do ganho da direita: 

em Salvador, Lula perdeu votos sobretudo porque menos gente votou.

 No interior, a direita cresceu com mais eleitores indo às urnas.

author: Unknown
title: AYM, Tayfun Kahraman kararının gerekçesini açıkladı, mahkemeyi uyardı: Yeniden yargılansın
content:
Anayasa Mahkemesi (AYM), Gezi Parkı davasında 18 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırılan Tayfun Kahraman’ın adil yargılanma ve bireysel başvuru haklarının ihlal edildiğine hükmederek yeniden yargılama yapılmasına ve Kahraman’a 100 bin TL manevi tazminat ödenmesine karar verdi. Kararı uygulamayan mahkemeyi uyaran AYM, "Kararların bağlayıcılığının sorgulanması ve uygulanmaması hukuk devletini işlemez hâle getirir, kaçınılmaz bir şekilde hukuk sistemini kaosa sürükler" dedi.

AYM, Temmuz 2025'te Kahraman'ın adil yargılanma hakkının ihlal edildiğine karar vermiş ve yeniden yargılama için kararı İstanbul 13. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi'ne göndermişti. Mahkeme, AYM'nin "yetki gasbı" yaptığını belirterek yeniden yargılama talebini reddetmişti. AYM, bu kez bireysel başvuru hakkının oybirliğiyle, hakkaniyete uygun yargılanma hakkının ise oyçokluğuyla ihlal edildiğine hükmetti ve yeniden yargılama için kararı aynı mahkemeye bir kez daha gönderdi. Kahraman’a ayrıca 100 bin TL manevi tazminat ödenmesine hükmedildi. Ödemenin Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığına başvurudan itibaren dört ay içinde yapılması, gecikme halinde yasal faiz uygulanması kararlaştırıldı.

Yeni Parti Grup Başkanvekili Gökhan Günaydın, AYM'nin kararının akıbeti benzer olan çok sayıda siyasi tutuklu için emsal teşkil ettiğini belirterek "Böylece Anayasa Mahkemesi, ilk derece mahkemesi niteliğindeki ağır ceza mahkemesine ve temyiz mercii olan Yargıtay’a bir kez daha Anayasa’yı hatırlatmış oldu" yorumunda bulundu.

title: Akın Gürlek'in "muhatap almadığı" ve dava gerekçesi yaptığı Ahmet Şık soruları
content:
Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek'in avukatı Abdullah Adır, Türkiye İşçi Partisi (TİP) İstanbul Milletvekili Ahmet Şık'ın Gürlek'le ilgili iddialarını destekleyen belge sunmadığını savunarak, hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunulduğunu ve tazminat davası açıldığını bildirdi.

Adır'ın açıklaması şöyle: "TİP Milletvekili Ahmet Şık'ın daha önce dile getirdiği iddialara ilişkin kendisinden somut bilgi ve belge sunması istenmiş; ancak bugüne kadar iddialarını destekleyen tek bir belge dahi ortaya konulamamıştır. Dayanaktan yoksun ve gerçeği yansıtmayan paylaşımları nedeniyle hakkında suç duyurusunda bulunulmuş ve tazminat davası açılmıştır. İddiasını ispat edemeyen bu müptezelin iftira ve hakaretleri tarafımızca muhatap alınmamaktadır. Gerekli cevap yalnızca hukuk önünde verilecektir. Kamuoyuna saygıyla duyurulur."

Ahmet Şık, 26 Eylül'de X hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda "Akın Gürlek, tutuklu şüphelilerden E.Tezmen ve M.Yarız ile tutuksuz E. Özel ile Adalet Bakan Yardımcılığı döneminden bugüne kadar 2024, 2025, 2026'da İstanbul’daki belirli otellerde kaç kez görüşmüştür? Görüşmelerin tarihleri, yerleri, amaçları ve içerikleri nelerdir?" sorusunu sormuştu.

Şık ayrıca New York'taki BM Genel Kurulu sırasında çekilen bir fotoğrafı paylaşarak "Geçen hafta New York’taki BM toplantısı sırasında çekilen bu fotoğrafta, solda Akın Gürlek’in yanında duran kişi fon soygunu soruşturmasında hakkında yakalama kararı bulunan Bilal Çalışkan" demişti.

Ahmet Şık son olarak bugün Ahmet Saymadi'nin kendisiyle olan dostluğu ve ortaklığı yüzünden hedef alınarak tutuklandığını söyledi ve Gürlek'e şu soruları yöneltti:

“Off shore bağlantılı hesaplarla ilişkili sizin, sair akraba ve efradınız ile yakın çevrenizde bulunan bazı isimler üzerine yurtdışında kurulu tabela şirketleriniz var mı? Bu şirketler üzerinden 'yurtdışı yatırımcısı' perdelemesiyle fon soygunu soruşturmasında adı geçen portföy yatırım şirketlerinden yüklü miktarlarda işlemler yapılmış mıdır? Fon soygunu ortaya çıkmadan birkaç ay önce Tera Portföy yönetim şirketine manipülatif işlemler nedeniyle yaklaşık 9 milyon ceza kesen SPK yönetimi sonrasında bu vurgunu önleyici/denetleyici hiçbir işlem yapmadı. Eğer menfaat ilişkisi yoksa en hafifinden “görevi ihmal/kötüye kullanma” suçlamasından şüpheli olan ve bu tür soygunları önleyici/denetleyici kurum olan SPK yönetiminde eşiniz varken sizin soruşturmayı yürüten yargının başında olmanız çıkar çatışması değil midir? Fon soygunu soruşturmasının tutuklu şüphelileri Emre Tezmen, Muhammed Yarız ve Erdin Özel ile Adalet Bakan Yardımcılığı döneminden bugüne kadar 2024, 2025, 2026'da İstanbul’daki belirli otellerde görüştünüz mü? Görüşmelerin tarihleri, yerleri, amaçları ve içerikleri nelerdir? Yeni Parti Genel Başkanı Özgür Özel, üzerinize kayıtlı olduğunu öne sürdüğü 16 ayrı taşınmaz olduğunu açıkladı. Yaptığınız açıklamada 4 tapunuz olduğunu söylediniz. Ancak geçmişten bugüne kadar yaptığınız tüm taşınmaz alım satımların hepsini içere pasif tapu kayıtlarını açıklayacak mısınız? İlgili bakanlıktan bu pasif kayıtların silinmesini talep ettiniz mi? İlgili bakanlıktaki üst düzey yetkiliden “200 yıldır silinemedi dolayısıyla silinmesi imkânsız” yanıtı aldınız mı? Danışmanlığınızı yapan Furkan Torlak’ın, Mehmet Kap sahte kimliğiyle trol+medya manipülasyon çetesiyle birlikte işlediği suçlardan haberiniz var mı?”

Geçen hafta NewYork’taki BM toplantısı sırasında çekilen bu fotoğrafta, solda Akın Gürlek’in yanında duran kişi fon soygunu soruşturmasında hakkında yakalama kararı bulunan Bilal Çalışkan. https://t.co/nJ5PF5FVf2

title: Israel Bans Polanski After UK’s Green Party Votes to Classify Zionism as Racism
content:
The Green Party motion also calls for a single state in historic Palestine with equal rights for all.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On Sunday, the United Kingdom’s Green Party passed a motion defining Zionism as a form of racism. Within hours of the vote, Israel’s foreign ministry responded, slamming the motion and barring Green Party leader Zack Polanski from entering Israel.

“The Greens have adopted not only the green of Hamas, but also its ideology: the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle,” Israel’s foreign ministry posted on X, speciously comparing the left-wing British political party to the Palestinian resistance group.

The foreign ministry also called on the U.K.’s Labour Party to denounce the motion.

The motion passed at the Green Party’s annual conference on Sunday in a vote of 1,022 to 813. In addition to denouncing Zionism, it calls for a single state in historic Palestine with equal rights for all, with the right of return for Palestinians. The motion also acknowledges the right of Palestinians to resist, and reasserts the Green Party’s commitment to the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) campaign and a total arms embargo.

Israeli politicians from various political parties smeared the motion.

“Those who claim the antisemitic lie that ‘Zionism is racism’ deliberately endanger Jews and Israelis everywhere,” Israeli President Isaac Herzog posted on X after its passage.

Opposition leader Yair Lapid wrote on social media that “the UK Green Party has chosen to side with terrorists and antisemites” as Israel prepares to mark three years since the October 7 attack.

Notably, the vote was passed through the rank-and-file membership — which has nearly tripled in size over the past year since the election of Green Party Leader Zack Polanski and left-wing voters leaving the Labour Party over its stance on Gaza. But Polanski himself did not vote on the motion, and other Green Party leaders distanced themselves from the motion.

Backlash has also emerged within the U.K., including from members of the Labour Party — some of whom are calling on Labour leader Andy Burnham to rule out forming a coalition with the Greens.

This is not surprising, Charlie Hore, a socialist activist in the U.K., explained to Truthout — but it ignores the fact that the Palestine solidarity movement has transformed U.K. politics.

“At the Labour Party conference earlier this month, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband was forced to say that the Labour government had gotten Gaza wrong. What forced that is the massive shift in public opinion in the last couple of years in favor of Palestine and against Israel,” explained Hore.

The solidarity movement, and widespread shift in opinion, has also been credited as key to the Labour government imposing sanctions on Israeli settlements last month.

“Every major party in British politics supports the state of Israel, despite the occasional criticism,” Hore said. “The Greens have chosen the side of Palestine, and that’s going to be a good thing for taking the Palestine solidarity movement forward.”

We now have three full months of data since Google changed its search to feature AI results. The numbers are worse than we anticipated. Overall readership that comes to Truthout through Google is down 54 percent against last year. The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

The only way we can keep publishing is with strong reader support. We are asking you to start a monthly donation to Truthout today — anything you can do, whether $5 or $25, makes a difference.

author: Unknown
title: Fransa: Liseliler, üniversitelileri ve işçileri yanlarına alarak sokağa dönüyor
content:
Fransa’da liselerden yükselen isyan sokağa çıkıyor: İşçiler öğrencilerin yanına geliyor. Fransa salı günü son on yılların en büyük lise öğrenci hareketinin yeni aşamasına hazırlanıyor.




21 Eylül’de Paris’in güneydoğusundaki Créteil’de Saint-Exupéry Lisesi öğrencileri, veliler ve öğretmenlerin, öğretmen kadrolarındaki açıklara karşı başlattıkları eylem on günde ülkeye yayıldı. 1 Ekim’de 1.027 lise eylemlerden etkilendi, 222 okul bloke edildi. Pazartesi günü de 400-500 okulda dersler tamamen ya da kısmen durdu.




Ancak hareketin çıkış noktası katılım sayılarından daha dikkat çekici: Protestolar, Fransa’da 1968’den bu yana öğrenci hareketleriyle özdeşleşmiş olan üniversitelerden değil liselerden; Paris’in merkezinden değil, işçi ve göçmen nüfusun yoğun olduğu banliyölerden başladı.




Üniversiteler harekete, başladıktan sonra katıldı. Şimdi işçi sendikaları geliyor.




Bir reforma değil okul hayatına isyan




Hareketi tetikleyen belli başlı bir yasa tasarısı, hükümet kararı ya da bir öğrenci örgütünün gündeme getirdiği merkezi bir talepler listesi yok.




Öğrenciler öğretmen istiyor. Kalabalık sınıflardan, değişmeyen öğretmenlerden, ağır ders programlarından, personel eksikliğinden, eski ve sağlıksız binalardan şikâyet ediyor. Üniversiteye girişte öğrencileri eleyen seçme ve yerleştirme düzeneği Parcoursup ise gelecek kaygısının cisim leşmiş simgelerinin başında geliyor. 




Sorunlar, yılların birikimiyle ortaya çıkıyor. Halen Fransa'da kamu ortaöğretim okullarında 2008’e göre

 

250 bin daha fazla öğrenci, buna karşılık daha az öğretmen var. Genel ve fen liselerinde sınıfların yüzde 70’inden çoğunda öğrenci sayısı 30’dan fazla. Öğretmenlerin on beş günü aşan devamsızlıklarının telafi edilemediği durumlar 2018-2024 arasında iki katına çıktı. Okul binalarının ortalama yaşı 61, meslek liselerinde bu 71'i buluyor.




Fransa, daha fazla genci daha uzun süre eğitim sisteminde tutarken, kitleselleşmenin gerektirdiği ölçüde öğretmen, personel ve altyapıyı sağlayamadı.




1968’in tersine: Üniversite sakin, liseler ayakta




Mayıs 1968, Nanterre Üniversitesi’nden Sorbonne’a, oradan liselere ve milyonlarca işçinin grevine yayılmıştı. 2026’da güzergâh tersine dönüyor: Liseler başı çekiyor, üniversiteler onları izliyor, işçi sendikaları desteğe geliyor. 




Fransa'nın ciddi günlük gazetesi Le Monde da, kendisinden önce bir üniversite hareketi olmaksızın liselerde kendiliğinden doğmasının hareketin ayırt edici özelliklerinden biri olduğuna dikkat çekiyor. Eylemler yalnızca genel liselerde değil, fen liselerinde ve meslek liselerinde de görülüyor.




Toplumsal tabakalaşma büyüdü




Aradan geçen yarım yüzyılda Fransa'da yükseköğretim kitleselleşti, ancak toplumsal eleme yok olmadı. 2024-25’te yükseköğretim öğrencilerinin yüzde 36,1’i yönetici ve üst düzey entelektüel meslek sahibi ailelerden gelirken, işçi çocuklarının oranı yüzde 9,1’di. Seçkin yükseköğretim kurumlarına çıkıldıkça makas da açılıyor.  Grandes écoles (Büyük Okullar) denilen Fransa’nın seçkin yükseköğretim kurumlarına hazırlık sınıfları CPGE’lerde makas daha da büyük yüzde 50’ye karşı yüzde 6,4.




Devlet üniversitelerinin nispeten düşük harçları da öğrenciliğin maliyetini ortadan kaldırmıyor. Barınma, beslenme ve gündelik yaşam giderlerini ailelerinin karşılamadığı gençler için üniversite aynı zamanda eğitim masrafları için ücretli çalışma anlamına geliyor.




Üniversiteye girişteki rekabet de Parcoursup aracılığıyla lise yıllarına kadar inmiş durumda. 2024'te gerçekleştirilen bir araştırmada gençlerin yüzde 77’si Parcoursup’un kendilerinde stres yarattığını söylemişlerdi. 




Dolayısıyla 2026’nın liseli isyanı 1968’in tekrarı değil. Kendi koşullarından kaynaklanıyor. Üniversiteyi daha seçici, mesleğe yönelik ve öngörülebilir kılan mekanizmalar, eğitim sistemindeki rekabetin ve gelecek kaygısının bir bölümünü daha genç yaştakilere, liselilerin arasına taşımış görünüyor.




Bugünün lisesi geleceğin üniversite öğrencisini de, işçisini de, teknisyenini de, işsizini de aynı çatı altında topluyor.




Sokağa önce öğrenciler çıktı, örgütler arkadan geldi




Başbakan Sébastien Lecornu, öğrencileri sokağa Boyun Eğmeyen Fransa (La France insoumise, LFI) Partisi ve “aşırı sol” çevrelerin yönlendirdiğini ileri sürdü.




Paris Polis Müdürlüğü İstihbarat Dairesi (DRPP) raporu, yalnızca Seine-Saint-Denis ilçesinde bulunan  yaklaşık 20 lise çevresindeki olaylara dayanarak öğrencilerin “aşırı sol unsurlar” tarafından eyleme itildiği yargısını ortaya atıyor. Oysa o sırada ülke çapında 1.027 lisede eylem vardı. Ancak Raporu inceleme imkanı bulan Le Monde gazetesinin rapor üzerindeki incelemesi, sol örgütlerin liselerde merkezi olarak örgütledikleri bir hareketten çok, zaten başlamış dağınık harekete sol örgütlerin dahil olmaya çalıştıklarını gösteriyor.




Kronoloji de aynı buna denk düşüyor: Önce öğrenciler sokağa çıktı; hareket diğer liselere yayıldı; öğrenci örgütleri, siyasi yapılar ve sendikalar daha sonra ağırlıklarını koydu.




CGT öğrencilere kapılarını açtı




Genel İş Konfederasyonu’nun (Confédération générale du travail-CGT) gençlik hareketlerine desteği yeni bir durum değil. Ancak konfederasyon bu kez yalnızca dayanışma açıklaması yapmakla kalmadı. Yerel örgütlerinden öğrencilere sendika mekânlarını açmalarını, gösterilerin düzenlenmesine ve güvenliğine yardımcı olmalarını ve gerektiğinde grev hakkını kullanmalarını istedi.




CGT çağrısını şu cümleyle gerekçelendirdi:







“Bugünün lise ve üniversite öğrencileri yarının işçileridir.”







Bu, 1968’le karşılaştırıldığında ayrıca anlamlı. O dönemde Fransız Komünist Partisi ve CGT başlangıçta üniversite radikalizmine kuşkuyla yaklaşmıştı. 2026’da CGT, kendisinin başlatmadığı lise hareketinin önüne geçmek yerine örgütlü işçi hareketinin mekânlarını ve kapasitesini gençlerin arkasına koyuyor.




6 Ekim’de eğitim sendikaları da greve ve gösterilere katılacak.




Polis müdahalesi yeni bir çatışma yarattı




Hareketin başlangıçtaki eğitimden kaynaklanan taleplerine kısa sürede baskı altındaki gösteri hakkı da eklendi. Uluslararası Af Örgütü Fransa Şubesi, reşit olmayan öğrencilere karşı aşırı güç kullanıldığına ilişkin bir uyarıda bulundu. Bazı göstericilerin şiddete başvurduğunu da kayda geçiren örgüt, bunun barışçıl göstericilere ayrım gözetmeden müdahaleyi haklı çıkarmadığını vurguladı.




Hareket boyunca 5 binden fazla kişi gözaltına alındı; 

Le Monde

’un aktardığı verilere göre 180 öğrenci yaralandı. Saint-Ouen-l’Aumône’da 14 yaşındaki bir öğrenci, yüzüne yakın mesafeden bombaatar kullanılması sonucu çenesinden yaralandı ve dişlerini kaybetti. Buna karşılık 24 lisede tahribat ya da yangın meydana geldi, 78 personel yaralandı.




Balkondan öğrencilere silah




Gerilim polis müdahalesiyle sınırlı kalmadı. Caen’ın Grâce-de-Dieu mahallesinde bir kadın apartman balkonundan protestocu gençlere silah doğrulttu. Kadının daha sonra polise teslim ettiği silahın taklit olduğu belirlendi. Bir grup gencin saldırdığını düşündüğü bir kızı korumaya çalıştığını söyledi ve özür diledi.




Fakat aşağıdaki öğrencilerin bunu bilmeleri mümkün değildi: “Silahın taklit olup olmadığını bilmiyoruz.” dediler. Caen’daki görüntüler, lise boykotlarının toplumun bir kesiminde karşılaştığı tahammülsüzlüğün uç örneklerinden biri oldu.




6 Ekim’de ne sınanacak?




İki hafta önce Créteil’de boş öğretmen kadrolarına karşı başlayan Salı gününe üç dinamiği yan yana getirmiş olarak giriyor: liselilerin eğitim ve gelecek talepleri, onlarla dayanışma içindeki eski liseliler, üniversite öğrencileri ve polis müdahalelerine karşı tepki olarak örgütlü işçi hareketinin açtığı destek hattı.




6 Ekim  Fransa için yalnızca kaç lisede derslerin durdurulduğunun izlendiği  yeni bir protesto günü olmakla kalmayacak. Büyük ölçüde kendi dinamiğiyle ortaya çıkan lise hareketinin üniversite öğrencileri ve örgütlü işçi hareketiyle buluştuğunda eğitim protestosunun ötesinde bir içeriğe bürünüp bürünmediği de görülecek.




(AEK)

author: Edith Romero
title: ICE Jail Policies for Pregnant People Built on Legacy of Eugenics, Critics Say
content:
A record number of pregnant women and teenagers have been arrested by ICE. They cannot access medical care they need.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

While detained at Michigan’s North Lake Processing Center, Lucia learned she was pregnant — a nightmare scenario for her and many other women who are held in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody while pregnant.

“I prayed every day for God to take care of my little angel,” said Lucia, who is using a pseudonym for fear of retaliation and harm.

Originally from Venezuela, Lucia left the political turmoil of her home country in 2022 as the COVID-19 pandemic also abruptly ended her ability to study nursing.

“I left because I was looking for a better future,” she said.

She was in the U.S. for three years before the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) rescinded Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for multiple countries, including Venezuela, in February 2025. An ICE traffic stop that year in Detroit landed Lucia in detention, just weeks after her partner was also detained by ICE.

Lucia was transferred to four different detention centers before arriving at the South Louisiana Processing Center in Basile, Louisiana. She described her time there as “horrible.”

“I saw many high-risk pregnancies,” Lucia said.

Her own pregnancy was classified as high-risk due to a previous miscarriage. Lucia told Prism that she met dozens of pregnant women while in detention.

“I saw a woman who gave birth,” she said. “I saw her in a wheelchair with her newborn crying, and a nurse was taking her somewhere. I never saw her or her baby again.”

A recent investigation from The Guardian corroborated Lucia’s claims. ICE is arresting a record number of pregnant women and teenagers who cannot access the medical care they need, according to the reporting. At the same time, the agency appears to have lost count of how many people had miscarriages after October 2025.

In an emailed statement to Prism, a DHS representative said that “being in detention is a choice” and that “pregnancy in ICE detention is exceedingly rare.” The spokesperson also alleged that pregnant women receive regular prenatal visits, mental health services, and nutritional support.

“Claims that there are subprime conditions at ICE detention centers are false,” the representative said. “For many illegal aliens this is the best healthcare they have received their entire lives.”

According to experts and advocates, the racist cruelty and abusive immigration policies women in ICE detention face are built on a legacy of eugenics, an ideology that aimed to “improve” the human population based on white supremacy.

Often referred to as “Basile,” the South Louisiana Processing Center is the single women-only immigrant detention center in the state. In July, videos created by women detained at the facility went viral, exposing inhumane conditions and alleging sexual abuse.

Basile is located in rural Louisiana and has an extensive history of denying migrants access to food, interpreters, and medical care. The facility is 1 of 10 ICE detention centers in Louisiana, known as the “incarceration capital” of the U.S. for having the county’s highest rates of incarceration.

Documents from DHS released earlier this year further corroborated Lucia’s account of meeting a large number of pregnant women in detention.

According to government records, ICE detained approximately 498 pregnant, postpartum, or nursing immigrants between Jan. 1, 2025, and Feb. 16, 2026. The detention of pregnant people shows an alarming shift away from Biden-era policies that required their immediate release from federal custody.

Louisiana is often at the center of allegations of reproductive injustice in detention. Over the last year alone, detained women in the state have made serious allegations of medical neglect and sexual abuse. This includes the case of a Jane Doe, who alleged last year that she was sexually abused and threatened by Manuel Reyes, Basile’s former assistant warden. Trans immigrants have also alleged that Reyes “ran an off-the-books late-night work scheme” that coerced them into “physically and psychologically painful labor.”

For women detained at Basile, it can be difficult to separate fact from fiction, due to ICE’s extensive history of malpractice and dishonesty.

Lucia told Prism that this reality, paired with the everyday mistreatment of detained immigrants, has fueled an environment that is full of medical mistrust. As an example, when she was first detained at Basile, she said that women inside instructed her not to accept any vaccines or medications from the medical staff because they would “make you miscarry.” Because Prism would not reveal Lucia’s identity to DHS, the agency said it could not comment on any of her claims.

Allegations of medical abuse have been documented at other detention centers. For example, in 2020 at the Irwin County Detention Center, ICE contracted an OB-GYN named Mahendra Amin to provide care to detained women. He was later found to have carried out invasive and unnecessary gynecological procedures on detained women without their full and informed consent.

The mistreatment of pregnant people in detention was a daily reality that also shaped the views of women inside, according to Lucia. She said she once witnessed guards push a pregnant woman into solitary confinement, where she remained for several days.

“She was crying and telling me to please talk to an officer. She had gone three days without food,” Lucia recalled.

ICE did not respond to requests for comment and neither did GEO Group, the private prison company in charge of Basile.

GEO Group profits tremendously from overseeing a vast network of ICE’s detention centers. In August, GEO Group reported total revenues of up to $732.1 million — an increase of nearly $96 million — over the same period last year. President Donald Trump owns stock in GEO Group and other private prison companies financially benefiting from his immigration policies. A GEO Group subsidiary even donated more than $1.4 million to Trump’s political operation in July after his administration awarded the company detention contracts amounting to $165 million a year.

The money flowing from the detention system does not improve the healthcare detained migrants receive, according to Lucia and immigrant rights advocates.

Lucia said she was allowed just one prenatal medical visit during the four months she was detained in Louisiana. Medical services for pregnant people are typically accessed off-site, as detention centers do not employ OB-GYNs as staffers. According to Denáe Hebert, a medical advocacy program volunteer with the grassroots organization Louisiana Advocates for Immigrants in Detention, healthcare providers at nearby hospitals told her that a guard must be present during all appointments with detained immigrants. This is one of the detention system’s many overlaps with the carceral system.

In both settings, Hebert said having a guard in the exam room obliterates any possibility of confidentiality between the patient and their medical provider. Even more troubling, Hebert said, is that detained people likely don’t receive even a fraction of the healthcare they need. Hebert told Prism that she’d heard rumors from people detained in Basile that ICE has refused to pay for at least one person’s surgery.

Last year, DHS left thousands of medical claims unpaid when the agency abruptly ended its payment processing system for outside providers. Hebert and other advocates fear that this has delayed critical medical services for detained immigrants. An investigation from the Los Angeles Times detailed 2,267 unpaid DHS and ICE medical claims from last year, most of them related to pregnancy and maternal care.

“These are for-profit detention facilities,” Hebert said. “When you create an environment where that is the structure, it necessitates poor treatment. The primary objective is saving and making money, not doing what is best for the people within those facilities.”

A system that allows private prison companies to financially benefit from detention, and detains immigrants in remote areas with little outside oversight, is poised to usher in human rights abuses, said Alexandra Minna Stern, the author of “Eugenic Nation: Faults and Frontiers of Better Breeding in Modern America” and UCLA’s dean of the humanities.

The eugenics movement began in the 19th century with British scientist Francis Galton, who believed the burgeoning field of heredity should be used to control human populations so that they could “be better,” Stern said. What constituted “better,” according to Stern, was based on ableism and racial hierarchies.

By the 20th century, the eugenics movement was global. The U.S. eugenics movement shaped sterilization campaigns and immigration laws. However, as Public Health Post reported, forced sterilization is “not a relic of our distant past.” California, a trailblazer in the eugenics movement, forcibly sterilized 150 incarcerated women between 2006 and 2010. Stern’s Sterilization and Social Justice Lab, which for 10 years studied eugenic sterilization in the U.S. during the 20th century, informed the historic California reparations bill that compensated survivors.

Immigrants’ legitimate mistrust of healthcare providers and institutions speaks to broader, historical reproductive injustices against Black and Brown communities, according to advocates.

For centuries, women of color have been the target of eugenics. This includes enslavers’ reproductive violence against African women during the early colonial period until chattel slavery was abolished in 1865, the mass sterilization of Puerto Ricans through the 1960s, and eugenics policies that sterilized Mexican women in California and Indigenous women nationwide through the 1970s.

Women who were detained at Basile while pregnant told Prism that they were regularly berated by guards; forced to wear shackles on their wrists, hands, belly, and feet; and were made to eat inedible food that, in Lucia’s case, made her vomit. They also reported a lack of language access, adding to their isolation.

Experts have long said that detention is dangerous for women’s health, especially for those who are pregnant. Not only can psychological stress affect health during pregnancy, but ICE has a documented practice of subjecting women to unsafe conditions and denying prenatal care.

Lucia still remembers comforting a friend who miscarried while detained.

“She slept in the same block as I did. We would talk, and we would touch each other’s belly,” Lucia recalled. “She lost her baby, and it was her first pregnancy at 22 years old.”

Miriam, who is using a pseudonym for fear of retaliation, is a Nicaraguan doula and organizer with Louisiana’s Southeast Dignity Not Detention Coalition (SEDND Coalition) that supports people impacted by detention. She told Prism that she has witnessed abuse and eugenic harm — and not only in detention.

Lucia was in her 20s and still pregnant when she was released from ICE custody. For the remainder of her pregnancy, Miriam supported her as a doula and interpreter. This included several instances when Miriam said she had to intervene during medical appointments because staff at the local public hospital repeatedly asked Lucia if she wanted a tubal ligation, even after she said no. Miriam said that medical staff again brought up the procedure after Lucia gave birth.

“I thought: Are you offering this to any of your white patients, or is this just because she’s a younger, Brown woman?” Miriam said.

According to Lucia, being an immigrant and monolingual Spanish speaker from a Latin American country only seemed to worsen the treatment women received in healthcare settings. This was especially true in the detention system, she said.

“I remember a woman who needed a translator being berated by an officer for not eating fast enough. He threatened to throw her plate in anger,” Lucia said.

According to Stern, the eugenics movement has always operated in lockstep with immigration law. The professor attributed “nativist” restrictive immigration policy in the early 20th century to eugenic ideals of racial purity in the U.S. However, Stern noted, “nativist” is a misnomer because white Anglo-Saxon elites were not native to the U.S.

“Nativism and eugenics co-created each other, and they worked hand in hand,” Stern said, citing the 1917 Immigration Act as a policy directly shaped by eugenic goals. The law distinguished between “classes of aliens” who were “defective” and thus, should be excluded from admission to the U.S.

In “Eugenic Nation,” Stern also characterizes the earliest forms of border enforcement, carried out by the U.S. Public Health Service (USPHS), as a “eugenic endeavor.” In 1917, this included harsh quarantine measures such as kerosene baths that USPHS forced upon Mexican migrants traversing the Texas-Mexico border. Under the guise of “defending Texas” from “infected and disease-ridden Mexicans,” USPHS officials also enforced physical examinations and brandings with permanent ink. Today, medical examinations are still required as part of immigration proceedings.

Fatima Khan, a New Orleans-based immigration lawyer who previously represented detained immigrants in Louisiana, cites the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882 as another example of anti-immigrant policies operating in unison with eugenic projects. For a time, the law banned Chinese migration to the U.S.

“The underlying tone was that the people who were coming to America really did want to control the makeup of the society, and it went down to race, but also religion, values, and land ownership,” Khan explained.

Like many before her, Khan traces the origins of laws related to racial superiority and migration to the trafficking of enslaved Africans.

“We can’t deny that this is baked into it,” Khan said. “We know that the criminal legal systems, especially in the South, developed from slave patrols.” Today, criminal and immigration law are so enmeshed, there’s a phrase for it: crimmigration. The overlap in these systems is perhaps most apparent in the hundreds of 287(g) agreements local law enforcement agencies have entered into with ICE, allowing them to carry out immigration enforcement.

Today, eugenics rhetoric is easy to spot in immigration discourse at the highest levels of government.

For example, Trump continues to challenge birthright citizenship and has publicly stated that immigrants are “coming in with bad genes.” Khan said these racist and xenophobic dog whistles are the same as those perpetuated by eugenics and racist movements focused on racial purity.

Over hundreds of years, eugenics transformed into policy, practice, and law, as illustrated by today’s immigration quotas, surveillance systems, detention centers, and instances of modern-day slavery.

Hebert told Prism that detention centers, along with the policies and laws that shape immigration enforcement and mass incarceration, are “inherently eugenicist.”

“Folks are demonized solely because they weren’t born here, and they don’t have whatever paperwork the current administration deems that they should have,” the volunteer said.

With no human rights framework guiding their treatment, women in detention have found ways to affirm their humanity and show care for each other.

Lucia said that in detention, women were given a meager amount of toiletries intended to last the whole month but were never enough. The women often banded together to buy hygiene items they could share, and they combed and styled each other’s hair.

These are just small examples of solidarity between detained women, moments that were plentiful and brave in the face of cruelty and dehumanization.

Hebert told Prism that volunteers routinely see women translating for each other during visitation or when filling out forms, writing letters, or talking to officers.

“We’ve seen cases where folks are so ill or in so much pain that they’re not able to care of themselves … and folks who are detained with them will assist them, walking them to the bathroom and helping them shower or bringing them food,” Hebert said.

Similarly, when Miriam visits detention centers in Louisiana and Mississippi as a representative of the SEDND Coalition, she routinely encounters detained people who ask for help for those they’ve become friends with inside. More broadly, detained people show each other care by sharing resources, being a listening ear, forming networks, organizing hunger strikes, and even helping their friends inside who are struggling with suicidal ideation.

In an immigration system structured to divide people and destroy their care for each other, detained women such as Lucia banding together and taking care of each other can be an act of courage and a vision for the future.

It’s easier for Lucia to be joyful now that she is free from the literal and figurative shackles of detention.

“When I got out, I felt so happy because I had my son in my belly, and I thank God that I am out of that detention center. I never wish this on anyone, I never want to go back,” said Lucia. During an interview in February, the young mother smiled as she sat at her dining room table with her giggling 8-month-old son, the two of them now far removed from the harm they endured.

After her release from detention when she was seven months pregnant, Lucia gave birth in Louisiana and has since raised her child in the state. However, at the time of publication, she was making arrangements to return to Venezuela with her American citizen son. Many of the friends she made at Basile remain detained.

Louisiana remains the center of detention and incarceration systems in the U.S. An investigation from the New Orleans-based nonprofit newsroom The Lens found that ICE apprehensions in Louisiana are at an all-time high. And in the deportation hub of Alexandria, a family detention center was recently approved to move forward on contaminated land. The SEDND Coalition and other groups are fighting the project while providing support to people currently detained in the state.

Louisiana’s newly approved family detention center, which will detain mothers alongside their young children, brings eugenics to the forefront once again.

Miriam, who is organizing against the family detention center, said that after centuries of eugenics, any hope for justice requires dismantling the idea that immigrant families and women of color’s reproductive choices are problems “that need to be managed.”

For families such as Lucia’s who have survived these systems, it’s perhaps more difficult to envision the long arc of justice. She can think only of the pregnant women who remain locked behind bars and the freedom they desperately yearn for.

”They have to have faith that they will get out,” she said, “that all women everywhere get to be free. … That is what is important.”

Prism is an independent and nonprofit newsroom led by journalists of color. We report from the ground up and at the intersections of injustice.

title: Quebec election day goes smoothly in Nunavik, officials say
content:
Officials say voting in the Ungava riding during Quebec’s provincial election is unfolding with no issues — a stark contrast from the 2025 federal election.




Polling stations are open in every community in the region, with two elections officers in each community, said Élections Québec spokesperson Julie St-Arnaud-Drolet in an email on Monday.




From Sept. 26 to Sept. 30, the advance polling dates in Nunavik, election staff helped residents get on the electors list to participate in the election, she said.




Election staff also recruited and trained locals to run the election, she added.




“In most communities, they were able to hire local residents; as a result, voters have access to services in Inuktitut today, on election day,” she said.




Kuujjuaq deputy Mayor Claude Gadbois said the voting process was smooth in his community.




“Everything seems to be under control,” Gadbois told Nunatsiaq News over Facebook on Monday afternoon.
















During the 2025 federal election, some 

Nunavimmiut were unable to cast ballots

. On election day in April, polling stations in two communities did not open at all, while seven others had reduced hours.




Elections Canada released a report last November that said a lack of planning and almost no local outreach were responsible for the problems.




The polls for the 2026 provincial election close at 8 p.m. Monday. Five candidates are 

running

 in Ungava, Quebec’s largest riding by geography.




Voters can cast their ballot from their village’s municipal office, except for those in Kuujjuaraapik, who must go to the community’s cultural centre.

title: Nie żyje Oskar Kasperek – obdżektor, artysta, anarchista
content:
Nie żyje Oskar Kasperek (ur. 1960), artysta grafik (absolwent PWSSP), anarchista, obdżektor (spędził prawie dwa lata w więzieniu za odmowę służby wojskowej w czasach PRL-u).  Był twórcą loga Międzymiastówki Anarchistycznej i Federacji Anarchistycznej. W Poznaniu prowadził pracownię graficzną Weksla na skłocie Od:zysk. Jego grafiki, także w formie szablonów odbijanych na murach można było zobaczyć na ulicach różnych miast. Przez pewien czas mieszkaniec skłotu Rozbrat.













Przyjaciołom, rodzinie i bliskim przesyłamy nasze kondolencje.

title: “Μύρισε θάνατος στις Σκουριές”, Κάλεσμα της Επιτροπής Αγώνα της Μ. Παναγιάς και κάλεσμα σε συγκέντρωση τη Πέμπτη 8/10, ενόψει των εγκαινίων του μεταλλείου
content:
Ανακοίνωση της Επιτροπής Αγώνα Μεγάλης Παναγιάς και κάλεσμα σε συγκέντρωση την Πέμπτη 8/10, στις 09.00, στο Χοντρό δέντρο ενάντια στα εγκαίνια του μεταλλείου της El Dorado στις Σκουριές, που θα λάβουν χώρα την ίδια μέρα παρουσία του πρωθυπουργού Κυριάκου Μητσοτάκη.




(Χοντρό Δέντρο είναι η διασταύρωση πάνω στον κεντρικό, όπου ξεκινάει ο δρόμος που ανεβαίνει στο βουνό προς το μεταλλείο.)




Επιτροπή Αγώνα Μεγάλης Παναγιάς:




“Μύρισε θάνατος




Αφήστε μας να σας ξεναγήσουμε και πάλι στην παρακμοχώρα της ΒΑ χαλκιδικής, στο σκοτεινό βασίλειο των μεταλλείων της Εldorado, εκεί όπου οι δυνάμεις του σκότους έχουν συνομωτήσει για την κονόμα, ένας σκοπός για να τους ενώνει πάντα.




Κυρίες και κύριοι, για μία και μοναδική εμφάνιση, την Πέμπτη 8 Οκτωβρίου, στο εργοτάξιο των Σκουριών, τα μπαλέτα της Eldorado, θα παρουσιάσουν το ντεμπούτο τους: 




“Εγκαίνια του μεταλλείου των Σκουριών ή Μύρισε Θάνατος”.




Την βρομερή δυσωδία θα πλαισιώσει στον ρόλο της πρίμα μπαλαρίνας, ο γνωστός για τις σκοτεινές του χορογραφίες, Κυριάκος Μητσοτάκης και οι χορευτές του. Σε ρόλο σαλτιμπάγκου γελωτοποιού ο δήμαρχος Βαλιάνος ενώ τους λοιπούς αυλικούς θα υποδυθούν οι ντόπιοι αιρετοί και κομματικοί παρατρεχάμενοι.




Το θέαμα περιλαμβάνει, εκτός από σεμινάρια του τύπου “μαθαίνω να γλείφω κοκαλάκια”, και ξεκοιλιασμένα δάση, στερευμένες πηγές, σκοτωμένους μεταλλωρύχους, χωριά ζόμπι, έρμαια στην διχόνοια και την ένοχη σιωπή, πεδία πια ψυχικής έρευνας και κοινωνικής παρακμής. Την μαγική ατμόσφαιρα ολοκληρώνει το πέπλο της αιωρούμενης αμιαντούχας σκόνης, που υπόσχονται ότι θα μας αγκαλιάσει απαλά σαν σάβανο.




Επειδή όμως οι παραστάσεις δεν έχουν ουσία χωρίς το ευρύ κοινό και η συγκεκριμένη θα παίζεται καθημερινά στις δικές μας ζωές, εμείς θα παραβρεθούμε και ας μην έχουμε εισιτήριο, γιατί η δικιά μας τέχνη είναι ο δρόμος, η αντίσταση και η αξιοπρέπεια. Γιατί ο αγώνας μας ενάντια στα μεταλλεία ήταν, είναι και θα είναι δίκαιος.




Δεν προσκυνάμε, δεν μετανιώνουμε, θα πολεμάμε για πάντα.




Ραντεβού στο Χοντρό δέντρο, την Πέμπτη 8 Οκτωβρίου, στις 9:00, για μια παράσταση που θα μας μείνει σε όλα αξέχαστη.




Επιτροπή αγώνα Μ. Παναγίας”







 




Κάλεσμα της 

Επιτροπής Αγώνα Θεσσαλονίκης ενάντια στην εξόρυξη χρυσού:







Ο πρόεδρος της Hellas Gold, Χ. Μπαλάσκας, ανακοίνωσε στη ΔΕΘ τα εγκαίνια στις Σκουριές για τις 8 Οκτωβρίου.

Πήγαμε στο βουνό. Είδαμε το δάσος να υποχωρεί, το νερό να απειλείται. Νιώσαμε τη σκόνη, τον θόρυβο, την αλλαγή του τοπίου.

Και τώρα, μαζί με τις χρυσές κορδέλες, έρχονται οι εκρήξεις, η αποστράγγιση, η λειτουργία ενός έργου που θα αποτελέσει ταφόπλακα για τη ΒΑ Χαλκιδική και την ευρύτερη περιοχή.

Ανησυχούμε για τον αέρα που θα αναπνεύσουμε, για το νερό που έχουμε ανάγκη, για τον τόπο μας.

Την Πέμπτη, στις 9 το πρωί, στο Χονδρό Δέντρο, μαζί με τους κατοίκους της Μεγάλης Παναγίας.

Εμείς θα είμαστε εκεί.

Γιατί το βουνό είναι η ζωή μας.

author: Jessica Corbett
title: Another Trump Administration Boat Strike Claims 4 More Lives
content:
“Where is Congress to stop the horror?” asked Amnesty International USA.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

US President Donald Trump’s boat-bombing spree continued on Sunday despite condemnation from around the world, claiming four more lives and bringing the death toll from the 13-month campaign to at least 238.

Sharing a video of the strike, U.S. Southern Command said on social media late Sunday that “under the direction of SOUTHCOM, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere executed a lethal, kinetic strike on a go-fast vessel operating along established narco-trafficking routes in the Caribbean.”

“Confirmed intelligence revealed the vessel’s active involvement in narco-trafficking,” SOUTHCOM continued, without offering any evidence, as with at least 70 previous strikes since September 2025. “The operation killed four narco-terrorists.”

Citing a federal memo that it aims to keep concealed from the public, the Trump administration claims to be at war with drug cartels and that the killings in the Caribbean Sea and Pacific Ocean are justified. Legal experts and human rights advocates argue the bombings are at least war crimes, if not outright murder.

Sunday’s strike was the administration’s first confirmed boat bombing since Ben Saul, the United Nations special rapporteur on human rights and counterterrorism, said last month that even if the targeted vessels were engaged in drug trafficking, there are no “international legal rights to unilaterally use military force” to counter cartels.

After SOUTHCOM’s announcement, Gizmodo reporter Matt Novak declared, “We murdered four more people in a boat today.”

Brian Finucane, a former State Department legal adviser who now advises the U.S. Program at the International Crisis Group, called it “more performative killing at sea.”

Nearly 240 dead in this illegal campaign of extrajudicial killings, i.e., murder at sea. Where is Congress to stop the horror? https://t.co/yYQdIVkjTE

Highlighting the rising death toll from Trump’s “illegal campaign of extrajudicial killings, ie, murder at sea” initiative, Amnesty International USA asked, “Where is Congress to stop the horror?”

The Republican-controlled Congress has declined to pass war powers resolutions intended to stop the strikes — though the odds of passage could change if Democrats reclaim one or both chambers in next month’s midterm elections.

Trump’s bombing spree has apparently been not only illegal but ineffective. The Washington Post reported in July that a Drug Enforcement Administration analysis concluded that the boat-bombing campaign has not “reduced the amount of cocaine entering” the United States.
